item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL AGRICULTURE (IITA)
INTERNAL & EXTERNAL ADVERTISEMENT
Call for Expression of Interest (EOI) - TAAT Technical Advisor-Seed Systems
The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) is a not-for-profit organization dedicated to generating agricultural innovations to address Africa's most pressing challenges, including hunger, malnutrition, poverty, and natural resource degradation. Collaborating with partners across sub-Saharan Africa, IITA aims to improve livelihoods, enhance food and nutrition security, increase employment, and preserve natural resources. IITA is a member of CGIAR, a global agricultural research partnership working towards a food-secure future. For more information, visit www.iita.org.
The Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) funded by the African Development Bank (AfDB), is a major continent-wide program designed to boost agricultural productivity across the continent by rapidly delivering proven technologies to millions of farmers. The overall goal of TAAT is to double crop, livestock, and fish productivity by expanding access to productivity-increasing technologies to more than 40 million smallholder farmers across Africa. TAAT aims to generate an additional 120 million metric tons (MT) of food while lifting 130 million people out of poverty. Getting certified seeds of the most modern varieties into the hands of tens of millions of farmers is the primary objective of TAAT.
The program supports the Feed Africa Initiative of the AfDB by providing the needed, proven agricultural and food processing technologies and implementation strategies for inclusion within the Bank's loans to Regional Member Countries (RMCs). It is implemented by the Regional Technology Delivery Infrastructure (RTDI) made up of the Commodity Technology Delivery Compacts (Compacts); the TAAT Clearinghouse (CH); the Program Management Unit (PMU), and a Program Steering Committee (PSC). The Compacts are currently composed of 11 CGIAR centers, 3 Advanced regional R&D African centers, National Agricultural Research and Extension System (NARES) institutions, private sector partners and development partners. IITA is the executing agency of TAAT.
The Program Management Unit (PMU) is responsible for overall coordination and implementation of the TAAT program providing oversight and direction of the program. This is achieved through the provision of technical assistance from technical experts supporting the project. Specifically, the PMU team consists of experts from M&E, Procurement, Financial Management, Environment and Social Safeguards, and Gender, all working together to ensure delivery of TAAT activities in close collaboration with partners to get proven technologies into the programs of the government's agricultural infrastructure.
As the Executing Agency (EA) for TAAT, IITA will continue to oversee program implementation in partnership with other CGIAR Centers and specialized agencies acting as Implementing Agencies for specific components.
OBJECTIVES OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES
The objective of this consultancy is to engage an Individual Consultant for the position of Technical Advisor - Seed Systems, seconded to Rwanda's Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI), to provide technical leadership and coordinate implementation of the project "Building a Sustainable Private Sector-Led Seed Sector in Rwanda's Food Basket Sites," in support of a more efficient, inclusive, and sustainable seed system in Rwanda.
Specifically, the consultancy aims to strengthen Rwanda's seed sector through a market-driven, private sector-led approach, by supporting youth Agripreneurs in building profitable enterprises in certified maize seed production and basic seed potato multiplication, in partnership with anchor seed companies, Farmer Service Centers, and financial institutions. Beyond the technical production support provided by anchor seed companies, the consultancy will also strengthen youth enterprises' entrepreneurial, financial management, and business development capacities to ensure long-term sustainability, while ensuring implementation aligns with national priorities through liaison with the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) and the Rwanda Inspectorate, Competition and Consumer Protection Authority (RICA) on harmonizing seed certification protocols.
Requirements
MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES
Among others, the consultant is expected to liaise with the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) and the Rwanda Inspectorate, Competition and Consumer Protection Authority (RICA) to harmonize seed certification protocols. The position will be seconded to the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI) in Rwanda to support implementation and ensure alignment with national priorities.
The Technical Advisor - Seed Systems will:

Provide technical leadership in the development of sustainable, market-driven seed systems in Rwanda, working closely with MINAGRI and national stakeholders. 
Coordinate project planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting across target Food Basket Sites. 
Strengthening partnerships with government institutions, financial institutions, private seed companies, Farmer Service Centers (FSCs), and youth Agripreneurs. 
Ensure the production and delivery of high-quality certified seed of priority crops, particularly maize, rice and potato. 
Facilitate seed demand forecasting and seed balance sheets for maize, rice and potato at the district level
Coordinate and provide technical business support to partner youth enterprises to support their business development. 
Facilitate and monitor linkages between Youth enterprises and Anchor Farmers/companies
Ensure youth enterprises ‘access to adequate extension services and knowledge needed to run the seed business. 
Support MINAGRI in other matters related to seed business and technologies transfer to FOBASIs.

Deliverables
The Advisor will be expected to produce, as applicable:

Approved annual and quarterly implementation plans for seed-system and youth Agripreneurs activities
Functional coordination mechanism involving MINAGRI, implementing partners, FSCs, anchor seed companies, financial institutions and other stakeholders
Technical seed production and quality-assurance protocols developed and operationalized
FSCs and anchor seed companies strengthened and functioning as incubation and service-delivery hubs for youth seed Agripreneurs
Youth Agripreneurs trained, mentored and supported to establish or strengthen commercially viable seed enterprises
Youth enterprise/business plans developed, and financing linkages established, including catalytic grants and contract-based lending arrangements
Functional results-based M&E system and project performance database/dashboard established and regularly updated
Four quarterly technical reports and one consolidated annual technical report produced each year
Stakeholder partnerships and market linkages strengthened across government, finance, seed companies, input suppliers and buyers
Knowledge products and documented lessons produced to support learning, replication and scaling of successful youth-led seed business models

Educational Qualifications And Experience.

Master's degree in Agronomy, Seed Science, Agribusiness, Agricultural Economics, or a related field
Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in seed systems, agribusiness, or agricultural value chain development. 
Proven experience in project coordination and implementation. 
Strong understanding of seed production, certification, and extension systems. 
Experience working with government, private sector, and farmer organizations
At least 3 years of experience in East Africa with knowledge of local seed market dynamics, residence in Rwanda is an added advantage. 
Fluency in English (working language); knowledge of Kinyarwanda is an added advantage
Demonstrated working experience with international financial institutions (e.g., AfDB, World Bank,) is an added advantage

CORE COMPETENCIES

Strong technical knowledge of seed systems, certification processes, and agronomy. 
Demonstrated experience in multi-stakeholder coordination and partnership building. 
Strong analytical, organizational, seed business and reporting skills
Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary teams
Good understanding of private sector-led agricultural development approaches. 
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills

Benefits
DURATION
The duration of the assignment will be for an initial period of one year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance and fund availability from the donors. The assignment will commence in November 2026.
Eligibility criteria, establishment of the short-list and the selection procedure shall be in accordance with the African Development Bank's Procurement policy framework, October 2015, which is available on the Bank's website at https://www.afdb.org/en/projects-and-operations/procurement/new-procurement-policy
Interested consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 08:00-16:30
Expressions of interest should be sent to the address below on or before Monday 12th October 2026.
Attn: Zozo Rachel
Interim TAAT Program Coordinator | Program Management Unit
International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, www.iita.org
Headquarters & West Africa Hub
PMB 5320, Oyo Road, Ibadan 200001, Oyo State, Nigeria
International Mailing Address: IITA, Carolyn House, 26 Dingwall Road, Croydon, CR9 3EE, UK
Email: R.Zozo@cgiar.org
Copy: m.a.bakare@cgiar.org

  • Ensure the production and delivery of high-quality certified seed of priority crops, particularly maize, rice and potato.
  • Facilitate seed demand forecasting and seed balance sheets for maize, rice and potato at the district level
  • Coordinate and provide technical business support to partner youth enterprises to support their business development.
  • Facilitate and monitor linkages between Youth enterprises and Anchor Farmers/companies
  • Ensure youth enterprises ‘access to adequate extension services and knowledge needed to run the seed business.
  • Support MINAGRI in other matters related to seed business and technologies transfer to FOBASIs.

Deliverables The Advisor will be expected to produce, as applicable:

  • Approved annual and quarterly implementation plans for seed-system and youth Agripreneurs activities
  • Functional coordination mechanism involving MINAGRI, implementing partners, FSCs, anchor seed companies, financial institutions and other stakeholders
  • Technical seed production and quality-assurance protocols developed and operationalized
  • FSCs and anchor seed companies strengthened and functioning as incubation and service-delivery hubs for youth seed Agripreneurs
  • Youth Agripreneurs trained, mentored and supported to establish or strengthen commercially viable seed enterprises
  • Youth enterprise/business plans developed, and financing linkages established, including catalytic grants and contract-based lending arrangements
  • Functional results-based M&E system and project performance database/dashboard established and regularly updated
  • Four quarterly technical reports and one consolidated annual technical report produced each year
  • Stakeholder partnerships and market linkages strengthened across government, finance, seed companies, input suppliers and buyers
  • Knowledge products and documented lessons produced to support learning, replication and scaling of successful youth-led seed business models

Educational Qualifications And Experience.

  • Master's degree in Agronomy, Seed Science, Agribusiness, Agricultural Economics, or a related field
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in seed systems, agribusiness, or agricultural value chain development.
  • Proven experience in project coordination and implementation.
  • Strong understanding of seed production, certification, and extension systems.
  • Experience working with government, private sector, and farmer organizations
  • At least 3 years of experience in East Africa with knowledge of local seed market dynamics, residence in Rwanda is an added advantage.
  • Fluency in English (working language); knowledge of Kinyarwanda is an added advantage
  • Demonstrated working experience with international financial institutions (e.g., AfDB, World Bank,) is an added advantage

CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Strong technical knowledge of seed systems, certification processes, and agronomy.
  • Demonstrated experience in multi-stakeholder coordination and partnership building.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, seed business and reporting skills
  • Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary teams
  • Good understanding of private sector-led agricultural development approaches.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills

Benefits DURATION The duration of the assignment will be for an initial period of one year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance and fund availability from the donors. The assignment will commence in November 2026. item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 AVSI Rwanda ni umuryango w’imbere mu gihugu wemewe na Guverinoma y’u Rwanda, wabaruwe mu Kigo cy’Igihugu gishinzwe Imiyoborere (RGB) nk’umuryango utegamiye kuri Leta ukorera mu Rwanda, ufite nimero y’iyandikwa 717/RGB/NGO/LP/12/2020.
Intego yawo ni gukorera buri munsi mu kubaka umuryango wubahiriza agaciro n’icyubahiro bya buri muntu kandi urangwa n’ubutabera, wubaha amahitamo n’ibyifuzo by’abana n’imiryango yabo, ndetse no guteza imbere umutekano n’ubusabane mu miryango binyuze mu bufatanye bukomeye hagati y’ababyeyi, abaturage n’amashuri, hagamijwe imibereho myiza’iterambere ryuzuye ry’abana.
AVSI Rwanda ikorera mu turere 6 tw’u Rwanda, mu byiciro bitandukanye by’ibikorwa. Ifasha kandi ikorana n’abantu barenga 240.000, binyuze mu mishinga ijyanye n’ibi bikurikira:
Uburezi
Kurengera umwana n’uburenganzira bw’urubyiruko
Uburinganire n’iterambere ry’abagore
Ubuzima bwo mu mutwe
Iterambere ry’ubukungu
Imihindagurikire y’ikirere
Ubuhinzi
AVSI Rwanda ikorana n’abaturage, imiryango, amashuri, inzego za Leta n’abandi bafatanyabikorwa kugira ngo iteze imbere imibereho myiza, uburenganzira n’iterambere rirambye ry’abana, imiryango ndetse n’abaturage muri rusange.
ITANGAZO RY’ISOKO RYO KUGURA NO GUTANGA ARROSOIRS
AVSI Rwanda iramenyesha abacuruzi cyangwa ibigo bicuruza arrosoirs ko yifuza gutanga isoko ryo kugura no gutanga arrosoirs zifite ubushobozi bwo kujyamo litiro 10 z’amazi kuri buri arrosoir.
Ibisabwa kuri arrosoirs
Arrosoir igomba kuba ijyamo litiro icumi (10L) z’amazi, kandi ifite umufuniko urimo utwenge amazi acamo mu gihe cyo kuhira imyaka/imbuto/imboga.
Umubare wa arrosoirs n’igiciro
Lot 1: Akarere ka Gicumbi (koresha iyi mbonerahamwe mu gihe uri gupiganira iri soko)
UmurengeUmubarewa arrosoirs zikenewe mu karereIgicirokuri arrosoir imweIgiteranyoIkiguzi cy’urugendo (Transport)Igiciro cyose ku gikoresho n’igiciro cy’urugendo (transport)cyo kubigezayoRuvune21Nyamiyaga39Rukomo30Lot 2: Akarere ka Ruhango (koresha iyi mbonerahamwe mu gihe uri gupiganira iri soko)
UmurengeUmubarewa arrosoir zikeneweIgicirokuri arrosoir imweIgiteranyoIkiguzi cy’urugendo (Transport)Igiciro cyose ku gikoresho n’igiciro cy’urugendo (transport) cyokubigezayoRuhango33Bweramana21Ntongwe21Kinazi15Lot 3: Akarere ka Nyanza (koresha iyi mbonerahamwe mu gihe uri gupiganira iri soko)
UmurengeUmubareIgicirokuriIgiteranyoIkiguziIgiciro cyose kuwaarrosoir imwecy’urugendogikoreshoarrosoirs(Transport)n’igicirozikenewecy’urugendo(transport)cyokubigezayoCyabakamyi15Kigoma33Mukingo21Ibyangombwa bisabwa kandi bikorerwaho isuzuma
Uwitabira isoko agomba gutanga:
Inyandiko igaragaza ko yemerewe gukora ubucuruzi iriho na TIN number
Icyangombwa cy’uko ikigo cyanditswe muri TVA / VAT cyanwa cyasonewe
Inyandiko igaragaza ko umucuruzi atanga inyemezabuguzi (EBM invoice)
Icyangombwa cy’uko nta mwenda abereyemo Rwanda Revenue Authority, kitarengeje amezi atatu
Icyangombwa kigaragaza ahandi yakoze iyo mirimo akayirangiza neza (ni akarusho)
Igiciro kuri buri arrosoir n’igiteranyo rusange, hashingiwe ku mubare wa arrosoirs zikenewe (reba imbonerahamwe uko iteye hejuru)
Igihe cyo gutanga arrosoirs kitarengeje iminsi 2 y’akazi muri buri karere.
Icyitonderwa: Igiciro gito si cyo cyonyine kizashingirwaho; hazitabwa ku bwiza no kubahiriza ibisabwa byose.
Uwitabira isoko asabwa kugaragaza niba igiciro yatanze kirimo ubwikorezi kugeza arrosoirs bizashyirwa mu murenge wa Ruvune, Rukomo, Nyamiyaga, Ruhango, Bweramana, Ntongwe, Kinazi, Cyabakamyi, Mukingo na Kigoma.
AVSI Rwanda ifite uburenganzira bwo kwanga isoko ritubahirije ibisabwa, ifite kandi uburenganzira bwo kugabanya no kongera ingano (umubare wa arrosoirs zikenewe), hashingiwe ku kigereranyo cy’ingengo y’imari yateganyijwe n’ibiciro biri ku isoko.
NB: AVSI Rwanda ntabwo itanga avance ku kigo cyatsindiye isoko.
4. Gutanga amasoko
Ibitabo by’amasoko bigomba gutangwa ku biro bikuru bya AVSI Rwanda,
| Kigali | Gasabo - Kimironko | Bibare | Inyamibwa village |KG 145 St. House No 10, bitarenze ku wa 29/09/2026 saa kumi n’imwe (5:00 pm)
Gufungura isoko: Ku wa 30/09/2026 kuva saa kumi ku biro bya AVSI Rwanda.
Bikorewe i Kigali, ku wa 21/09/2026
Lorette Birara
Umuyobozi wa AVSI Rwanda

Bifite umuyoboro usohoramo amazi arenze urugero (Overflow).

Byujuje ubuziranenge bukenewe mu kubikamo amazi (Ibara ry’umukara cyangwa icyatsi bituma nta rumuri rwinjira mu kigega)

item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 Project/Activity Name
Heifer International Rwanda
Agresso Work order:
RW1350
Country:
Rwanda 
Advertisement for Procurement
Request for Quotation (RFQ)
Supply of Cows for the Rwanda Dairy Development Project (RDDP II)
Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a nonprofit International non-governmental organization whose mission to end hunger and poverty, while caring for the earth through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become the flagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. 
Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. 
Heifer International Rwanda is in partnering with the Government of Rwanda through the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources for the implementation of the Rwanda Dairy Development Project (RDDP II). Under this partnership, Heifer International Rwanda invites qualified and eligible suppliers to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of cowsheds construction materials to the project locations as listed in the RFQ.
Purpose and Objective
The main objective is to invite qualified bidders to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of pregnant dairy heifers to beneficiaries in fifteen (15) districts. The procurement is divided into four (4) lots corresponding to Rwanda's four provinces. A bidder may submit a quotation for one or more lots but may be awarded a maximum of one (1) lot.
 Each lot will be evaluated independently.
How to Apply
Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below.
All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Cows for RDDP II” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 22nd October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. 
Done on September 24th, 2026.
Heifer International Rwanda Management

item.title: Call For Expression Of Interest (eoi) - Consulting Firm For Youth Agribusiness
item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL AGRICULTURE (IITA)
INTERNAL & EXTERNAL ADVERTISEMENT
Call for Expression of Interest (EOI) - Selection of a Consulting Firm for Youth Agribusiness Training, Mentorship and Business Development Support
The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), a member of CGIAR, is a not-for-profit research organization dedicated to developing and promoting agricultural innovations that address Africa's most pressing challenges, including hunger, malnutrition, poverty, and natural resource degradation. Through its collaboration with governments, development partners, research institutions, and the private sector, IITA works to improve livelihoods, strengthen food and nutrition security, create employment opportunities, and promote sustainable agricultural development across sub-Saharan Africa. Under the African Development Bank (AfDB)-funded Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) Program, IITA is implementing interventions to accelerate the adoption of proven agricultural technologies, with a strong focus on strengthening seed systems to increase the availability and accessibility of certified seeds of improved, climate-resilient crop varieties.
As part of the TAAT Program, IITA is implementing the project "Building a Sustainable Private Sector-Led Seed Sector in Rwanda's Food Basket Sites," which seeks to strengthen Rwanda's seed sector through a market-driven and private sector-led approach. The project supports youth agripreneurs establish profitable enterprises engaged in certified maize seed production and basic seed potato multiplication by fostering partnerships with anchor seed companies, Farmer Service Centers (FSCs), financial institutions, and other stakeholders. While technical support for seed production will be provided by anchor seed companies, there is also a need to strengthen the entrepreneurial, financial management, and business development capacities of youth enterprises to ensure their long-term sustainability. To achieve this, IITA intends to engage a qualified service provider to deliver structured agribusiness training, entrepreneurship learning, mentorship, and business development support, enabling youth groups to develop bankable business plans, access financing, manage loans responsibly, and operate sustainable agribusiness enterprises.
Within the TAAT ecosystem, IITA Rwanda, in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI)- Rwanda, intends to engage a consulting firm to deliver structured agribusiness training, entrepreneurship learning, mentorship, and business development support, enabling youth groups to develop bankable business plans, access financing, manage loans responsibly, and operate sustainable agribusiness enterprises.
SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT
The consulting firm will deliver agribusiness training and capacity-building services to youth groups through a combination of in-person workshops, learning, mentorship, and business development support. Key areas of focus will include entrepreneurship, agribusiness management, financial literacy, marketing, value chain development, governance, leadership, and risk management. The provider will also develop and deliver training modules, webinars, mentoring sessions, and digital learning resources to ensure continuous learning throughout the project period.
In addition, the consulting firm will support youth groups in developing bankable agribusiness business plans by conducting market and financial analyses, designing investment and financing strategies, and strengthening enterprise viability. Continuous mentorship and coaching will be provided through advisory services, performance monitoring, and support in addressing operational and management challenges. The provider will further assist youth groups in establishing sound financial management systems, improving record-keeping practices, promoting responsible loan utilization and repayment, and facilitating engagement with financial institutions when required.
Requirements
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITES
The consulting firm will be responsible for:

Organizing and delivering agribusiness and entrepreneurship training programs for youth groups
Developing and implementing learning and entrepreneurship training initiatives
Building the capacity of youth groups in financial literacy, marketing, and enterprise manage-ment
Supporting the development and refinement of bankable agribusiness business plans
Providing continuous mentorship, coaching, and advisory services to youth enterprises
Monitoring the performance of youth businesses and recommending improvement measures
Supporting the establishment of sound financial management and record-keeping practices
Promoting responsible loan utilization and repayment among youth enterprises
Preparing and submitting periodic reports on training, mentorship, and enterprise development activities
Participating in coordination meetings with the project coordination team and relevant partners
Collaborating with project stakeholders to ensure effective implementation and achievement of project objectives

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
The selected consulting firm will be expected to deliver the following:

A comprehensive agribusiness training curriculum
Organization and facilitation of agribusiness workshops
Entrepreneurship training modules accessible to youth participants
Bankable business plans developed by youth groups
Continuous mentorship and advisory support
Financial literacy and loan management training
Periodic progress and performance reports (on quarterly basis)
Documentation of lessons learned and best practices

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
The initiative focuses on designing the financial product and training 135 youths. The performance of the service provider will be assessed using the following indicators:

Number of youths trained in agribusiness and entrepreneurship
Number of agribusiness workshops conducted
Number of youth enterprises supported to develop business plans
Percentage of youth enterprises with viable business plans
Number of mentorship sessions delivered
Improvement in financial management practices among youth enterprises
Loan repayment performance of supported youth groups
Satisfaction of youth participants with training and mentorship services

PROJECT MANAGEMENT & COORDINATION
The consulting firm will operate under the technical supervision of the Seed System Specialist.
The consulting firm will also work closely with:

Anchor Seed Companies supporting youth seed production
Farmer Service Centers (FSCs) providing extension services
Financial institutions supporting youth enterprise financing
Government agencies responsible for agricultural development
Project implementation partners

Benefits
DURATION
The selected consulting firm will be contracted for a period aligned with the project implementation timeline, approximately one year and a half, renewable, subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements.
Eligibility criteria, establishment of the short-list and the selection procedure (Quality and Cost Based Selection) shall be in accordance with the African Development Bank's Procurement policy framework, October 2015, which is available on the Bank's website at https://www.afdb.org/en/projects-and-operations/procurement/new-procurement-policy
Interested consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 08:00-16:30

INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL AGRICULTURE (IITA)
INTERNAL & EXTERNAL ADVERTISEMENT
Call for Expression of Interest (EOI) - Selection of a Consulting Firm for Youth Agribusiness Training, Mentorship and Business Development Support
The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), a member of CGIAR, is a not-for-profit research organization dedicated to developing and promoting agricultural innovations that address Africa's most pressing challenges, including hunger, malnutrition, poverty, and natural resource degradation. Through its collaboration with governments, development partners, research institutions, and the private sector, IITA works to improve livelihoods, strengthen food and nutrition security, create employment opportunities, and promote sustainable agricultural development across sub-Saharan Africa. Under the African Development Bank (AfDB)-funded Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) Program, IITA is implementing interventions to accelerate the adoption of proven agricultural technologies, with a strong focus on strengthening seed systems to increase the availability and accessibility of certified seeds of improved, climate-resilient crop varieties.
As part of the TAAT Program, IITA is implementing the project "Building a Sustainable Private Sector-Led Seed Sector in Rwanda's Food Basket Sites," which seeks to strengthen Rwanda's seed sector through a market-driven and private sector-led approach. The project supports youth agripreneurs establish profitable enterprises engaged in certified maize seed production and basic seed potato multiplication by fostering partnerships with anchor seed companies, Farmer Service Centers (FSCs), financial institutions, and other stakeholders. While technical support for seed production will be provided by anchor seed companies, there is also a need to strengthen the entrepreneurial, financial management, and business development capacities of youth enterprises to ensure their long-term sustainability. To achieve this, IITA intends to engage a qualified service provider to deliver structured agribusiness training, entrepreneurship learning, mentorship, and business development support, enabling youth groups to develop bankable business plans, access financing, manage loans responsibly, and operate sustainable agribusiness enterprises.
Within the TAAT ecosystem, IITA Rwanda, in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI)- Rwanda, intends to engage a consulting firm to deliver structured agribusiness training, entrepreneurship learning, mentorship, and business development support, enabling youth groups to develop bankable business plans, access financing, manage loans responsibly, and operate sustainable agribusiness enterprises.
SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT
The consulting firm will deliver agribusiness training and capacity-building services to youth groups through a combination of in-person workshops, learning, mentorship, and business development support. Key areas of focus will include entrepreneurship, agribusiness management, financial literacy, marketing, value chain development, governance, leadership, and risk management. The provider will also develop and deliver training modules, webinars, mentoring sessions, and digital learning resources to ensure continuous learning throughout the project period.
In addition, the consulting firm will support youth groups in developing bankable agribusiness business plans by conducting market and financial analyses, designing investment and financing strategies, and strengthening enterprise viability. Continuous mentorship and coaching will be provided through advisory services, performance monitoring, and support in addressing operational and management challenges. The provider will further assist youth groups in establishing sound financial management systems, improving record-keeping practices, promoting responsible loan utilization and repayment, and facilitating engagement with financial institutions when required.
Requirements
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITES
The consulting firm will be responsible for:

Organizing and delivering agribusiness and entrepreneurship training programs for youth groups
Developing and implementing learning and entrepreneurship training initiatives
Building the capacity of youth groups in financial literacy, marketing, and enterprise manage-ment
Supporting the development and refinement of bankable agribusiness business plans
Providing continuous mentorship, coaching, and advisory services to youth enterprises
Monitoring the performance of youth businesses and recommending improvement measures
Supporting the establishment of sound financial management and record-keeping practices
Promoting responsible loan utilization and repayment among youth enterprises
Preparing and submitting periodic reports on training, mentorship, and enterprise development activities
Participating in coordination meetings with the project coordination team and relevant partners
Collaborating with project stakeholders to ensure effective implementation and achievement of project objectives

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
The selected consulting firm will be expected to deliver the following:

A comprehensive agribusiness training curriculum
Organization and facilitation of agribusiness workshops
Entrepreneurship training modules accessible to youth participants
Bankable business plans developed by youth groups
Continuous mentorship and advisory support
Financial literacy and loan management training
Periodic progress and performance reports (on quarterly basis)
Documentation of lessons learned and best practices

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
The initiative focuses on designing the financial product and training 135 youths. The performance of the service provider will be assessed using the following indicators:

Number of youths trained in agribusiness and entrepreneurship
Number of agribusiness workshops conducted
Number of youth enterprises supported to develop business plans
Percentage of youth enterprises with viable business plans
Number of mentorship sessions delivered
Improvement in financial management practices among youth enterprises
Loan repayment performance of supported youth groups
Satisfaction of youth participants with training and mentorship services

PROJECT MANAGEMENT & COORDINATION
The consulting firm will operate under the technical supervision of the Seed System Specialist.
The consulting firm will also work closely with:

Anchor Seed Companies supporting youth seed production
Farmer Service Centers (FSCs) providing extension services
Financial institutions supporting youth enterprise financing
Government agencies responsible for agricultural development
Project implementation partners

Benefits
DURATION
The selected consulting firm will be contracted for a period aligned with the project implementation timeline, approximately one year and a half, renewable, subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements.
Eligibility criteria, establishment of the short-list and the selection procedure (Quality and Cost Based Selection) shall be in accordance with the African Development Bank's Procurement policy framework, October 2015, which is available on the Bank's website at https://www.afdb.org/en/projects-and-operations/procurement/new-procurement-policy
Interested consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 08:00-16:30
Expressions of interest should be delivered to the emails below on or before Monday 12th October 2026 at 16:30 pm. Any proposal received after the closing date shall be rejected.
Attn: Zozo Rachel

item.title: Terms of Reference (ToR) for Tender No. RS-T002/2026 for Supply, Installation, Testing and Commissioning of Fire Suppression Systems for Critical Environments
item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

  TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR) FOR TENDER NO. RS-T002/2026 
Supply, Installation, Testing and Commissioning of Fire Suppression Systems for Critical Environments 
Headquarters and Disaster Recovery Sites 
18th September 2026 
Procuring Entity RSwitch LimitedAddress KG 563 St, Plot 1200, Kacyiru, Kigali, RwandaTender Email rswitch.tender@rswitch.co.rwSubmission Deadline 16th October 2026 at 5:00 PM Kigali TimeI. Background and Procurement Purpose 
RSwitch Limited invites qualified and experienced contractors to submit proposals for the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of a complete fire detection and clean-agent suppression solution across its Headquarters (HQ) and Disaster Recovery (DR) sites. The procurement is intended to protect mission-critical environments, including data centres, power rooms and battery rooms, while safeguarding personnel, sensitive IT/electrical equipment and business continuity. 
This TOR is designed to obtain the solution that offers the best overall value to RSwitch through open, fair, transparent and competitive procurement. Requirements shall be applied objectively and shall not be interpreted or administered so as to favour or disadvantage any bidder, manufacturer, brand, technology, distributor or country of origin except where a restriction is objectively necessary for safety, compatibility, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance or continuity of existing infrastructure. 
II. Procurement Integrity, Competition and Vendor Neutrality 
Specifications are functional, performance-based and vendor-neutral. A reference to a technology, certification, standard, manufacturer or product shall be read as including “or equivalent” unless this TOR expressly states and objectively justifies otherwise. 
A bidder offering an equivalent solution must demonstrate equivalence through verifiable technical documentation, independent certification, test reports or other objective evidence. 
No RSwitch employee, evaluator, adviser or committee member may privately disclose non-public tender information, privately clarify requirements with one bidder, or modify evaluation criteria after publication. 
All persons participating in specification development or evaluation shall disclose actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest and recuse themselves where required.
Any material clarification, correction or change to the TOR shall be issued by formal addendum and made available simultaneously to all bidders. 
RSwitch may verify any certificate, reference, manufacturer authorization, project history, insurance document or other evidence submitted. 
III. Objectives and Scope 
The following section presents the objective and scope of the Tender:
Supply, installation, testing and commissioning of a complete clean-agent fire suppression system, with no proprietary brand mandated. 
Coverage of HQ Data Center, HQ Power Room, HQ Battery Room and DR Data Center. 
Integrated early-warning detection, alarms, manual call points, control panels, evacuation signaling and interfaces required for safe suppression release. 
Mandatory warranty, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance and Service Level Agreement (SLA). 
Provision of dedicated portable clean-agent fire extinguishers suitable for occupied spaces and sensitive equipment: 4 units for the Data Center, 3 for the Power Room and 2 for the Battery Room. 
Training, as-built documentation, operation manuals, maintenance schedules, spare parts/consumables support and final acceptance testing. 
Minimum commercial requirements 
Minimum warranty period: two (2) years. 
Preventive maintenance: at least every four (4) months during the covered maintenance period. 3. No advance payment. 
Delivery, installation, testing and commissioning: within fifty (50) calendar days from contract award, subject to the final agreed implementation plan. 
Detailed Technical and Performance Requirements 
4.1. Mandatory site walkthrough 
All participating bidders shall attend the scheduled site walkthroughs to assess pipe routing, ceiling pathways, equipment placement, room dimensions, existing interfaces, spatial constraints and logistical conditions. RSwitch shall provide the same material site information to all attendees. Questions of general relevance raised during or after the walkthrough shall be answered through the formal clarification process.
4.2. Detection and alarm system 
An aspirating/high-sensitivity smoke detection system (HSSD) - VESDA smoke detectors as the first line of detection. 
Heat detectors, audible/visual alarms, manual call points and compatible control panels. 
The proposed design shall identify detection zoning, alarm logic, release logic, interfaces and fail-safe behaviour. 
4.3. Exit, evacuation and access-control interfaces 
Exit/evacuation signals at each door of protected rooms, clearly directing personnel toward safe exits. 
Automatic activation of relevant evacuation signals upon suppression-release sequence, subject to testing. 
Door/access-control behaviour during a release shall support safe evacuation and comply with the approved fire/life-safety design. item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 PUBLIC TENDER NOTICE # PIH/IMB/10868/M09/FY27
TENDER TITTLE: MAINTENANCE AND REHABILITATION OF PARTNERS IN HEALTH STAFF HOUSES IN RWINKWAVU SECTOR, KAYONZA DISTRICT.
SOURCING METHOD: OPEN COMPETITION FOR DOMESTIC COMPANIES.
Partners In Health (PIH) is a nonprofit organization with its headquarters in Boston, Massachusetts, whose mission is to provide quality health care for poor and most in need populations around the world. Since 2005, the Ministry of Health in Rwanda has worked with PIH Rwanda, also known as Inshuti Mu Buzima, to improve the quality of care in the country and increase health care access for Rwanda most in need populations. PIH/IMB have since helped to bring high-quality health care to three Districts namely: Kayonza, Burera and Kirehe. 
Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima is seeking proposals from qualified and authorized Construction companies for maintenance and rehabilitation of Partners In Health staff houses in Rwinkwavu Sector, Kayonza District as per term of reference (ToRs) and BoQ found in annex. Interested and qualified bidders should provide their proposals bearing the following requirements:
I. BIDDERS/ VENDORS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA 
The bidders falling in any of the following categories will be ineligible to participate in this tender and / or its award:
The Bidder should not be suspended or blacklisted by PIH-IMB or OnePIH nor blacklisted or revoked licenses by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or other relevant regulatory bodies. 
The Bidder should not have any ongoing contracts with PIH-IMB that demonstrates poor performance. 
Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge.
Any bidder that owns operates, or exercises controlling shareholding in more than one company is strictly prohibited from submitting more than one bid under this tender. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules.
NB: Non-compliance with any of above provision shall result in the annulment of bid examination process/ tender competition.
II. COMPULSORY REQUIREMENTS: 
a. Site visit certificate is obligatory required.  A Site Visit Certificate is a mandatory requirement for this tender. The site visit for the referenced project is scheduled on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 10:00 AM and will take place at the Partners In Health (PIH/IMB) Office, Rwinkwavu Sector, Kayonza District. Attendance at the site visit is mandatory for all bidders. A Site Visit Attendance Certificate will be issued by a representative of Partners In Health (PIH/IMB) to all participating companies. Bidders must submit this certificate as part of their bid documentation.
b. Bid Security Requirements: The Bidders must submit a bid security based on the value of their financial proposal, as follows:
For financial proposals ≥ RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.1%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 950,000,001 to RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.5%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 500,000,001 to RWF 950,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.0%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 100,000,001 to RWF 500,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.5%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 20,000,001 to RWF 100,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 2.0%.
No bid security is required for financial proposals with a value of ≤ RWF 20,000,000.
III. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENT:
The Bidder shall submit Company profile include: company name; location details, showing a well-known physical address building; Street number Emails, contacts. 
The Bidder shall submit registration of domestic company issued by RDB in the same domain required.
The Bidder shall submit valid RRA tax clearance.
The Bidder shall submit VAT registration certificate. 
IV. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Interested construction companies should consider ToRs (Terms of references) and BoQ available in Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System following this link: (https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/index.php) 
V. FINANCIALLY, THE BID SHALL INDICATE:
 a. A commitment letter for the submission of the Performance Security (Bank Guarantee). The letter shall state that, if awarded, the bidder will provide a Performance Security (Bank Guarantee) prior to signing the contract. The Performance Security shall depend on the contract value, as follows:

item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 NOTICE OF INVITATION TO TENDER N° A-RWA030-2026-8525
Title: Acquisition of Industrial Food Processing Equipment (Butchery, Sausage-Making and Bakery Systems (Goods)
This notice of invitation is launched by and according to the procedures of LuxDev, the Luxembourg Development Cooperation Agency, on behalf of project RWA/030 receiving financial support from the governments of Rwanda and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
1. Identification and financing of the Project/Programme
Title: Project RWA/030 - Improving skills for holistic employment in modern agriculture (ISHEMA)
Source of financing: The government of Rwanda and the government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg as set out in the project’s/programme’s bilateral agreement n° dated 18/10/2024.
Status of financing: Approved
2. Identification of the Contract
Type of contract: Goods
Object: Acquisition of Industrial Food Processing Equipment (Butchery, Sausage-Making and Bakery Systems.
Number: A-RWA030-2026-8525
Number of lots: 2
Lot 1: Butchery and Sausage-Making plants
Lot 2: Bakery plants (500 kg flour/day) 
Grouping of lots: possible, a tenderer may be awarded more than a single lot if he satisfies, cumulatively, the administrative and technical requirements of the lots to which he is tendering. 
3. Eligibility and evaluation criteria
Origin: No restriction
Eligibility: Economic operators satisfying the criteria included in the statement of good standing and in the ethics clauses of the general regulations.
Evaluation: The most economically advantageous tender on the basis of price, administrative and technical criteria and incoterm CPT (Mombasa port, Kenya) will be granted the contract.
Variants: Variants will be considered 
4. Location and timeframe
Location of the project: Rwanda
Terms and place of delivery: as per the technical specifications, Incoterm will be either FCA (Departure port), CPT (Mombasa port, kenya) or DAP (Designated TSS sites in Rwanda). The tenderers shall propose a price for each option. 
For comparison and evaluation of the offers, bids will be assessed based on Incoterm CPT (Mombasa port, Kenya) prices, ONLY.The final destination and installation of the equipment shall be at the following TSS in Rwanda: 
Lot 1: one unit shall be delivered and installed at Kinazi TSS, Ruhango District, and one unit shall be delivered and installed at Mutobo TSS, Musanze District and one unit shall be delivered and installed at Gitwe TSS, Ngoma District.
Lot 2: one unit shall be delivered and installed at Mutobo TSS, Musanze District and one unit shall be delivered and installed at Gitwe TSS, Ngoma District. 
Performance period of the contract (per lot and not cumulative in case of award of several lots to the same tenderer): 
for incoterm FCA: two (2) months with a suspension for transport from departure port to destination sites and installation instructions from the contracting authority;
for incoterm CPT: four (4) months with a suspension for transport from Mombasa to destination sites and installation instructions from the contracting authority;
for incoterm DAP: six (6) months with a suspension for installation instructions from the contracting authority; 
commencing from the date indicated in the administrative order to commence services and ending with provisional acceptance.acceptance. 
Final acceptance and warranty obligations shall be governed by Articles 40 and 42 and shall survive the performance period.;
Validity period of tenders:120 days from the time limit for receipt of tenders 
5. Definitions 
Awarding authority: Lux-Development
Contracting authority: Project RWA/030 c/o Lux-Development
Beneficiary: Rwanda TVET Board (Mutobo TSS, Gitwe TSS and Kinazi TSS)
Supervisor: to be appointed at a later stage
Donor: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
Donor’s representative: Lux-Development 
6. Tender Dossier (TD)
How to obtain the TD: The TD may be obtained free of charge at: procurement.rwanda@luxdev.lu
Consultation of the dossier: N/A
Written notifications and communications must be sent to the following address: procurement.rwanda@luxdev.lu
Deadline for requests for additional information: fourteen (14) days before the deadline for submission of tenders
Deadline for providing explanations to tenderers: eight (8) days before the deadline for submission of tenders
7. Language, currency, receipt and opening of tenders
Language: English
Currency: EUR
Tenders may be submitted electronically (in a zipped folder with dossier A-RWA030-2026-8525 and the tenderer’s identity in the subject line) to the following deposit area: https://luxdev1-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/coltilda_mujawingoma_luxdev_lu/IgC2AHiuETv7RpJa2Rxg7y9zAU7aRMxP98rzyCgQaU28Vbc
Once you have submitted your technical and financial offer, you must send an email to the address below to inform us of your submission: procurement.rwanda@luxdev.lu
Any infringement of these measures (e.g. submission of offers outside the specified e-mail addresses or deposit areas) will constitute an element of non-compliance and will result in the rejection of the offer by the evaluation committee.
You will receive an acknowledgement of receipt of your offer following the deposit of the offer.
Deadline for receipt of tenders: 23.10.2026 at 02:30pm (Kigali time)
Date and time of the public opening session: One hour after the deadline for submission
8. Guarantees
Tender guarantee: Not required
Performance guarantee: 10% of the value of the contract
Other guarantees: see TD
7. Payments
All eligible payments which are part of this contract will be processed by Lux-Development on behalf of project RWA/030.
8. Information meeting and/or site visit
There will be a non-mandatory online information session 14 days after the publication of this tender on 07.10.2026.
9. Complementary or additional services
This contract does not include any complementary or additional acquisition of goods. In the event where complementary or additional acquisition of goods would be required (initially not included), its value will be limited to a maximum of 50% of the initial value of the contract. When several successive amendments are made, this limit applies to the value of each amendment.
10. Additional information
See TD

item.title: Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Supply and Delivery of Animal Feeds for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project
item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 Project/Activity Name
Heifer International Rwanda
Agresso Work order:
RW1338
Country:
Rwanda 
Advertisement for Procurement
Request for Quotation (RFQ)
Supply and Delivery of Animal Feeds for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project.
Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become theflagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. 
Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. 
Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges.
Purpose and Objective
The objective is to obtain the required quantities of animal feeds, of the specified quality, and deliver them to designated locations in 88 sectors across 15 districts. The procurement is divided into three (3) lots, and a bidder may submit a quotation for one or more lots but may be awarded a maximum of two (2) lots. Each lot will be evaluated independently.
How to Apply
Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below.
All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Animal Feeds for PRISM Project” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 13th October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time.

item.title: Tender Notice for Maintenance and Rehabilitation of Partners in Health Staff Houses in Rwinkwavu Sector, Kayonza District
item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 PUBLIC TENDER NOTICE # PIH/IMB/10868/M09/FY27
TENDER TITTLE: MAINTENANCE AND REHABILITATION OF PARTNERS IN HEALTH STAFF HOUSES IN RWINKWAVU SECTOR, KAYONZA DISTRICT.
SOURCING METHOD: OPEN COMPETITION FOR DOMESTIC COMPANIES.
Partners In Health (PIH) is a nonprofit organization with its headquarters in Boston, Massachusetts, whose mission is to provide quality health care for poor and most in need populations around the world. Since 2005, the Ministry of Health in Rwanda has worked with PIH Rwanda, also known as Inshuti Mu Buzima, to improve the quality of care in the country and increase health care access for Rwanda most in need populations. PIH/IMB have since helped to bring high-quality health care to three Districts namely: Kayonza, Burera and Kirehe. 
Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima is seeking proposals from qualified and authorized Construction companies for maintenance and rehabilitation of Partners In Health staff houses in Rwinkwavu Sector, Kayonza District as per term of reference (ToRs) and BoQ found in annex. Interested and qualified bidders should provide their proposals bearing the following requirements:
I. BIDDERS/ VENDORS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA 
The bidders falling in any of the following categories will be ineligible to participate in this tender and / or its award:
The Bidder should not be suspended or blacklisted by PIH-IMB or OnePIH nor blacklisted or revoked licenses by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or other relevant regulatory bodies. 
The Bidder should not have any ongoing contracts with PIH-IMB that demonstrates poor performance. 
Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge.
Any bidder that owns operates, or exercises controlling shareholding in more than one company is strictly prohibited from submitting more than one bid under this tender. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules.
NB: Non-compliance with any of above provision shall result in the annulment of bid examination process/ tender competition.
II. COMPULSORY REQUIREMENTS: 
a. Site visit certificate is obligatory required.  A Site Visit Certificate is a mandatory requirement for this tender. The site visit for the referenced project is scheduled on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 10:00 AM and will take place at the Partners In Health (PIH/IMB) Office, Rwinkwavu Sector, Kayonza District. Attendance at the site visit is mandatory for all bidders. A Site Visit Attendance Certificate will be issued by a representative of Partners In Health (PIH/IMB) to all participating companies. Bidders must submit this certificate as part of their bid documentation.
b. Bid Security Requirements: The Bidders must submit a bid security based on the value of their financial proposal, as follows:
For financial proposals ≥ RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.1%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 950,000,001 to RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.5%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 500,000,001 to RWF 950,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.0%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 100,000,001 to RWF 500,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.5%.
For financial proposals ranging from RWF 20,000,001 to RWF 100,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 2.0%.
No bid security is required for financial proposals with a value of ≤ RWF 20,000,000.
III. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENT:
The Bidder shall submit Company profile include: company name; location details, showing a well-known physical address building; Street number Emails, contacts. 
The Bidder shall submit registration of domestic company issued by RDB in the same domain required.
The Bidder shall submit valid RRA tax clearance.
The Bidder shall submit VAT registration certificate. 
IV. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Interested construction companies should consider ToRs (Terms of references) and BoQ available in Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System following this link: (https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/index.php) 
V. FINANCIALLY, THE BID SHALL INDICATE:
 a. A commitment letter for the submission of the Performance Security (Bank Guarantee). The letter shall state that, if awarded, the bidder will provide a Performance Security (Bank Guarantee) prior to signing the contract. The Performance Security shall depend on the contract value, as follows:
5% of the contract whose value exceeds FRW 500,000,000;
6% of the contract value between FRW 100,000,000 FRW to FRW 500,000,000;
7% of the contract value between FRW 50,000,000 to FRW 100,000,000;
10% of the contract price whose value is between FRW 20,000,001 to FRW 50,000,000.
The performance security is not required for contracts valued at or below FRW 20,000,000.
b. The financial proposal shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs currency.
c. The financial proposal shall include all applicable taxes and charges. 
d. The financial proposal shall include terms and conditions of payment (preferably after execution of project).
e. The proposal should indicate the shortest execution period.
f. The financial proposal validity shall not be lower than 120 calendar days from the day of its submission to PIH. 
VI. SUBMISSION OF BIDS TO PIH:
All proposals from interested bidders must be electronically submitted to Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System ( https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/suppliersubmission.php ) before October 22, 2026 to 11: 59 pm (closing time) Kigali time prompt – Failing to follow this instruction proposals will not be considered.
The results of public opening will be available in the system starting from October 23, 2026 00: 00 am.
Special Notes: 
(1) There is no fee paid to obtain the Tender document. 
(2) Partners In Health is not obliged to purchase or to pay for any costs incurred by the bidder in preparation of his/her proposal in response to this tender notice.
 (3) PIH/IMB employees are restricted from participating in any PIH tender.
(4) For more information about this tender interested bidders shall contact Partners In Health team using following email address:imbprocurement@pih.org/procurement.pih@gmail.com
(5)PIH e-procurement bidding processes tutorial is available on: 
https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/biddingvideo.html
Done at Kigali on September 18, 2026
Senior Director of Procurement & Logistics
Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima

item.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL AGRICULTURE (IITA)
TECHNOLOGIES FOR AFRICAN AGRICULTURAL TRANSFORMATION (TAAT) PHASE II
TAAT FISH COMPACT
WORLDFISH
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SERVICES
SECTOR: Agriculture
CONSULTANCY SERVICES: Research Consultant for assessment of Limnothrissa miodon (Isambaza) in Lake Kivu for Sustainable Production and Fisheries Management
Financing Agreement reference: 2100155041681
Project ID. P-Z1-AA0-139
_______________________________________________________________________
This Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) follows the General Procurement Notice for this Project that appeared on the African Development Bank Group's Internet Website (www.afdb.org) 12th August 2022.
The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) has received financing from the African Development Bank toward the cost of the Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) Phase II and intends to apply part of the agreed amount for this grant to payments under the contract for a Research Consultant for assessment of Limnothrissa miodon (Isambaza) in Lake Kivu for Sustainable Production and Fisheries Management, who will be field-based with regular travel to Lake Kivu, Rwanda, combined with partial remote work.
The successful Consultant will assist the Fish Compact Coordinator; conduct a systematic and comprehensive review of scientific and grey literature related to L. miodon, small pelagic fisheries, and lake fisheries management, with a focus on Lake Kivu. This includes, but is not limited to: ecology, biology, and population dynamics; Fisheries exploitation patterns and stock assessment approaches; Governance systems, co-management frameworks, and sustainability pathways; Socio-economic dimensions and value chain dynamics; The consultant will also support the design and implementation of primary data collection, including structured surveys, in-depth interviews, Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs); conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and contribute to robust interpretation of findings within ecological, fisheries, and socio-economic contexts; assist in the coordination of field activities, including logistical planning, stakeholder engagement, and data collection campaigns; facilitate and contribute to stakeholder consultations, capacity-building initiatives, and community engagement processes; prepare a comprehensive, publication-quality review and analytical report aligned with international scientific and technical standards.
The selected consultant should possess a PhD in Fisheries Science, Zoology, Aquatic Biology, or related disciplines; demonstrated expertise in: scientific literature review and evidence synthesis, field-based data collection (ecological and socio-economic), quantitative and qualitative data analysis and scientific writing, including preparation of technical reports and peer-reviewed publications; prior experience in fisheries research, particularly in small pelagic systems or inland water bodies, is highly desirable.
The selected consultant will report to the TAAT Fish Compact Coordinator, and the assignment is for a period of five (5) months with a possibility of renewal subject to availability of funding. The assignment will commence August 1, 2026.
The IITA now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services. A detailed CV and letter of motivation detailing past related experience in similar assignments should be submitted.
Eligibility criteria, establishment of the short-list and the selection procedure shall be in accordance with the African Development Bank's Procurement Framework, October 2015, which is available on the Bank's website at https://www.afdb.org/en/projects-and-operations/procurement/new-procurement-policy
Interested consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours (0800-1630hrs).
Expressions of interest should be delivered to the address below on or before 3rd July 2026.
Attn: Zozo Rachel
Interim TAAT Program Coordinator | Program Management Unit
International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, www.iita.org
Headquarters & West Africa Hub
PMB 5320, Oyo Road, Ibadan 200001, Oyo State, Nigeria
International Mailing Address: IITA, Carolyn House, 26 Dingwall Road, Croydon, CR9 3EE, UK
Email: R.Zozo@cgiar.org
Copy: m.a.bakare@cgiar.org

item.title_raw: Scrum Master  at BPR Bank Rwanda : (Deadline 28 Sep 2026)
item.description:
Scrum Master (1)

Job Purpose

The Scrum Master manages the Agile practice execution, ensuring it is understood and enacted. The primary goal of the Scrum Master is to assist the team in meeting delivery goals and operate as a leader who helps team to self-organize, self-manage and deliver via effective Agile practice. The scrum master shall be the facilitator for the agile team working under the scrum methodology. Shall be responsible for delegating tasks appropriately and ensuring the team is working on the right tasks at the right time. Working together with Technology relation team and product owners to ensure a healthy product portfolio and to translate epics, stories, and other items on the sprint list into actionable tasks for development organization.

Main Responsibilities

Ownership and accountability of establishing agile values, methods, principles and practices and their application for the delivery of projects and business initiatives and acts as an evangelist for adoption agile methodology within the enterprise.

Ensures that the Scrum Team is provided with an environment conducive for project delivery while facilitating discussions, decision making, and conflict resolution and helps to remove any impediments to the project delivery.

The Scrum Master guides, facilitates, coaches, mentor and teaches agile standards and Scrum practices (e.g. Lean, Kanban, Scrum, XP, DevOps, SAFe, LeSS etc) to the scrum, project teams and the whole development organization;

Organizes and facilitates and leading scrum ceremonies (sprint planning meeting, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, sprint retrospects etc), events, meetings, and decision-making processes.

Collaborates closely with Product Owners and Technology Relationship Management teams to prepare and clarify the Prioritized Product Backlog and the Definition of the Done Criteria and facilitates Prioritized Product Backlog Reviews with the product owner.

Facilitates identification of the stakeholders and manages the stakeholders and vendors as required for business projects or initiatives

Responsible for creating release plans including deliverables and the release deadline, plans and estimates the highest value deliverables for the next release

Demonstrate and Validate Sprints by facilitating presentation of completed Deliverables by the Scrum Team for the Product Owner’s approval

Supports the Scrum Team in determining the length of sprint, creating the deliverables, identification of tasks and effort estimation for the tasks agreed for a sprint.

Monitoring progress and performance of the scrum teams and keeping the organization up to date on the progress of the scrum team’s projects & initiatives by preparing and presenting status reports to stakeholders.

Daily Responsibilities:

Helping the Scrum teams agree on what they can achieve during each development sprint (or other period of time).

Helping the team continuously make progress on the projects by making sure each person is working on the right tasks, helping to remove any obstacles to the team members’ progress, and protecting the team from distractions.

Working with the product owners to maintain a healthy product backlog.

Facilitating scrum ceremonies (daily standups, sprint planning, retrospect etc) as needed.

Working with Technology Relationship management to interface with the product managers so as to prioritize and ensure continuous flow of delivery to meet business needs.

Educational qualifications and work experience:

Bachelor’s degree in any IT- related field

Professional Qualifications in Scrum Master certification.

3 Years of minimum experience in administering Burndown technologies, Retrospective formats, and handling bugs, experience working with Agile and Scrum methodology in successful projects, an understanding of the rules and practices of other Agile approaches. This includes the differences between Scrum and Kanban and how they may be blended for optimum results.

Collaborates closely with Product Owners and Technology Relationship Management teams to prepare and clarify the Prioritized Product Backlog and the Definition of the Done Criteria and facilitates Prioritized Product Backlog Reviews with the product owner.

Facilitates identification of the stakeholders and manages the stakeholders and vendors as required for business projects or initiatives

Responsible for creating release plans including deliverables and the release deadline, plans and estimates the highest value deliverables for the next release

Demonstrate and Validate Sprints by facilitating presentation of completed Deliverables by the Scrum Team for the Product Owner’s approval

Supports the Scrum Team in determining the length of sprint, creating the deliverables, identification of tasks and effort estimation for the tasks agreed for a sprint.

Monitoring progress and performance of the scrum teams and keeping the organization up to date on the progress of the scrum team’s projects & initiatives by preparing and presenting status reports to stakeholders.

Daily Responsibilities:

Helping the Scrum teams agree on what they can achieve during each development sprint (or other period of time).

Helping the team continuously make progress on the projects by making sure each person is working on the right tasks, helping to remove any obstacles to the team members’ progress, and protecting the team from distractions.

Working with the product owners to maintain a healthy product backlog.

Facilitating scrum ceremonies (daily standups, sprint planning, retrospect etc) as needed.

Working with Technology Relationship management to interface with the product managers so as to prioritize and ensure continuous flow of delivery to meet business needs.

Educational qualifications and work experience:

Bachelor’s degree in any IT- related field

Professional Qualifications in Scrum Master certification.

3 Years of minimum experience in administering Burndown technologies, Retrospective formats, and handling bugs, experience working with Agile and Scrum methodology in successful projects, an understanding of the rules and practices of other Agile approaches. This includes the differences between Scrum and Kanban and how they may be blended for optimum results.

item.description:
AML Manager (1)

Job Purpose

Play a pivotal leadership role in ensuring implementation of the comprehensive financial crime and internal compliance strategies, ensuring the bank’s unwavering adherence to financial crime compliance standards and internal policies and procedures. This pivotal position involves leading initiatives and driving awareness programs, to fortify the bank’s financial crime and internal compliance standing. As a strategic leader, the role holder will play a key role in shaping and safeguarding our financial integrity landscape, contributing significantly to the bank's commitment to financial crime and internal compliance excellence.

Main Responsibilities

Lead implementation of the financial crime compliance program and internal policies compliance risks management and lead a team of compliance analysts to execute the program.

Oversee the development and implementation of policies and procedures related to financial crime compliance and internal policies compliance and provide guidance and feedback to the compliance team on implementation.

Lead risk assessment tasks and develop mitigation strategies for financial crime and internal policies and procedures compliance, and work with the compliance team to implement and monitor the mitigation strategies.

Lead reporting to senior management on compliance with financial crime compliance requirements and internal policies & procedures and make recommendations for improvement.

Stay up to date on the latest financial crime compliance regulations and disseminate this knowledge to the compliance team, and all bank employees.

Collaborate with other departments to ensure compliance with financial crime regulations and internal policies across the organization.

Drive the direction, development, maintenance, and distribution of Financial Crime compliance awareness programs, systems training, and other internal compliance training across the bank units.

Foster continuous engagement with business units to provide expert advice on compliance aspects of new products and projects, for conformance with financial crime compliance program.

Oversee preparation of internal and external compliance reports under the central compliance office regarding financial crime compliance and internal policies & procedures.

Lead implementation of financial crime and internal compliance initiatives and projects overseeing their seamless integration across the bank and ensuring alignment with financial crime regulatory requirements and organizational objectives.

Daily Responsibilities:

Supervise handling of the financial crime monitoring tools, including AML/CFT systems in BPR Bank Rwanda Plc and provide liaison across the Group.

Coordinate with relevant departments and regulator on financial crime compliance related issues

Provide expert advice on financial crime compliance aspects on new/changed products, services, and channels..

Periodically carry out comprehensive financial crime (including AML/CFT/CFP) risk assessment for BPR Bank Rwanda activities.

Lead and guide the financial crime compliance analysts’ team on the progress of the financial crime compliance program and internal policies compliance risks management plan.

Educational qualifications and work experience:

Bachelor’s degree in any related field

Professional Qualifications ACAMS/ACCPA

5 years of minimum experience In Banking Compliance /audit Banking, Analytical skills experience and Supervisory/Managerial experience.

item.title_raw: Audit and Accounts Trainee at HLB Rwanda : (Deadline 27-09-2026)
item.description:
Audit and Accounts Trainee Job Vacancy at HLB Rwanda. 

HLB Rwanda is a leading Accounting and Business Advisory firm in the region with a diverse  client portfolio. The firm is currently sourcing for talent to join our team in the Audit  department and Accounts department. This is a unique opportunity for an ambitious candidate  willing to join a multicultural workforce. The successful candidate will be responsible for the  following: 

Your key responsibilities; 

As an Audit and Accounts Trainee, you will work on various audit engagements in different  industry sectors. You will; 

➢ Develop an understanding of the audit client’s business. 

➢ Interact with the clients in order to collect all the necessary data/information, set-up  and maintain audit files, prepare lead schedules, etc. 

➢ Support the planning, execution and delivery of assurance engagements.

➢ Clearly and accurately document the execution of specific audit procedures as defined  by the engagement objectives, audit client's engagement history, and planned audit  approach. 

➢ Recognize potential audit issues or unusual relationships from basic analysis of the  financial statements and communicate them to the assurance team. 

Qualifications and Competence Required: 

➢ Graduate in the field of accounting and finance. 

➢ At least two years’ experience in audit or accounting environment. 

➢ Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

➢ Strong drive to excel professionally, and to guide and motivate others.

➢ Advanced written and verbal communication skills. 

➢ Dedicated, innovative, resourceful, analytical and able to work under pressure.

➢ Foster an efficient, innovative and team-oriented work environment. 

Method of Application 

Interested candidates should submit their CV’s and copies of Academic/professional certificates  to; elie@hlbrwanda.com  and copy info@hlbrwanda.com ; using the position as the subject of  the email. Application Deadline is 27th September 2026.

Record laundry quantities, machine cycles, chemical usage, and equipment problems where required. Assist in identifying damaged linen and separating items requiring repair or disposal. Record laundry quantities, machine cycles, chemical usage, and equipment problems where required. Assist in identifying damaged linen and separating items requiring repair or disposal. Type of contract: Fixed term

Working location: National Office

Supervisor: Deputy National Director - Operations

Deadline: 27th September 2026

Context of the position:

To move ICT from 'fixing laptops' to 'leveraging technology' for social impact. The Senior Manager, ICT and Programmes Digitalisation leads SOS Rwanda's ICT function and drives the organisation's digital transformation agenda, designing and implementing ICT strategy, managing all ICT systems and infrastructure, leading the digitalisation of programme and operational workflows, implementing secure digital case management platforms, ensuring cybersecurity and data protection, and building staff digital literacy across all four Program Areas.

Main clients: 

Deputy National Director for Operations

National Director

All National Management Team (NMT) members

Head of Finance — ERP and financial systems

Head of MEAL — digital MEL platforms

Head of HROD — HRIS systems

Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics — procurement systems

Programme teams across all four area offices

SOS Regional ICT Advisor (ESAF) and SOS International ICT teams
