item.title: Notice for Provision of Long Term Car Leasing Services tender at Broadband Systems Corporation
item.description:
Notice for Provision of Long Term Car Leasing Services Tender at Broadband Systems Corporation Plc

Broadband Systems Corporation Plc ("BSC") is a licensed Internet Service Provider (ISP) that is incorporated under the laws and regulations of the Republic of Rwanda. The company is engaged in the business of providing advanced Information and Communication Technology ("ICT") services based on broadband connectivity. 

2. BSC Plc invites qualified bidders to submit bids for the PROVISION OF LONG TERM CAR LEASING SERVICES TO BSC LTD. The tender is indivisible. 

3. Participation to this tender is open on equal conditions to all companies specialised in the field of and qualifying bidder must present the following documents and requirements in their bids; 

Bid submission form and price schedules well printed and properly organized. 

Company profile including proven experience of at least 15 years in car leasing services. 

Copy of business registration certificate. 

Original or copy of clearance certificate for Rwanda Social Security Board. 

Copy of Valid Tax Clearance Certificate. 

RURA transport service certificate 

Three references of similar tender executed (good completion certificates) with government, corporate companies or international organisations. 

4. The tender documents can be downloaded from www.bsc.rw or obtained free of charge from BSC LTD Procurement office at Remera, Airport Road (KN5 RD), Opposite Chez Lando. 

5. Well printed, properly bound bids presented in 3 copies one of which marked original, must reach BSC 's Procurement office at Remera Airport Road (KN5 RD), Opposite Chez Lando not later than 23rd September 2026 at 11:00 A.m. late bids shall be rejected. The public opening will take place at 11h30 A.m. on the same day at BSC conference room. 

6. The copies should be put in 'inner envelopes' having the name and address of the company. All copies should be put in other envelope called "outer envelope" marked with the reference number of tender notice with the following mentions: 

To: Chairperson of the Tender Committee e BSC Plc 

Tender tittle: "PROVISION OF LONG TERM CAR LEASING SERVICES TO BSC LTD" Broadband Systems Corporation Ltd (BSC LTD), 

Remera Airport Road 

(KN5 RD), Opposite Chez Lando 

PO Box 7229, Kigali, Rwanda 

E-mail: <procurement-bsc@bsc.rw> 

7. The bids must have a validity period of one hundred twenty days (120) days from the bids opening date.

item.title: Notice for Provision of Cleaning Services for 2027 tender at SNV Rwanda
item.description:
Notice for Provision of Cleaning Services for 2027 Tender at SNV Rwanda

About SNV and Background of the assignment

SNV SNV Netherlands Development Organization is a not-for-profit international development organization founded in the Netherlands in 1965 with a global presence in 30 countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. As an organization, SNV focuses on the Agriculture, WASH, and Energy sectors with the belief that no one should have to live in poverty and that all people should have the opportunity to pursue their own sustainable development. SNV contributes to these sectors by strengthening the capacity of targeted partners and communities at the field level to realize increased skill sets and sustainable performance; reduce poverty levels and expand employment; and improve food security while paying special attention to gender equity, social inclusion of marginalized groups and stakeholder accountability.

1.2. Background of the Assignment 

SNV Rwanda invites reputable and experienced companies to submit quotations for the provision of cleaning services. The selected service provider will provide cleaning services on an as-needed basis for a period of twelve (12) months, in accordance with the requirements and terms set out in this RFQ.

Offerors are responsible for ensuring that their quotations are submitted in accordance with the instructions, requirements, terms and conditions contained in this RFQ. Failure to comply with the requirements may result in the offer being considered non-responsive.

2. General Instructions and conditions

This is a Request for Quotations only. Issuance of this RFQ does not obligate SNV to make an award or reimburse any costs incurred by an offeror in preparing or submitting an offer.

Any award resulting from this RFQ will be formalised through an appropriate SNV contractual instrument.

SNV reserves the right to request clarifications or negotiate with any offeror before making an award.

SNV may make a partial award or split the award among more than one service provider where this is considered to be in SNV's best interest.

SNV reserves the right to cancel the RFQ at any time.

Payment will normally be made within thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of a valid invoice and confirmation that the services have been satisfactorily delivered and accepted.

Release of payment is subject to satisfactory performance and written acceptance of the services in accordance with the RFQ and the resulting contract or purchase order.

3. Terms of reference and Service requirements

SNV is seeking offers from reputable, well established and experienced offerors, duly incorporated under the Laws of Rwanda to provide cleaning services under a Fixed Contract Agreement (FCA), at fixed prices for a period of 12 months.

3.1 Responsibilities of offeror (Company, supplier or vendor)

The following cleaning instructions are outlined by building, cleaning location within the building and cleaning schedule.

Empty all waste receptacles, replace liners as required, and remove waste to the designated collection point. SNV will provide waste-bin liners.

Spot-clean partition glass to remove fingerprints, smudges and other marks.

Dust horizontal and vertical surfaces, including windowsills, ledges, mouldings, telephones, pictures, office furniture and other furnishings.

Clean drinking fountains, removing watermarks and splashes from surrounding surfaces.

Dust-mop all hard-surface floors.

Damp-mop hard-surface floors, including corners, edges and areas beneath furniture where accessible.

Spot-clean walls, light switches and doors to remove fingerprints, smudges and spills.

Clean interior windows and both sides of partition glass, including damp-wiping window and glass frames.

Clean and sanitise toilets and urinals inside and outside, including polishing of brightwork.

Clean toilet seats on both sides.

Scour and sanitise all washbasins.

Remove splash marks from walls around washbasins.

Report any restroom repairs or maintenance requirements to the SNV Operations Department.

Clean and wipe restroom partitions on both sides.

Pour fresh water into floor drains as necessary to maintain the sewer line, with particular attention to Saturdays.

Provide and maintain a list of cleaning staff assigned to the SNV premises.

Provide designated staff to support tea and coffee service in the kitchen, as required and agreed with SNV.

3.2 Cleaning equipment and materials 

The selected service provider shall supply all cleaning equipment, cleaning chemicals, waste bags, paper towels, hand soap, toilet paper required to perform the services. The services are intended to cover approximately 934 square metres of office space and up to fifty (50) staff members at the SNV Country Office. Restocking requirements shall be coordinated with the SNV Operations Office.

3.3 Reporting Damage

The selected service provider shall promptly report any damaged facilities, fixtures or broken items to the SNV Operations Officer. Such reports should be made at least bi-weekly and immediately where the damage requires urgent attention, to ensure that the service provider is not held responsible for pre-existing or reported damage.

4. Quotation and price requirement 

Quotations shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs (RWF) and shall be presented as fixed prices. The quotation shall remain valid for at least forty-five (45) calendar days from the submission deadline.

Quoted prices shall remain fixed for the initial twelve (12)-month contract period, unless a price adjustment is mutually agreed by the parties and justified by significant changes in market conditions.

Offerors shall submit their quotation using their official quotation format or company letterhead and shall provide a clear breakdown of the proposed costs in the required price schedule.

5. Taxes and statutory requirements

All quoted prices shall be inclusive of all applicable taxes, charges, tariffs, duties and levies.

Offerors shall provide the following supporting documents, as applicable:

A signed cover letter containing the full contact details of the person authorised to receive correspondence, including name, position, email address and telephone number.

VAT registration certificate, where applicable.

Valid Rwanda Development Board (RDB) registration certificate, where applicable.

Valid Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) tax clearance certificate.

Valid business registration certificate or business licence, including evidence of compliance with applicable social security requirements.

6. Eligibility: By submitting an offer in response to this RFQ, the offeror certifies that the company and its principal officers are not debarred, suspended or otherwise considered ineligible to participate in procurement under applicable Rwandan laws or relevant international requirements. SNV will not award a contract to any firm that is debarred, suspended or otherwise ineligible.

7. Evaluation and Award: 

The award will be made to a responsible and eligible offeror whose quotation complies with the RFQ requirements and provides the best value to SNV based on the evaluation criteria below.

Evaluation Criterion
Description
Maximum Score

Technical responsiveness / compliance
Extent to which the bidder meets the required cleaning specifications and demonstrates adequate capacity, including personnel, equipment, cleaning materials, and proposed approach to delivering the services.
25

Company experience and track record
Demonstrated experience (minimum three years) in providing office cleaning or similar services, supported by evidence of previous or current comparable assignments (At least three Certificates) and client references.
35

Financial proposal / price
Overall cost of the proposed services, supported by a clear and complete price breakdown.
40

Note: Offers with significant deficiencies in meeting the requirements may be considered non-responsive and disqualified. SNV reserves the right to waive immaterial deficiencies at its discretion.

8. Offer submission Checklist

To facilitate the preparation and review of offers, each offer should include the following:

Official quotation on company letterhead.

Signed statement confirming acceptance of the requirements and terms of this RFQ.

Completed price schedule with a clear cost breakdown.

Valid business registration certificate or business licence.

VAT certificate, where applicable.

Valid tax clearance certificate.

Evidence of relevant experience, including copies or references for similar contracts where available.

Complete contact details of the authorised contact person.

9. Submission of offers.

Completed quotations, together with all required supporting documentation, shall be submitted by email to rwandaprocurement@snv.org no later than 15 October 2026. The email subject line shall clearly state “Provision of Cleaning Services.”

Office Visit: Interested bidders may visit the office between 22nd to 30th September 2026, from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM, during which time access to the premises will be permitted.

10. Key compliance issues 

Consultant must comply with SNV’s environmental and Social Safeguarding policies and procedures as well as take into consideration donor-specific requirements. 

11. Data Protection assurance 

SNV will not retain your Personal Data for longer than is allowed by law or is necessary for the Purposes.

If you are selected and offered consultancy assignment, the Personal Data you have provided will be used by SNV for the purpose of this bidding administration. If you are unsuccessful on this occasion to secure tender with SNV, SNV will retain your Personal Data for required period for the purpose of any future internal or external audit.

4. Quotation and price requirement

Quotations shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs (RWF) and shall be presented as fixed prices. The quotation shall remain valid for at least forty-five (45) calendar days from the submission deadline.

Quoted prices shall remain fixed for the initial twelve (12)-month contract period, unless a price adjustment is mutually agreed by the parties and justified by significant changes in market conditions.

Offerors shall submit their quotation using their official quotation format or company letterhead and shall provide a clear breakdown of the proposed costs in the required price schedule.

5. Taxes and statutory requirements

All quoted prices shall be inclusive of all applicable taxes, charges, tariffs, duties and levies.

Offerors shall provide the following supporting documents, as applicable:

Valid business registration certificate or business licence, including evidence of compliance with applicable social security requirements.

Valid Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) tax clearance certificate.

Valid Rwanda Development Board (RDB) registration certificate, where applicable.

VAT registration certificate, where applicable.

A signed cover letter containing the full contact details of the person authorised to receive correspondence, including name, position, email address and telephone number.

6. Eligibility: By submitting an offer in response to this RFQ, the offeror certifies that the company and its principal officers are not debarred, suspended or otherwise considered ineligible to participate in procurement under applicable Rwandan laws or relevant international requirements. SNV will not award a contract to any firm that is debarred, suspended or otherwise ineligible.

The award will be made to a responsible and eligible offeror whose quotation complies with the RFQ requirements and provides the best value to SNV based on the evaluation criteria below.

Evaluation Criterion
Description
Maximum Score

Technical responsiveness / compliance
Compliance with the required list of kitchen materials and refreshments, including the required specifications, quantities, quality requirements, packaging, and delivery requirements. The offeror must demonstrate its ability to supply all required items.
20

Company experience and track record
Relevant experience in supplying kitchen materials, catering supplies, refreshments, beverages, snacks, or similar goods. Offerors should provide evidence of at least three (3) completion certificates from current or previous clients.
40

Financial proposal / prices
Overall cost of the proposed supplies including unit prices, quantities, and all applicable taxes.
40

Note: Offers with significant deficiencies in meeting the requirements may be considered non-responsive and disqualified. SNV reserves the right to waive immaterial deficiencies at its discretion.

8. Offer submission Checklist

To facilitate the preparation and review of offers, each offer should include the following:

Official quotation on company letterhead.

Completed price schedule with a clear cost breakdown.

RDB Valid business registration certificate

Valid tax clearance certificate.

Evidence of relevant experience, including copies or references for similar contracts where available.

Complete contact details of the authorised contact person.

9. Submission of offers.

Completed quotations, together with all required supporting documentation, shall be submitted by email to rwandaprocurement@snv.org no later than October 15, 2026. The email subject line shall clearly state “Supply of Kitchen Materials and Refreshments.”

Key compliance issues

Consultant must comply with SNV’s environmental and Social Safeguarding policies and procedures as well as take into consideration donor-specific requirements.

Data Protection assurance

SNV will not retain your Personal Data for longer than is allowed by law or is necessary for the Purposes.

If you are selected and offered consultancy assignment, the Personal Data you have provided will be used by SNV for the purpose of this bidding administration. If you are unsuccessful on this occasion to secure tender with SNV, SNV will retain your Personal Data for required period for the purpose of any future internal or external audit.

item.title: Provision of Operation and Maintenance Services of Oxygen PSA Plants in Rwanda Hospitals tender at Rwanda Medical Supply Limited
item.description_html:
Provision of Operation and Maintenance Services of Oxygen PSA Plants in Rwanda Hospitals Tender at Rwanda Medical Supply Ltd

Medical oxygen is an essential medicine for which there are no alternatives. It is required to treat chronic and acute conditions and to conduct safe surgeries and oxygen is included on the World Health Organization (WHO) list of Essential Medicines. In Rwanda, it is designated by the Ministry of Health (MOH) of Rwanda as an essential inhalation medicine.

The public supply of medical oxygen should be sustained and reach all those in need. Due to Government of Rwanda (GOR) investments, 28 of 55 public health facilities currently have one or more oxygen production plants on site. Overall, these plants combined have a maximum oxygen production capacity of 20,300,000 L per day or approximately 406,000 cylinders (50L) per month.

Recent investments by the GOR and its partners have increased the oxygen production capacity of public hospitals and most of public health facilities are equipped with medical gas piping systems for easy and safe delivery of medical oxygen to the bedside. Although a remarkable progress, there are still some barriers to be addressed; in the production, and distribution including the PSA plants maintenance.

The GoR, through the Ministry of Health (MoH), Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC), Clinton Heath Access Initiative (CHAI) and Rwanda Medical Supply (RMS), intends to establish a Partnership under an Operate–Maintain–Replace (OMR) model to ensure sustainable, equitable, and reliable access to medical oxygen across public health facilities in Rwanda.

The partnership will leverage the existing national network of PSA oxygen plants distributed across public hospitals and associated health facilities. The selected contractor(s) shall assume responsibility for operation, maintenance, distribution, lifecycle management, and replacement of designated oxygen production assets while ownership of the assets remains with the GOR. This TOR provides a framework to guide the contractor(s) in the respective scopes of work to ensure continued and reliable access to oxygen.

The Competitive Dialogue process is being undertaken with selected supplier(s) to refine the final technical, operational, commercial, legal, and contractual structure before issuing the final tender and contract award..

2. Objective of the Competitive Dialogue

The objective of the Competitive Dialogue is to engage oxygen PSA plants’ suppliers in structured discussions to refine and optimize the proposed model and support the development of a bankable, sustainable, and performance-based procurement structure.

Specifically, the dialogue aims to:

  • Validate the operational feasibility of the OMR model;
  • Determine optimal lot configuration and hub allocation arrangements;
  • Define efficient oxygen production and distribution models;
  • Establish sustainable operation, maintenance and asset replacement mechanisms;
  • Define measurable service levels and key performance indicators (KPIs);
  • Establish surge preparedness and emergency response mechanisms;
  • Ensure affordability, value for money, and long-term sustainability;
  • Finalize the contractual and payment framework.

3. SCOPE OF PROCUREMENT

3.1 Operation of PSA Oxygen Plants

The operator shall:

  • Operate designated PSA oxygen plants and associated infrastructure;
  • Optimize PSA plants placement across the network
  • Ensure continuous oxygen production in accordance with required purity and quality standards.;
  • Manage plant staffing, operational scheduling, utilities coordination, and production planning;
  • Plan the demand and supply of medical oxygen its designated areas
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable health, environmental, and safety regulations.
  • Operator shall have the minimum national oxygen reserve stock and filled backup cylinders

3.2 Maintenance and Asset Management

The operator shall:

  • Conduct preventive, corrective, and emergency maintenance for all assigned equipment;
  • Maintain PSA plants in accordance with manufacturer standards and specifications;
  • Ensure availability of spare parts and consumables;
  • Develop and implement lifecycle management plans for all assigned assets;
  • Replace end-of-life equipment and major components in accordance with agreed contractual requirements;
  • Maintain accurate maintenance logs and asset registers.
  • The operator shall return all government-owned assets in good operating condition, subject to independent technical verification

3.3 Oxygen Distribution Services

The operator shall:

  • Manage end-to-end oxygen distribution through the designated hub-and-spoke network;
  • Invest in cylinders, filling equipment, and distribution fleet (All sizes of oxygen cylinders, trucks, trolleys,)
  • Ensure timely refill and delivery of oxygen cylinders to all assigned health facilities up to primary health level facilities including ambulances.
  • Optimize transport routes and delivery schedules;
  • Maintain adequate cylinder tracking and inventory management systems;
  • Ensure uninterrupted supply within the agreed service coverage area.

3.4 Quality Assurance and Regulatory Compliance

The operator shall:

  • Ensure oxygen purity meets applicable medical standards;
  • Maintain calibration and testing systems for quality verification for both PSAs and cylinders;
  • Comply with Rwanda FDA, MoH, RBC, and other applicable regulatory requirements;
  • Establish quality assurance protocols and incident reporting mechanisms.

3.5 Risk Mitigation for Emergency Preparedness 

  • The contingency framework will include two levels of reserve oxygen stock. First, each PSA plant operator shall maintain a minimum reserve equivalent to 100 cylinders of oxygen at each lot.
  • By design, the contractor will maintain a reasonable number of competing PSA plant operators to promote supply security, operational resilience, and market stability. No merger or monopoly arrangement shall be permitted under this framework, and no single oxygen PSA operator shall supply more than 35% of the national public-sector medical oxygen demand. 
  • The contractor will also require mandatory performance bond arrangements throughout the contractual period. This mechanism will protect both the GOR and the PSA plant operators while promoting sustainable and reliable medical oxygen supply through a partnership model based on mutual accountability and shared benefits. 
  • Operators shall maintain adequate stocks of preventive and corrective maintenance spare parts, as well as emergency cylinder filling and backup supply mechanisms. Considering the lifespan and replacement schedules of critical equipment and components, operators will be required to plan and execute maintenance and replacement activities proactively to avoid any interruption in medical oxygen supply. 
  • While optimization is a primary objective, any relocation, consolidation, or repurposing of PSA plants shall be carefully assessed and justified based on the availability of adequate and reliable alternative sources of medical oxygen supply. No movement of PSA infrastructure shall occur without comprehensive contingency planning, formal risk assessment, and mutual agreement with the designated representative of the GoR. 

3.6 Financing

  • Cover all needed CAPEX to run the network including but not cylinders, distribution trucks, relocating PSAs, replacing PSA, supply chain management tools
  • Cover all operational costs needed to operate the production including but not limited to staffing, maintenance and repair of equipment, power supply, and other utilities, administrative and office costs.
  • Revenue will be recovered from supplying oxygen to health facilities per cubic meter
  • Oxygen will be delivered on standardized tariff per cubic meter delivered to health facility

4. Key Discussion Areas During Competitive Dialogue

The Competitive Dialogue process will focus on the following areas:

4.1 Technical and Operational Structure

  • Hub allocation and lot structure;
  • Management of co-located PSA facilities;
  • Production optimization strategies;
  • Fleet and cylinder management systems;
  • Transition arrangements from current operational structures.

4.2 Commercial and Financial Structure

  • Payment mechanisms;
  • Output-based financing arrangements;
  • Tariff structure and affordability considerations;
  • Asset replacement financing mechanisms;
  • Revenue sustainability and commercial viability.

4.3 Contractual and Risk Allocation

  • Allocation of operational, maintenance, and demand risks;
  • Force majeure and emergency response obligations;
  • Performance guarantees and penalties;
  • Contract duration and renewal provisions.

4.4 Performance Management

The dialogue shall define KPIs including but not limited to:

  • Plant uptime;
  • Asset condition score
  • Oxygen purity compliance;
  • Delivery lead times;
  • Order fulfillment rates;
  • Stock out days per facility
  • Cylinder turnaround time
  • Reporting compliance
  • Safety incident rate
  • Maintenance response times; Emergency response readiness
  • Strategic stock level (days of cover)
  • Spare part stock availability

5. Deliverables Expected from Bidders

Shortlisted bidders participating in the dialogue process shall be expected to provide:

  • Initial technical and operational proposals;
  • Proposed lot allocation and hub management approach;
  • Proposed maintenance and lifecycle management strategy;
  • Proposed distribution and logistics model;
  • Proposed staffing and technical support arrangements;
  • Preliminary commercial and financial model to the different cost centers;
  • Risk allocation recommendations;
  • Proposed service level agreements and KPIs;
  • Emergency preparedness and business continuity plans;
  • Recommendations for contract structure and implementation arrangements.

6. Eligibility requirements

Interested bidders are required to submit the following documents:

  1. A letter addressed to Rwanda Medical Supply expressing the interest in participating in the oxygen PSA plant O&M PPP model
  2. A signed technical proposal of PSA plant operation and maintenance approach
  3. Valid company certificate of incorporation/Business registration certificate
  4. Valid tax clearance certificate
  5. At least 3 years experience in the operation and maintenance of PSA plants, proven by 2 good completion certificates or contracts, with a combined cost not less than 500,000,000 Frw
  6. Requirements for Engineers: 2
  • Bachelor’s degree in any of the following fields: Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Biomedical Engineering proven by a copy of the degree certificate
  • At least 2 years’ experience in operation and maintenance of PSA plants
  • Update curriculum vitae
  1. Requirements for technicians: 4
  • Diploma in any of the following fields: Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Biomedical Engineering proven by a copy of the degree certificate
  • At least 1 years experience in operation and maintenance of PSA plants
  • Update curriculum vitae
  1. Local bidders are required to provide any PSA plant manufacturer authorization

7. Duration of the Contract

The anticipated contract duration shall be discussed during the Competitive Dialogue process and may include provisions for renewal based on performance and achievement of contractual obligations.

8. PPP Framework

  • The framework will be overseen by a MOH designated multidisciplinary Performance Review Technical Working Group (TWG). The TWG will support the RMS designated Contract Manager in managing overall contract(s) performance, evaluating key performance indicators (KPIs), reviewing compliance with contractual obligations, including maintenance and asset replacement requirements, and providing technical recommendations on contractual decisions and corrective actions where necessary.
  • The TWG will comprise representatives from the MOH, Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC), RMS, the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), and other development partners supporting the GOR in strengthening the national medical oxygen ecosystem. The TWG will support the proper transition, operational oversight, and asset management of the oxygen PSA plants throughout the PPP lifecycle.
  • In collaboration with the host institutions and relevant government entities, the TWG will also follow up on the continuity of supply arrangements and ensure sustained access to essential utilities and infrastructure required for uninterrupted PSA plant operations, including electricity, water, and network connectivity. The TWG will serve as the technical coordination and oversight arm for the effective implementation of the PPP framework, from transition and operationalization through final contractual completion.
  • Working closely with the designated Contract Manager, the TWG will support the establishment and effective implementation of standardized systems for oxygen measurement across production, storage, and distribution operations, as well as quality assurance, monitoring, reporting, and real-time operational oversight. The TWG will also promote and support data-driven performance management, transparency, accountability, and continuous quality improvement to ensure a sustainable, efficient, resilient, and uninterrupted national medical oxygen supply system.

9. Governing Framework

The Competitive Dialogue and subsequent procurement process shall be conducted in accordance with:

  • Rwanda Medical supply procurement policy;
  • Rwanda Medical Supply PPP regulatory framework;
  • Applicable health sector regulations and policies;
  • Any additional guidance issued by the Government of Rwanda.

10. PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE

The competitive dialogue procedure will follow these key steps:

Phase I.

  1. Call for Initial Proposals: Interested bidders are invited to submit the proposals in response to this tender. The documents required at this stage are specified in section VI
  2. Shortlisting of Bidders: Bidders will be shortlisted based on evaluation findings of initial proposals as described in section VI.

Phase II:

  1. Dialogue Phase RMS will conduct structured dialogues with each of the shortlisted bidders. During this phase:
    • Technical specifications will be refined.
    • Confidentiality will be maintained for all bidder-specific information unless explicitly agreed otherwise.
    • Equal treatment of all bidders will be ensured.
  2. Submission of Final Offers After the dialogue phase concludes and specifications are finalized, RMS will invite final offers from all shortlisted suppliers.
  3. Evaluation and Contract Award

Final offers will be evaluated based on the established evaluation criteria. The contract will be awarded to the most economically and technically advantageous offer.

11. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES

Interested suppliers are invited to submit initial proposals by 30/9/2026 at 10:00am local time

Submissions must be made only electronically to our confidential email: tenders@rms.rw with the subject line: “Tender for oxygen PSA plant Operation”.

For questions and clarifications, please contact rms.procurement@rms.rw with a copy to cgatsinzi@rms.rw ,jmvnkurunziza@rms.rw, jczimurida@rms.rw and erugamba@rms.rw

item.title: Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) monitoring services  tender at Trinity Musha Mines Ltd
item.description:
Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) monitoring services Tender at Trinity Musha Mines Limited

Trinity Metals (Trinity Nyakabingo mines ,Trinity Rutongo mines and Trinity Musha mines Limited) invites Expressions of Interest from qualified experts and service providers to undertake independent Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) monitoring across its mining operations. The assignment is intended to establish a historical deformation baseline and provide continuous, independent quarterly monitoring of waste rock facilities, tailings storage facilities, and ground subsidence to achieve precise stability data.

1. Scope of Work

The scope of the InSAR monitoring services includes, but is not limited to, the following:

Establish a historical displacement baseline utilizing a minimum of 2 years of archived SAR satellite imagery.

Provide continuous surface displacement monitoring, delivering update reports to provide independent technical assurance.

Monitor ground displacements across critical infrastructure, specifically focusing on waste dumps, tailings storage facilities, and areas impacted by underground mining or subsidence.

Measure displacements of the ground's surface at the millimetre scale. 

Calculate and model the line-of-sight (LOS), vertical, and east-west components of the surface displacement.

Distil the geotechnically relevant signal from the geotechnically irrelevant noise.

Provide comprehensive reports that highlight displacement anomalies where velocity rates have accelerated compared to the historical baseline.

2. Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

Have demonstrated expertise in interferometry and geodetic estimation techniques.

Preferably possess proprietary software, algorithms, and intellectual data processing capabilities for InSAR data processing. 

Demonstrate the ability to utilize advanced processing techniques, such as Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSI) combining persistent and distributed scatterers, or Small Baseline Subset (SBAS) approaches.

Possess the capability to account for, process, and visualize SAR geometric effects inherent in steep mining terrain, including radar shadow, foreshortening, and layover.

Have a proven track record of providing satellite InSAR monitoring services across the mining industry.

All interested service providers should submit an Expression of Interest together with the following supporting documents:

Cover letter introducing the company or individual consultant, confirming interest, availability, and understanding of the technical assignment.

Company profile detailing InSAR technical capabilities, proprietary processing tools, and domain expertise.

Summary of similar InSAR surface displacement monitoring assignments undertaken for the mining industry.

Proposed methodology for establishing the 2-year historical baseline and conducting the ongoing quarterly analysis.

CVs of proposed personnel clearly demonstrating experience in undertaking of InSAR monitoring work. 

Summary of at least three similar assignments undertaken in the last five years, including client name, project scope, location, and contactable references. 

Certificate of domestic company registration issued by RDB.

VAT registration certificate, where applicable.

Valid tax clearance certificate issued by RRA.

Submissions should be forwarded to tender@trinity-metals.com  no later than 30 September 2026 at 11:00 AM local time.

Expressions of Interest received after 11:00 AM local time on 30 September 2026 will not be considered.

Shortlisted respondents may be invited for further technical discussions to confirm capability and suitability. Thereafter, Trinity Metals may issue an invitation to tender to selected qualified bidders.

Establish a historical displacement baseline utilizing a minimum of 2 years of archived SAR satellite imagery.

Provide continuous surface displacement monitoring, delivering update reports to provide independent technical assurance.

Monitor ground displacements across critical infrastructure, specifically focusing on waste dumps, tailings storage facilities, and areas impacted by underground mining or subsidence.

Measure displacements of the ground's surface at the millimetre scale. 

Calculate and model the line-of-sight (LOS), vertical, and east-west components of the surface displacement.

Distil the geotechnically relevant signal from the geotechnically irrelevant noise.

Provide comprehensive reports that highlight displacement anomalies where velocity rates have accelerated compared to the historical baseline.

2. Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

Have demonstrated expertise in interferometry and geodetic estimation techniques.

Preferably possess proprietary software, algorithms, and intellectual data processing capabilities for InSAR data processing. 

Demonstrate the ability to utilize advanced processing techniques, such as Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSI) combining persistent and distributed scatterers, or Small Baseline Subset (SBAS) approaches.

Possess the capability to account for, process, and visualize SAR geometric effects inherent in steep mining terrain, including radar shadow, foreshortening, and layover.

Have a proven track record of providing satellite InSAR monitoring services across the mining industry.

All interested service providers should submit an Expression of Interest together with the following supporting documents:

Cover letter introducing the company or individual consultant, confirming interest, availability, and understanding of the technical assignment.

Company profile detailing InSAR technical capabilities, proprietary processing tools, and domain expertise.

Summary of similar InSAR surface displacement monitoring assignments undertaken for the mining industry.

Proposed methodology for establishing the 2-year historical baseline and conducting the ongoing quarterly analysis.

CVs of proposed personnel clearly demonstrating experience in undertaking of InSAR monitoring work. 

Summary of at least three similar assignments undertaken in the last five years, including client name, project scope, location, and contactable references.

item.title: Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to supply a Geotechnical Engineering Software Suite and Technical Support  tender at Trinity Musha Mines Ltd
item.description:
Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to supply a Geotechnical Engineering Software Suite and Technical Support Trinity Musha Mines Limited

Trinity Metals (Trinity Nyakabingo mines ,Trinity Rutongo mines and Trinity Musha mines Limited) invites Expressions of Interest from qualified software service providers to supply a comprehensive geotechnical engineering software suite across its mining operations. The assignment is intended to provide advanced 3D numerical modelling, stability analysis, and data interpretation tools to support the continued stability and safety of surface and underground mining infrastructure.

Scope of Work

The scope of the software provision and technical support includes, but is not limited to, the

following:

Provision of multi-seat annual lease licenses for 3D finite element analysis (FEA) software or integrated suite capable of:

Evaluating soil and rock mechanics, 3D excavation design, tunnelling, support design, and groundwater seepage.

3D stability analysis software for evaluating underground excavations in jointed rock and modelling intersecting rock wedges.

Graphical and statistical analysis tools for orientation-based geological data, stereonet plotting, and kinematic analysis of rock slopes.

Analysis of rock and soil strength data, failure criteria evaluation, and material property determination.

Integration of data from geological and mine planning software for numerical model building

Delivery of software licenses via a Cloud/Online License management system, with full administrative privileges granted to Trinity Metals for independent user management. Local servers and physical dongles will not be accepted.

Provision of ongoing updates and maintenance, including major version releases and minor patches.

Comprehensive technical support covering software functionality, bug resolution, and license troubleshooting, with a guaranteed initial response time of 1 to 2 business days.

Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

Be an established developer or authorized provider of globally recognized geotechnical engineering software, with demonstrated application in hard rock underground mining environments.

Provide software products that natively integrate and interoperate (e.g., importing material properties into numerical models, exporting joint orientations into stability analysis modules).

Ensure the software suite is fully compatible with standard corporate IT environments, specifically Windows 64-bit systems.

Demonstrate compliance with data protection and privacy laws (such as Rwanda Law No. 058/2021 or equivalent international standards), including appropriate technical and organisational measures for data security.

All interested service providers should submit an Expression of Interest together with the following supporting documents:

Cover letter introducing the company or individual consultant, confirming interest, availability, and understanding of the assignment.

Company profile, including technical capability, qualifications, professional registrations, and relevant geotechnical experience.

CVs of proposed personnel for technical support clearly demonstrating rock engineering/geotechnical engineering numerical modelling proficiency and technical IT support.

Summary of at least three similar software supply contracts undertaken in the last five years, including client name, project scope, and contactable references.

Certificate of domestic company registration issued by RDB.

VAT registration certificate

Valid tax clearance certificate issued by RRA.

Submissions should be forwarded to tender@trinity-metals.com no later than 30 September 2026 at 11:00 AM local time.

Expressions of Interest received after 11:00 AM local time on 30 September 2026 will not be considered.

Shortlisted respondents may be invited for further technical discussions to confirm capability and suitability. Thereafter, Trinity Metals may issue an invitation to tender to selected qualified bidders.

item.title: Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake independent geotechnical reviews tender at Trinity Musha Mines Ltd
item.description:
Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake independent geotechnical reviews Tender at Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake independent geotechnical reviews

Trinity Metals(Trinity Nyakabingo mines ,Trinity Rutongo mines and Trinity Musha mines Limited) invites Expressions of Interest from qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake independent geotechnical reviews across its mining operations. The assignment is intended to provide independent technical assurance, identify geotechnical risks and areas for improvement, and support the continued stability and safety of surface and underground mining infrastructure.

1. Scope of Work

The scope of the independent geotechnical review work includes, but is not limited to, the following:

Conduct visual inspections of surface infrastructure, including slopes and haul roads, and underground workings to identify deterioration, rockfalls, instability, or environmental impacts.

Provide expert guidance and input into existing strategies for the stability of slopes, underground workings, haul roads, and waste rock dumps.

Review and model identified areas of interest specified by the client to improve global geotechnical stability.

Identify gaps, risks, uncertainties, or areas for improvement in the underlying technical work and current geotechnical management practices.

Provide expert guidance on ground support, rock mass characterisation, and the calibration and interpretation of geotechnical monitoring instruments.

Deliver written geotechnical review reports and formal management presentations summarising findings, risks, conclusions, and recommendations.

Provide ad-hoc geotechnical expertise as and when required by the client.

2. Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

Be a qualified Rock Engineer or Geotechnical Engineer with demonstrated competence in hard rock underground mining environments.

Be registered with a recognised professional organisation, such as the International Society for Rock Mechanics and Rock Engineering (ISRM) or a national ISRM-affiliated branch, or an equivalent professional body.

Have a minimum of 10 years demonstrated rock/geotechnical engineering experience in hard rock underground mining, including work on mine infrastructure stability such as road slopes, and waste rock facilities.

Possess a solid track record of working on external consultancy assignments, technical rock engineering audits, numerical modelling, geotechnical peer reviews, or independent geotechnical assurance reviews.

All interested service providers should submit an Expression of Interest together with the following supporting documents:

Cover letter introducing the company or individual consultant, confirming interest, availability, and understanding of the assignment.

Company profile, including technical capability, qualifications, professional registrations, and relevant geotechnical experience.

CVs of proposed personnel clearly demonstrating rock engineering or geotechnical engineering qualifications, professional registration, and relevant experience as stipulated.

Summary of at least three similar assignments undertaken in the last five years, including client name, project scope, location, and contactable references. 

Certificate of domestic company registration issued by RDB.

VAT registration certificate

Valid tax clearance certificate issued by RRA.

Submissions should be forwarded to tender@trinity-metals.com  no later than 30 September 2026 at 11:00 AM local time.

Expressions of Interest received after 11:00 AM local time on 30 September 2026 will not be considered.

Shortlisted respondents may be invited for further technical discussions to confirm capability and suitability. Thereafter, Trinity Metals may issue an invitation to tender to selected qualified bidders.

item.title: The Supply, Support, Maintain and Host the Licensed Software Incontrol Safety Management Module tender at Trinity Musha Mines Ltd
item.description:
The Supply, Support, Maintain and Host the Licensed Software Incontrol Safety Management Module Tender at Trinity Musha Mines Limited

Trinity Metals (Trinity Nyakabingo mines ,Trinity Rutongo mines and Trinity Musha mines Limited) embarked on a journey to become a world class Mining Group with world class mining SHEC standards. We have started the process of developing and implementing a SHEC system which will align our SHEC standards with ISO 45001 and 14001 requirements. To achieve that we need a software system to manage processes required to make the system effective. It is impossible to manage the scope of activities to be performed under ISO requirements manually, or on a paperwork system. The software must provide the ability to manage the following processes with outcomes:

Incident management software

Action Management software

Monitoring software

Document Management software

Audit Management

Compliance Management

Task Scheduling

Inspections outcome Management 

Statistical Data records and analysis

Scope of Work

The scope of the peer review work includes but not limited to the following: 

Can the INXIncontrol software be used to:

Record incidents, hazard observations, and injury events within a centralized solution 

Perform inspections, audits and pre-starts with checklists to keep your workforce accountable and protected 

Assign and track corrective actions to your workforce’s daily practices 

Leverages RCAT methodology 

Reporting and graphing capabilities for data-driven safety insights 

Automatic notifications to enable your workforce to stay on top of their actions and events 

Available on iOS and Android for easy on-the-go reporting 

Manage eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

Have a footprint in Africa

The ability to train users at Trinity Metals mine sites

The ability to provide support on a 24-hour basis

Have international exposure through implementation of their software to ensure they are keeping up with international trends.

All interested parties should submit an Expressions of Interest in accordance with the below requirements complete with supporting documents.

Application Cover Letter introducing your Company/Individual expressing interest, availability, and a brief business and experience profile including qualifications and experience.

Summary of clients using the software.

Details of at least three similar projects undertaken in the last five years.

VAT Registration.

RRA Valid ax clearance certificate

RDB Registration Certificate

Submission to be forwarded to tender@trinity-metals.com  by not later than 30thSeptember 2026 at 11:00AM Local time.

Expressions of Interest received after 11:00AM on 30th September 2026. will unfortunately not be considered.

Further discussion will be undertaken with selected respondents to prove the competence of the bidder and thereafter an invitation to tender will be provided to the bidder.

item.title: Consultancy service to develop a new five-year Strategic Plan covering the period 2027–2031 tender at Sager Ganza Microfinance Plc
item.description:
Consultancy service to develop a new five-year Strategic Plan covering the period 2027–2031

BACKGROUND

Sager Ganza Microfinance PLC (SGM) is a licensed Deposit-Taking Microfinance Institution regulated by the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR). SGM has been operational in Rwanda for the past 20 years, providing financial services to individuals, entrepreneurs, farmers, employees, and small and medium-sized businesses in Rwanda, with a particular focus on serving underserved and low-income communities.

As the current strategic planning period approaches its conclusion, SGM intends to develop a new five-year Strategic Plan covering the period 2027–2031. The Strategic Plan will provide a clear strategic direction for the institution, strengthen its competitiveness and sustainability, and guide management and the Board in achieving SGM's institutional objectives over the next five years.

SGM therefore invites qualified and experienced consulting firms or individual consultants to submit proposals for the provision of consultancy services for the development of its 2027–2031 Strategic Plan.

Published date: 17/09/2026

Deadline for submission: 28/09/2026

N.B: Incomplete and late bids will be rejected.

Interested companies may obtain the official tender documents from our Head Office located at Nyabugogo, Kigali, starting from 18/09/2026 from 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, upon presentation of proof of payment of a non-refundable fee of Fifty Thousand Rwandan Francs (50,000 RWF) to the following bank account:

Only bidders who purchase the tender documents and provide proof of payment will be eligible for participation.

item.title: Accounts Assistant/Manager job at Oasis Holdings Ltd
item.description:
Background

OASIS HOLDINGS LTD, a manufacturer of blow-molded plastic items, is seeking applications from self-motivated and qualified candidates to fill the following position.

Responsibilities

Under direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Accounts Assistant / Manager will perform the specific duties which are as follows:

Ensures invoices, cheque runs are processed in a timely manner.

Record all transactions in the accounting software / ERP in a timely manner.

Responsible to prepare month-end closing, petty cash, and bank reconciliations.

Prepare all documents that are required for the payment of suppliers’ invoices.

Take delivery of documents forwarded to the Accounting Department for payment.

Monthly declaration of all statutory taxes.

Any other assignment or relevant duties in the field of his/her competences as may be assigned by his supervisors.

Any other relevant duties as may reasonably be assigned by the Project Manager or General Manager.

Qualifications and Experience

A minimum Bachelor’s degree in accounting or Finance from a recognized University.

Practical experience of at least 4-10 years in a financial management unit and acquainted with accounting procedures in the private sector or public sector.

Recognized professional accounting qualifications is an advantage.

Working in a Manufacturing company will be an added advantage.

Fluency in English (reading, writing and speaking) is essential.

item.title: Procurement Pharmacist job at King Faisal Hospital
item.description:
King Faisal Hospital Kigali is looking for suitable candidate to fill the following positions

Procurement Pharmacist

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

•He/she must have Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy (BPharm) from a recognized institution with at least 7 years of experience Master’s degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Supply Chain Management with at least 5 years of experience• Registered with a relevant Professional body and having valid license to practice.

SKILLS AND ABILITIES

Good knowledge of pharmaceutical laws, procurement rules, and inventory systems.

Able to deliver services quickly and effectively to meet client needs.

Strong written and spoken communication skills.

Good at analyzing detailed information.

Team player with a positive attitude.

Teaching or management skills are a plus.

Knowledge of health and safety standards is an advantage.

A. Pharmaceutical Procurement Planning

Develop and maintain annual and periodic pharmaceutical procurement plans.

Consolidate pharmaceutical requirements from relevant departments.

Analyse historical consumption, morbidity patterns, stock levels, lead times, and available budgets to forecast requirements.

Participate in the preparation and review of annual procurement plans.

Identify critical and fast-moving medicines requiring close monitoring.

Ensure procurement plans are aligned with the Hospital formulary, essential

medicines requirements, approved budgets, and clinical needs.

Review procurement schedules to minimize emergency purchases

B. Quantification and Forecasting

Conduct regular quantification of medicines, vaccines, medical consumables, and other pharmaceutical products, as applicable.

Use consumption data, stock-on-hand, minimum/maximum stock levels, lead times, and anticipated demand to determine procurement quantities.

Monitor consumption trends and identify unusual variations.

Work with clinical and pharmacy teams to anticipate changes in pharmaceutical demand.

Ensure appropriate safety-stock levels for critical medicines.

C. Procurement Process Management

Initiate and coordinate procurement requisitions for pharmaceutical products.

Prepare accurate technical specifications for medicines and pharmaceutical supplies.

Develop or review Bills of Quantities, schedules of requirements, and other technical procurement documents.

Participate in preparation and review of requests for quotations, tender documents, purchase orders, and contracts.

Participate in technical evaluation of bids for pharmaceutical products.

Provide professional pharmaceutical input during bid evaluation while maintaining impartiality and confidentiality.

Ensure procurement processes follow approved procedures and authorization levels.

Coordinate with the Procurement Unit to monitor the progress of procurement processes from requisition to delivery.

D. Supplier and Vendor Management

Identify and assess potential pharmaceutical suppliers in collaboration with the Procurement Unit.

Verify supplier eligibility, licensing, product registration, and other relevant regulatory requirements.

Participate in supplier prequalification and evaluation.

Monitor supplier performance against contractual requirements.

Track delivery lead times, product quality, quantities delivered, documentation, and responsiveness.

A. Pharmaceutical Procurement Planning

  • Develop and maintain annual and periodic pharmaceutical procurement plans.
  • Consolidate pharmaceutical requirements from relevant departments.
  • Analyse historical consumption, morbidity patterns, stock levels, lead times, and available budgets to forecast requirements.
  • Participate in the preparation and review of annual procurement plans.
  • Identify critical and fast-moving medicines requiring close monitoring.
  • Ensure procurement plans are aligned with the Hospital formulary, essential
  • medicines requirements, approved budgets, and clinical needs.
  • Review procurement schedules to minimize emergency purchases

B. Quantification and Forecasting

  • Conduct regular quantification of medicines, vaccines, medical consumables, and other pharmaceutical products, as applicable.
  • Use consumption data, stock-on-hand, minimum/maximum stock levels, lead times, and anticipated demand to determine procurement quantities.
  • Monitor consumption trends and identify unusual variations.
  • Work with clinical and pharmacy teams to anticipate changes in pharmaceutical demand.
  • Ensure appropriate safety-stock levels for critical medicines.

C. Procurement Process Management

  • Initiate and coordinate procurement requisitions for pharmaceutical products.
  • Prepare accurate technical specifications for medicines and pharmaceutical supplies.
  • Develop or review Bills of Quantities, schedules of requirements, and other technical procurement documents.
  • Participate in preparation and review of requests for quotations, tender documents, purchase orders, and contracts.
  • Participate in technical evaluation of bids for pharmaceutical products.
  • Provide professional pharmaceutical input during bid evaluation while maintaining impartiality and confidentiality.
  • Ensure procurement processes follow approved procedures and authorization levels.
  • Coordinate with the Procurement Unit to monitor the progress of procurement processes from requisition to delivery.

D. Supplier and Vendor Management

  • Identify and assess potential pharmaceutical suppliers in collaboration with the Procurement Unit.
  • Verify supplier eligibility, licensing, product registration, and other relevant regulatory requirements.
  • Participate in supplier prequalification and evaluation.
  • Monitor supplier performance against contractual requirements.
  • Track delivery lead times, product quality, quantities delivered, documentation, and responsiveness.

item.title: Customer Care Officer job at King Faisal Hospital
item.description:
King Faisal Hospital Kigali is looking for suitable candidate to fill the following positions

Responsibilities or duties

Retrieval of all patient records in advance of the booked appointment

Filing to be completed daily

Appointments to be noted either in the appointment book or on a database if used

Clinical staff appraised daily of the appointment list for their clinic/ surgery

Patients requiring Blood investigations, X-rays, and removal of Plaster of Paris are requested to come in earlier to have these completed before the appointment

Constant contact maintained with patients, receptionist and Clinical staff to ensure smooth flow through the Department and to be able to warn the patient if there are anticipated delays

A database of complaints maintained in order to identify bottlenecks or other problems so that these issues can be addressed

Awareness of the functioning of the hospital, transport networks, Pharmacy Policy, and Procedures

Awareness of the Policies and Procedures governing the Out-Patient and Emergency Medical Departments

To ensure that Results of all waiting times surveys analyzed and reported to the customer care Manager

Wheelchairs are cleaned and the footrests are in place

Adherence to all Health and Safety Policies and Procedures

Compliance with Infection Prevention and Control Policies and Procedures maintained

Ensure that directions for patients are adequate and maintained: for example, colored lines/stripes/ painted footsteps for patients to follow to different wards areas

Patient and personnel fire and emergency evacuations practiced annually

Monitor all exits for obstacles, boxes, and vehicles blocking the free flow of people exiting that area

Qualifications or requirements 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

He/she must have Minimum a Diploma in Hospitality Management or any related field

SKILLS AND ABILITIES

Deep knowledge of work processes and/or procedures such as daily patient care tasks, planning, and organization

Basic computer knowledge.

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal skills.

Disposition, tact, courtesy, enthusiasm, cooperation, and sincerity as they affect fellow workers and others.

Makes clients and their needs a primary focus of work and actions. This includes clients that are both internal and external to the Hospital.

Gives out information and ideas clearly and concisely, including the requirement to inform and persuade.

Experience needed

A minimum of two (2) years’ experience in Hospitality Management Preferably in the hospital settings

item.title: Customer Care Officer (branch and outlet) job at Intsinzi SACCO Rulindo (ISR)
item.description:
Intsinzi SACCO Rulindo is seeking a Customer Care Officer.

Responsibilities or duties

To work diligently on the assigned work on time and to produce results.

To comply with the instructions of the employer or his/her representative.

To take good care of and manage the equipment assigned to him/her in his/her work.

To be at work and respect working days and hours.

To maintain the confidentiality of work.

To provide basic identification documents before starting work.

To follow the principles and codes of conduct governing the business activities of the Cooperative.

Welcomes members/customers, provides advice and recommendation where to find the right contact person.

Handles complaints professionally and provides a courteous approach to resolving complaints.

Files documents of the SACCO, e.g., member documents.

Initiates and updates all documents related to members information (e.g., electronic customer file, membership applications, authorizations, customer notes).

To provide good and efficient service to customers.

To follow up on customer complaints that have been referred to other appropriate authorities.

Assist in resolving daily customer issues and ensure that they are timely responded in accordance with established customer service policies and regulations.

Maintain knowledge of all products and services offered by the Cooperative and provide information on the Cooperative's products and activities to members and customers in general.

Receive and assist members and customers in general who require services related to deposits and withdrawals and ensure the security of related documents.

Ensure that the information recorded in the member's passbook matches with his/her account in the electronic system.

Collect and report on unresolved customer complaints or issues and requests for follow-up, documentation and submission to the relevant authority for consideration.

Assist in the implementation of the Cooperative's policies, procedures and guidelines for customer care.

Participate in the implementation of the customer care policy and in particular the protection of financial services consumers.

Inform and explain to members and customers information regarding the contents of their accounts.

Assist customers in completing any documents that may be required.

Conduct Customer Satisfaction Surveys in accordance with the relevant regulations.

Open new accounts and ensure that their documents are submitted to the relevant department or employee for approval.

Maintain good relations with all customers, focusing on changes and new needs in the Cooperative.

Issue bank statements to members and customers after payment of the required fees.

To provide advice to members and clients in general by teaching them how to invest and maintain a culture of saving.

To perform other duties that do not conflict with the laws and regulations required by the supervisor or his/her superior authority.

Qualifications or requirements 

At least secondary education (A2) in related domain.

Excellent service orientation and attention to details regarding the atmosphere in the SACCO.

Good communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking skills and be able to function under pressure.

Excellent negotiation skills and be able to influence people.

Must be patient and willing to help others in solving problems while maintaining a positive attitude at all times.

Experience needed

Two years’ experience in customer care services.

item.title: Internal Auditor job at Intsinzi SACCO Rulindo (ISR)
item.description:
Responsibilities & Tasks

To work diligently on the assigned work on time and to produce results.

To comply with the instructions of the employer or his/her representative.

To comply with the laws, regulations and decisions of the Cooperative.

To take good care of and manage the equipment assigned to him/her in his/her work.

To be at work and to respect working days and hours.

To maintain confidentiality of work.

To provide basic identification documents before starting work.

To follow the principles and rules governing the conduct of the Cooperative's business activities.

To prepare a monthly, quarterly and annual audit plan based on activities that appear to be likely to cause damage or waste the Cooperative's assets.

Ensure that internal audit guidelines and principles are properly followed to prevent errors or possible malpractices.

Report any shortcomings in the daily operations of the department with a view to preventing theft, embezzlement and misuse of funds.

Establish a table of issues identified by the audit, recommendations made by the audit and the methods for their implementation.

Review whether the internal audit system is working properly, identifying strengths and areas for improvement, and providing recommendations for action.

Review whether the accounting has been carried out in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), the regulations of the Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR), and that the information contained is complete and reliable to assist in making informed decisions.

Verify whether all activities of the Cooperative comply with applicable laws and regulations.

Analyze the efficient and effective use of the Cooperative's resources to achieve its objectives.

Monitor and analyze the causes of problems in order to determine methods and strategies to solve and prevent them.

Maintain proper records and audit evidence.

Conduct a special audit of the funds on hand and verify how these funds are used and authorized, to ensure that no errors are made.

Verify that shares, deposits, loan payments, and interests are correctly recorded in the Cooperative's IT system and ensure that they are properly processed.

Review whether loan files are completed as required by the loan policy, the loan disbursement and repayment procedures, and ensure that loan and interest payments are properly processed.

Review and confirm that all outstanding debts have been recovered as planned.

Prepare periodic reports on internal audits, showing whether the operating procedures and regulations are being followed.

Review the bank statements and corresponding documents and verify that the Cooperative's assets are properly protected.

Monitor the implementation of the resolutions of the meetings issued by the competent authorities.

Provide advice on all irregularities and submit them to the relevant authority.

Submit internal audit plans and reports to the supervisor.

Supervise the work carried out by other employees.

Supervise the implementation of the strategic & business plans, action plan and budget.

Timely prevent and disclose any conflicts of interest or lack of segregation of duties.

Perform other duties that are not contrary to the laws and regulations required by the supervisor, employer or superior body.

Qualification Criteria / Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance.

Three (3) years of experience in auditing, and a thorough understanding of Microfinance Banking and accounting practices.

Good strategic thinking, with risk and control consciousness.

Strong analytic skills.

Professional qualification in auditing is an added value.

High attention to detail and excellent analytical skills.

Excellent communication skills.

Professionalism and integrity.

Proven knowledge of auditing standards and procedures, laws, rules and regulations. Advanced computer skills on MS Office and Core Banking Software.

item.title: Relationship Officers job at Umutanguha Finance Company
item.location: Opposite Nyamirambo Pele Stadium, House # 177, KN2 Avenue | Kigali | Kigali
item.description:
UMUTANGUHA Finance Company (UFC) Plc, a company duly registered in the office of the Registrar General under company code number 101310843, licensed by National Bank of Rwanda to operate as Micro Finance Institution in Rwanda headquartered in Kigali, Opposite Nyamirambo Pele Stadium, House # 177, KN2 Avenue, P.O Box 2998 Kigali, Tel 0788387730, email: info@ufinance.co.rw is recruiting self-motivated, creative, persuasive individuals with excellent communication and sales skills to fill the positions of Relationship Officers with the following duties and responsibilities:

Responsibilities or duties,

A. Responsibilities with regard to saving mobilization

The Relationship Officer “RO” is responsible for the growth of deposit volume at branch level by mobilizing accounts and savings from field (from current and potential clients). The RO will be responsible for the development of the relationship between clients and UFC. His/her specific tasks are to:

Generate & develop deposits and new deposit pipeline by providing product knowledge, customer services and managing customer relationships

Sell the Deposits products to the existing and potential clients

Enhance and establish relationship with existing & perspective customers in the segment by visiting/talking to clients on a daily basis

Solicit new business from present and prospective customers; maintains ongoing business relationships with present customers in order to take advantage of additional cross-selling opportunities.

Involve in savings promotion activities according to specificities of areas.

Follow up and make sure that the accounts activated by his/her promotion are actively used by the customers.

Manage the High Network Individuals customer portfolio for the branch.

Ensure establishment and maintenance of the strong rapport with the clients

Achieve all business targets within allocated time

B. Responsibilities with regard to credit

The RO is responsible of the quality loan portfolio and its growth at the assigned branch with the following duties:

Mobilize clients for the purpose of lending to them.

Train individual clients and group members in the UFC lending methodology

Supervise financial education trainings conducted by clients’ trainer

Guide, monitor, and supervise clients as well as groups activities

Evaluate and assess the credit risk of individual clients and groups by inspecting business and household of potential clients, appraise client’s business and repayment capability before disbursing loans.

Generate and submit on time accurate documentation to enable loans to be disbursed.

Maintain complete and accurate loan documentation in the office and supervise the maintenance of group record keeping process.

Follow up with clients to recover loans.

Participate and/or hold cluster meetings.

Take individual action as per policy to recover delinquent loans

Prepare and submit reports on the number of clients, repayments, portfolio quality, loan recoveries and follow-up action on delinquent loans.

Prepare and submit reports on the number of clients, repayments, portfolio quality, loan recoveries and follow-up action on delinquent loans.

C. Sell of all financial products, services and delivery channels

Develop marketing and work plan for the establishment of solid clientele base.

Identify and sensitize the potential clients in the respective area of operation.

Advise clients on the use of UFC PLC Alternative delivery channels

Refer clients that are illegible for other UFC PLC products to the respective departments

Main Performance Measures

Portfolio at risk (PAR)

Value of outstanding portfolio (Average portfolio)

Number of loan clients

Growth in the number of loan clients

Growth in the value of outstanding portfolio

Growth of the saving portfolio

Number of saving clients

Client relationship

Ensure a perfect, good and quality customer service

Compliance with Client Protection Principles

Safeguard the good reputation of UMUTANGUHA FINANCE COMPANY PLC

Any other task assigned by the line supervisor.

Qualifications or requirements (e.g., education, skills),

Bachelor’s degree in economics, Management, Finance and Banking and related fields

Experience needed,

At least 3 years’ experience in banking or micro finance sector preferably in Business or Credit sections;

Any other provided details (e.g., benefits, work environment, team info, or additional notes).

Excellent understanding of the bank operations and credit functionalities

Negotiation and strong analytical skills

Excellent sales skills and strong credit analysis and loan portfolio management;

Excellent and effective communication skills, both orally and in writing

Able to work in any UFC Plc Branches located in all provinces in Rwanda

Having a driving license Category A will be an added value;

Maximum age 38 years’ old

Manage the High Network Individuals customer portfolio for the branch.

Ensure establishment and maintenance of the strong rapport with the clients

Achieve all business targets within allocated time

Mobilize clients for the purpose of lending to them.

Train individual clients and group members in the UFC lending methodology

Supervise financial education trainings conducted by clients’ trainer

Guide, monitor, and supervise clients as well as groups activities

Evaluate and assess the credit risk of individual clients and groups by inspecting business and household of potential clients, appraise client’s business and repayment capability before disbursing loans.

Generate and submit on time accurate documentation to enable loans to be disbursed.

Maintain complete and accurate loan documentation in the office and supervise the maintenance of group record keeping process.

Follow up with clients to recover loans.

Participate and/or hold cluster meetings.

Take individual action as per policy to recover delinquent loans

Prepare and submit reports on the number of clients, repayments, portfolio quality, loan recoveries and follow-up action on delinquent loans.

Prepare and submit reports on the number of clients, repayments, portfolio quality, loan recoveries and follow-up action on delinquent loans.

Develop marketing and work plan for the establishment of solid clientele base.

Identify and sensitize the potential clients in the respective area of operation.

Advise clients on the use of UFC PLC Alternative delivery channels

Refer clients that are illegible for other UFC PLC products to the respective departments

Portfolio at risk (PAR)

Value of outstanding portfolio (Average portfolio)

Number of loan clients

Growth in the number of loan clients

Growth in the value of outstanding portfolio

Growth of the saving portfolio

Number of saving clients

Client relationship

Ensure a perfect, good and quality customer service

Compliance with Client Protection Principles

Safeguard the good reputation of UMUTANGUHA FINANCE COMPANY PLC

Any other task assigned by the line supervisor.

Qualifications or requirements (e.g., education, skills),

Bachelor’s degree in economics, Management, Finance and Banking and related fields

Experience needed,

At least 3 years’ experience in banking or micro finance sector preferably in Business or Credit sections;

Any other provided details (e.g., benefits, work environment, team info, or additional notes).

Excellent understanding of the bank operations and credit functionalities

Negotiation and strong analytical skills

Excellent sales skills and strong credit analysis and loan portfolio management;

Excellent and effective communication skills, both orally and in writing

Able to work in any UFC Plc Branches located in all provinces in Rwanda

Having a driving license Category A will be an added value;

Maximum age 38 years’ old
