item.title: Accountant/PSAC Project job at National Agricultural Export Development Board
item.company: The National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB
item.description_html:
The National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB) would like to recruit self-motivated and qualified candidates to fill the following position.

Responsibilities or duties

Under direct supervision of the Chief Finance Officer with the daily supervision of the SPIU Coordinator, the accountant will perform the specific duties which are as follows:

  • Ensure all PSAC financial transactions are accurately approved and adequately supported according to IFAD and GOR Financial Management policies and for project and grant purpose in accordance with relevant PSAC financing agreement;
  • Ensures invoices, cheque runs are processed in timely manner;
  • Record all project and grant transaction into IFMIS accounting software in timely manner;
  • Responsible to prepare month ends closing, petty cash and bank reconciliations;
  • Monitor and track the use of project and grant assets, and report back to the chief accountants, the CFO and the coordinator of SPIU;
  • Assist with the preparation of withdrawal application for replenishment/direct payment, etc;
  • Assist with the preparation of the Interim unaudited financial report and other reports as required for the project and grant;
  • Capture in the books and file all supporting documents of expenditures paid from the petty cash;
  • Prepare all documents that are required for the payment of suppliers’ invoices duly approved by his supervisors;
  • Take delivery of documents forwarded to the Accounting Department for payment;
  • Monthly declaration of withholding tax deducted from suppliers’ invoices;
  • Any other assignment or relevant duties in the field of his/her competences as may be assigned by his supervisors.
  • Verification of supplier’s invoices for payment;
  • Timely posting of all project accounting vouchers on the accounting software;
  • Exercise proper custody of all posted vouchers and other accounting documents;
  • Verification and checking of bank statements and accounting software printouts;
  • Supervise and direct the accounting and logistical functions, to ensure efficiency;
  • Preparation and submission of periodical financial reports on deadlines;
  • Preparation of Withdrawal Applications;
  • Regular spot check of petty cash fund and other reconciliation reports;
  • Timely replenishment of operation account with project bank account;
  • Authorization of payments vouchers;
  • Facilitate financial audits and implementation support missions;
  • Regular follow up of smooth functioning of the accounting software, and make contact with ICT staff and software suppliers;
  • Submission of account printouts by components to the heads of components for analysis and comments;
  • Give advice to management on accounting and administration matters;
  • Liaise with bankers for bank matters;
  • Any other relevant duties as may reasonably be assigned by the Chief Finance Officer.

Qualifications or requirements

  • A minimum Bachelor’s degree in accounting or Finance from a recognized University;
  • Should be part of ACCA or CPA;
  • Recognized professional accounting qualifications is an advantage;
  • Adequate knowledge of basic accounting procedures and policies;
  • Adequate knowledge in generating financial statements;
  • Proficiency in accounting software;
  • good knowledge of computer applications in accounting
  • Good analytical financial skills;
  • Communicate effectively orally and in writing;
  • Team work spirit;
  • A Fluency in English or French (reading, writing and speaking) with a very good knowledge of the second language (French or English)

Experience needed

Practical experience of at least 5 years in a financial management unit and acquainted with accounting procedures in the public administration sector in or with internationally recognized financial institutions;

Previous experience with IFAD procedures and financial regulations would be an added advantage;

item.location: KN2 Avenue, Building No. 177-in front of Kigali Pele stadium; 2nd floor | Kigali | Kigali
item.description_html:
Background

UMUTANGUHA FINANCE COMPANY PLC (UFC Plc) in acronyms, a company incorporated in Rwanda under TIN:101310843; exercising the micro finance business activities under the License of the Central Bank (BNR); B. P :2998 KIGALI; having its registered office in the City of Kigali, District of Nyarugenge, Sector Nyamirambo; KN2 Avenue, Building No. 177-in front of Kigali Pele stadium; 2nd floor, Tel: +250-788387730,Email:info@ufinance.co.rw wishes to externally recruit focused, results-oriented and suitably qualified professionals to fill the following position:

Responsibilities

  • Draft and review loan contracts, ensuring all loan files are legally compliant before disbursement;
  • Draft, review, and negotiate contracts and other key documents, assessing their legal implications and advising UFC PLC accordingly;
  • Prepare, review, and amend contractual instruments to facilitate and support various business activities;
  • Enhance understanding of legal risks and obligations through training, communication, and advice, ensuring that staff are well-informed of relevant legal requirements;
  • Collaborate with concerned departments to identify legal risks and implement appropriate mitigation strategies;
  • Oversee the progress of ongoing litigation and manage relationships with external Lawyers;
  • Collaborate with Professional Court Bailiff in the execution of Court Cases and other related legal correspondences and make sure that they are executed successfully;
  • Provide timely and practical legal opinions to guide decision-making processes in compliance with existing laws and regulations;
  • Review ongoing legal cases and offer strategic advice to safeguard the interests of UFC PLC;
  • Ensure adherence to legal compliance within internal policies and procedures;
  • Monitor and ensure compliance with microfinance regulations governing the operations of UFC PLC;
  • Handle correspondence with clients, regulatory bodies, and law enforcement, ensuring appropriate responses;
  • Collaborate with various departments within UFC PLC to provide legal support and guidance as needed.
  • Promptly identify and advise on conflicts of interest in alignment with UFC PLC policies and the Code of Conduct.
  • Maintain all corporate records and documenting all corporate decisions;
  • Collect all documents for drawdown on credit facility to ensure that the institution’s interest is adequately protected and conditions precedent met before disbursement.
  • Provide legal advice to HR and Administration and to make sure about the compliance of Labor Laws and other related regulations
  • Prepare and Maintain Litigation Schedule in collaboration with External Lawyers
  • Verify and confirm letters of administration and other related correspondence of UFC PLC
  • Attend matters in court on behalf of the UFC PLC
  • Provide legal advice on litigation issues
  • Maintain accurate records of all legal documents and precedents related to UFC PLC's activities;
  • Ensure proper documentation and filing of contracts and other legal documentation used in financial services provision;
  • Ensure that all court cases of UFC PLC are well organized; executed successfully and available at any time;
  • Any other related duties assigned by the supervisor

Qualifications, Skills and Experience

The candidate should hold a Bachelor's degree in Law or related field;

  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant legal experience in the banking, microfinance sector or law firm;
  • Prior experience in providing legal counsel and ensuring compliance within a financial institution;
  • Deep understanding of relevant laws and regulations, with strong drafting and negotiation skills;
  • Ability to juggle multiple tasks while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment;
  • Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management abilities;
  • High level of integrity and ability to handle confidential matters;
  • Knowledge of IECMS (Integrated Electronic Case Management System) for following up on Court Cases of UFC PLC;
  • Fluency in English, French, and Kinyarwanda, both written and spoken.

Duties include customer reception and assistance, complaint handling and follow-up, member records, account opening support, customer information, statements, customer satisfaction surveys, product information and consumer support.

item.title: Front Office Officer job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
item.description:
Context of the position: 

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Front Office Officer, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.

JOB PURPOSE

The main role for this position is to provide professional, efficient, and welcoming front-office and administrative support by managing the reception area, receiving and directing visitors and calls, handling correspondence, and providing timely assistance to staff and external stakeholders. The Front Office Officer ensures effective communication and smooth day-to-day front-office operations while maintaining a professional image of the organization and safeguarding confidential information.

Main clients: 

All SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda staff and departments

All visitors, guests, and members of the public coming to SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda

Children, young people, families, and other programme participants visiting the organization

Government institutions, partners, donors, service providers, and other external stakeholders

Candidates, consultants, and other individuals visiting SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda for official purposes

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities: 

The Front Office Officer is responsible for managing the reception area and serving as the first point of contact for visitors, staff, partners, and other stakeholders. The position ensures professional handling of telephone calls, correspondence, visitors, and general inquiries while providing timely administrative support. The officer maintains accurate front-office records, ensures compliance with safeguarding, confidentiality, and security procedures, and contributes to creating a welcoming and professional image of SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda. Below are the details:

Reception and Customer Service

Receive and welcome all visitors, guests, and stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner.

Identify visitors and direct them to the appropriate staff members or departments.

Ensure that visitors receive timely and accurate information and assistance.

Maintain a professional, clean, and welcoming reception environment.

Handle inquiries and provide appropriate responses or referrals.

Telephone and Communication Management

Receive and manage incoming telephone calls and direct them to the appropriate staff members.

Take and relay messages accurately and promptly.

Manage general front-office email inquiries and ensure that correspondence is directed to the relevant departments.

Support effective communication between staff, visitors, and external stakeholders.

Visitor and Front Office Administration

Maintain accurate records of visitors, appointments, deliveries, and other front-office activities.

Manage visitor access in accordance with organizational security and safeguarding procedures.

Coordinate appointments and meeting arrangements as required.

Receive and distribute incoming correspondence, documents, and deliveries.

Maintain an organized filing system for front-office records.

Administrative Support

Provide general administrative support to the Administration and other departments as assigned.

Support the preparation and coordination of meetings, events, and official visits.

Assist with photocopying, scanning, printing, document distribution, and other routine administrative tasks.

Support the coordination of office supplies and other front-office requirements.

Safeguarding, Confidentiality and Security

Ensure that all visitors and stakeholders are treated in accordance with SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda's safeguarding standards and procedures.

Maintain confidentiality of organizational, staff, visitor, and programme-related information.

Immediately report any safeguarding, security, or other concerns through the appropriate channels.

Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and health and safety requirements.

Professional Representation

Serve as the first point of contact for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and promote a professional and positive image of the organization.

Maintain professional conduct and demonstrate respect, integrity, and courtesy in all interactions.

Build positive working relationships with staff, visitors, partners, government representatives, and other stakeholders.

Reporting and Other Responsibilities

Prepare routine front-office reports and maintain relevant records as required.

Monitor and report issues affecting the smooth operation of the reception area.

Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the supervisor.

Child Protection Policy

At all times, avoid actions or behaviour that could be construed as poor or potentially abusive practice. 

Report any child safeguarding concerns immediately in accordance with the organizational’s Child Protection Policy

Promote and uphold the organisation’s values and child safeguarding principles in all interactions and decision – making 

Data Protection Policy.

At all times ensure that personal data of SOS Children’s Villages beneficiaries and their families as well as SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda co-workers is handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing SOS Children’s Villages.

Ensure that personal sponsor information and data used and administered for the benefit of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda, is stored and transferred securely, handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing data protection laws. Donor data will remain under the control of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda and shall not be forwarded to or swapped with other organizations.

Required key skills set.

Must have the following:

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Strong customer service and reception skills

Good organizational and time-management skills

Professional, courteous, and welcoming attitude

Good telephone and email communication skills

Attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records

Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information

Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications

Ability to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds

Problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure

Formal qualifications 

Education: Diploma in Front Office Management, Business Admin, or related field

Professional Qualification: Customer Service certification preferred

Experience requirements 

Experience: 3+ years reception/front office experience; corporate environment

Skills & Competencies: Reception Management, Telephone Etiquette, Visitor Management, Mail Handling, Office Administration, Professional Presentation, Customer Service Orientation, English & Kinyarwanda fluency.

JOB PURPOSE

The main role for this position is to provide professional, efficient, and welcoming front-office and administrative support by managing the reception area, receiving and directing visitors and calls, handling correspondence, and providing timely assistance to staff and external stakeholders. The Front Office Officer ensures effective communication and smooth day-to-day front-office operations while maintaining a professional image of the organization and safeguarding confidential information.

Main clients:

  • All SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda staff and departments
  • All visitors, guests, and members of the public coming to SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
  • Children, young people, families, and other programme participants visiting the organization
  • Government institutions, partners, donors, service providers, and other external stakeholders
  • Candidates, consultants, and other individuals visiting SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda for official purposes

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:

The Front Office Officer is responsible for managing the reception area and serving as the first point of contact for visitors, staff, partners, and other stakeholders. The position ensures professional handling of telephone calls, correspondence, visitors, and general inquiries while providing timely administrative support. The officer maintains accurate front-office records, ensures compliance with safeguarding, confidentiality, and security procedures, and contributes to creating a welcoming and professional image of SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda. Below are the details:

Reception and Customer Service

  • Receive and welcome all visitors, guests, and stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner.
  • Identify visitors and direct them to the appropriate staff members or departments.
  • Ensure that visitors receive timely and accurate information and assistance.
  • Maintain a professional, clean, and welcoming reception environment.
  • Handle inquiries and provide appropriate responses or referrals.

Telephone and Communication Management

  • Receive and manage incoming telephone calls and direct them to the appropriate staff members.
  • Take and relay messages accurately and promptly.
  • Manage general front-office email inquiries and ensure that correspondence is directed to the relevant departments.
  • Support effective communication between staff, visitors, and external stakeholders.

Visitor and Front Office Administration

  • Maintain accurate records of visitors, appointments, deliveries, and other front-office activities.
  • Manage visitor access in accordance with organizational security and safeguarding procedures.
  • Coordinate appointments and meeting arrangements as required.
  • Receive and distribute incoming correspondence, documents, and deliveries.
  • Maintain an organized filing system for front-office records.

Administrative Support

  • Provide general administrative support to the Administration and other departments as assigned.
  • Support the preparation and coordination of meetings, events, and official visits.
  • Assist with photocopying, scanning, printing, document distribution, and other routine administrative tasks.
  • Support the coordination of office supplies and other front-office requirements.

Safeguarding, Confidentiality and Security

  • Ensure that all visitors and stakeholders are treated in accordance with SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda's safeguarding standards and procedures.
  • Maintain confidentiality of organizational, staff, visitor, and programme-related information.
  • Immediately report any safeguarding, security, or other concerns through the appropriate channels.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and health and safety requirements.

Professional Representation

  • Serve as the first point of contact for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and promote a professional and positive image of the organization.
  • Maintain professional conduct and demonstrate respect, integrity, and courtesy in all interactions.
  • Build positive working relationships with staff, visitors, partners, government representatives, and other stakeholders.

  • Monitor and report issues affecting the smooth operation of the reception area.

  • Professional, courteous, and welcoming attitude
  • Good telephone and email communication skills
  • Attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information
  • Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications
  • Ability to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure

Formal qualifications

Education: Diploma in Front Office Management, Business Admin, or related field

Professional Qualification: Customer Service certification preferred

Experience requirements

Experience: 3+ years reception/front office experience; corporate environment

Skills & Competencies: Reception Management, Telephone Etiquette, Visitor Management, Mail Handling, Office Administration, Professional Presentation, Customer Service Orientation, English & Kinyarwanda fluency.

item.title: Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
item.description:
Context of the position: 

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.

JOB PURPOSE

To move ICT from 'fixing laptops' to 'leveraging technology' for social impact. The Senior Manager, ICT and Programmes Digitalisation leads SOS Rwanda's ICT function and drives the organisation's digital transformation agenda, designing and implementing ICT strategy, managing all ICT systems and infrastructure, leading the digitalisation of programme and operational workflows, implementing secure digital case management platforms, ensuring cybersecurity and data protection, and building staff digital literacy across all four Program Areas.

The position is the functional supervisor of the ICT Administrator in Kigali and provides technical oversight to location-level ICT focal points.

Main clients: 

Deputy National Director for Operations

National Director

All National Management Team (NMT) members

Head of Finance — ERP and financial systems

Head of MEAL — digital MEL platforms

Head of HROD — HRIS systems

Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics — procurement systems

Programme teams across all four area offices

SOS Regional ICT Advisor (ESAF) and SOS International ICT teams

ICT Administrator- Kigali (direct report)

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities: 

ICT Strategy and Governance

Develop, implement, and update SOS Rwanda's ICT strategy — aligned with SOS Strategy 2030, MA Strategic Plan 2023–2027, and global SOS ICT standards.

Define national ICT budgets, procurement plans, and multi-year ICT investment roadmaps.

Develop and implement ICT policies and standards — covering architecture, security, disaster recovery, procurement, and service provision.

Participate in regional ICT knowledge-sharing processes and coordinate with the SOS ESAF ICT Advisor on global standards and initiatives.

Lead ICT governance — including vendor management, service level agreements, and ICT committee oversight.

Programmes Digitalisation & Digital Case Management

Implement and manage a secure, cloud-based digital case management platform for tracking child progress — ensuring data privacy and compliance with Rwanda data protection laws and SOS-KDI data protection rules.

Lead the digitalisation of SOS Rwanda's programme functions — introducing digital case management, beneficiary tracking, and electronic documentation workflows across all four locations.

Equip field staff with mobile tools for real-time community reporting — reducing the 'paperwork lag' and improving data quality.

Drive paperless operations across all locations — designing change management plans that support staff adoption of new digital tools.

Collaborate with the Director of Strategy and Programme Implementation and the MEAL function to align digitalisation initiatives with programme quality and RBM needs.

Explore, evaluate, and pilot AI adoption and knowledge management tools that enhance programme decision-making and organisational efficiency.

ERP, HRIS and Operational Systems

Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of SOS Rwanda's ERP system — ensuring integration across finance, procurement, HR, and programme functions.

Manage the HRIS system — ensuring data integrity, user access management, and alignment with HR processes.

Lead the digitisation of procurement and supply chain systems in coordination with the Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics.

Ensure all ICT systems are properly integrated, reducing data silos and enabling organisation-wide reporting and analytics.

Infrastructure, Cybersecurity and Business Continuity

Manage SOS Rwanda's IT network and server infrastructure across all locations — ensuring 99%+ system uptime, reliability, performance, and cost-effectiveness.

Develop and implement a comprehensive cybersecurity framework — including data protection, access control, threat monitoring, and incident response — ensuring the cybersecurity audit score meets SOS-KDI standards.

Ensure compliance with SOS-KDI data protection rules and Rwanda data protection regulations, including the privacy of child and family records.

Design and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans — ensuring operational resilience in the event of system failures.

Digital Literacy & Capacity Building

Build digital literacy across SOS Rwanda — designing and delivering ICT training programmes for staff at all levels and locations.

Supervise the ICT Administrator and provide technical oversight to location ICT focal points.

Coach programme and operations staff on effective use of digital tools for monitoring, reporting, and case management.

Train community partners and staff on using technology for education, health monitoring, and economic strengthening.

Formal qualifications and Experiencerequirements: 

Education & Professional Qualifications

Master’s or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or related field (Master's preferred for Grade 5).

ITIL, PMP, or relevant technical certifications required (Grade 5 requirement).

Cybersecurity certification (CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or equivalent) is a strong advantage.

Professional Experience

Minimum of 7 years of progressive ICT experience; 3+ years in senior ICT leadership or digital transformation role.

Demonstrated experience leading digital transformation initiatives in an INGO, NGO, or complex multi-site organisation.

Proven experience with ERP systems (SOS ERP, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, or equivalent) and HRIS platforms.

Strong track record in cybersecurity management, data protection, and ICT governance.

Experience with ICT4D tools — digital case management, mobile data collection, cloud platforms.

Experience working across multiple sites and geographically dispersed teams.

Skills & Competencies

Digital Transformation Strategy and Programme Digitisation.

ICT Infrastructure Management and Systems Architecture.

Data Governance and Cybersecurity.

ERP Systems Management and Integration.

Vendor Management and contract administration.

Strong change management and adult learning facilitation skills.

Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.

Good understanding of programme monitoring, MEAL, and data analytics.

Fluent English; Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage.

Commitment to SOS values and ethical use of data and technology in child-related programmes.

item.title: Institutional Partnership Development Specialist job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
item.description:
Context of the position: 

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Institutional Partnership Development Specialist, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.

JOB PURPOSE

The Institutional Partnership Development Specialist mobilizes institutional funding for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and is a key contributor to the growth of the IPD funding portfolio and day to day donor relationship management with bilateral donors, international donors, embassies, diplomatic missions, foundations to significantly increase the financial resources for national programs. This role involves developing and implementing institutional partnership plans, developing funding proposals to expand the organization’s programs and contributing to donor compliance.

Main clients: 

Internal – National Director, Deputy National Director – Operations, Director of Program Quality, Safeguarding and Partnership Development, Head of Fund Development and Partnerships, Program Managers, Project teams, finance team, and PSA staff

External – Institutional Donors, Implementing partners, Government, NGOs, Embassies, Diplomatic Missions, Foundations

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:

Fundraising and Donor Liaison

Develop and implement annual IPD plans in line with the national organizational strategy annual set targets.

Ensure IPD annual targets are met according to the national organizational strategy.

Identify monthly IPD funding opportunities from in-country, bilateral, multilateral, international donors, embassies, diplomatic missions and foundations to meet annual targets.

Develop and write program ideas, concept notes, expression of interests, grant applications, technical project proposals for IPD projects while ensuring they are provisioned with available information prior to involving additional teams.

Conduct comprehensive background research on relevant policies, political, economic, environmental factors, and existing strategies at national, sub-national, regional, and global levels to contextualize project proposal descriptions.

Develop different project proposal sections, including risk factors, mitigation measures, sustainable development impacts, paradigm shifts, result frameworks, impact matrices, problem and objective trees, stakeholder analyses and others.

Ensure the timely collection of content needed from program teams for high quality and competitive proposal development.

Facilitate the development of project proposals and organize proposal development workshops with program team, partners and/or stakeholders, serving as the focal point for coordination and logistics.

Together with the Head of Fund Development and Partnership and program team identify suitable lead applications, co-applicants and implementing partners to increase competitiveness in bid applications.

Donor Compliance Monitoring 

Regularly update the master partner landscape and partner mapping to reflect current information.

Update IPD project grant compliance matrices to ensure adherence to donor requirements.

Ensure that project one-pagers and program summaries are always current and accurate.

Maintain an up-to-date master list of IPD grants, including grant descriptions.

Facilitate project start following funding approvals.

Monitor changes in IPD projects, advise the Program Team on documenting amendments, and communicate risks effectively.

Monitor donor grant requirements to ensure compliance, providing advice on cost extensions, non-cost extensions, agreement addendums, and other contractual issues.

Monitor project spending to prevent overspending or underspending and advise project teams accordingly.

Oversee project implementation from compliance perspective, advising teams on contractual clauses, amendments, risk management, and supporting timely project delivery.

Support Donor Monitoring Field visits: Coordinate with relevant team members and stakeholders, prepare one pager, arrange logistics, accompany monitoring field visits.

Track donor monitoring network meetings, maintain detailed minutes, and keep records of donor interactions and follow-ups.

Ensure proper documentation of all project amendments, and donor correspondence.

Train project team on donor grant compliance, funding policies, donor relations, donor reporting, contract management, etc

Prepare and submit IPD weekly, monthly updates and quarterly IPD reports

Donor Contract Management 

Prepare, coordinate, and develop partner due diligence reports and maintain filing systems.

Develop and maintain a mechanism for management of IPD Partnership agreements and signature processes, including contract/partnership agreement preparation, and preparation of consortium agreements.

Ensure all funding files (electronic, system and paper) are complete, filed and kept up to date.

Register and update SOS Rwanda project proposal development information in ProDIGI software

Partnership Development and Networking 

Establish and maintain regular contact with donors, attend donor forums, conferences etc

Identify and engage with in-country donors, foundation, embassies, diplomatic mission, bilateral, multilateral, international donors, to proactively explore and secure funding opportunities for IPD initiatives.

Develop partnerships and consortiums with other like-minded organizations and donors for purposes of bidding for large donor project proposals 

Represent SOS Rwanda in sector level meetings (development and humanitarian/emergency) and other networking forums and use this to develop funding partnerships

Organize partnership roundtable meetings and networking meetings

Participate in regional IPD networking and training forums and contribute to development of new IPD strategies to improve practice

Formal qualifications and Experiencerequirements:

Excellent English language written skills are required for development of proposals

A holder of a bachelor’s degree in Sociology, Development studies, Economics or related field. Master’s degree will be an added advantage.

Excellent know how of project proposal writing skills is required, especially in the sectors of Child Protection, Alternative Care, Youth Empowerment, Livelihoods, Education, Health

He/she should have 5-8 years’ extensive experience in planning, securing and managing funds from institutional donors as well as a thorough understanding of writing of project proposal 

Potential candidates should demonstrate evidence of medium/large proposals they have developed and won (0.5 – 2M USD)

A thorough understanding of Project Cycle Management is an asset.

Knowledge of Results-Based Management (RBM) approach is an additional asset

The post holder should have the following competencies flexibility, self-drive, attention to detail, respecting tight deadlines, ability to work with different teams in a fast-paced environment and ability to work independently. 

He/she should be highly proficient in MS Word, Excel, Power-point and the use of Internet for research.

Excellent English language written skills are required for development of proposals

item.title: Regional Audit job at Eastern Province
item.company: East African Science and Technology Commission (EASTECO)
item.description:
Job responsibilities

Organise periodical and annual audits of the Province regarding legal texts and procedures governing organisation and human resources management:

Verify the compliance of the structure with the organizational one approved by the authorities

Audit the level of implementation of the institution programmes

Propose useful amendments to improve the procedures, supports, and rules related to the performance evaluation of the institution.

Verify the compliance with the legal framework of the administrative acts: salaries, incumbent/work position matching, recruitments, training, career evolution, files agents keeping, and updating of related data basis

Supervise District audit regarding the respect of legal texts and procedures governing the budget execution in District and provide advice thereupon:

Conduct the annual financial and accountancy audit

Evaluate the quality of the finance statements produced

Control the steadiness of expenses and payments

Verify the regular updating of the accountancy books

Verify the compliance, the legality and accuracy of all debts documents

Verify that the account operations correspond to assets movement and are cross checked at reasonable intervals, and that these assets exist

Verify that the expended funds have been used according to prior programmes

Propose useful amendments to improve the procedures, supports, and rules related to a priori and a posteriori budgetary controls and of financial and accountancy operations

Analyse the periodical and annual audits of the District and Province regarding legal texts and procedures governing the assets managements and provide advice thereupon:

Verify the quality of assets security

Propose indicators to trigger physical control (census) of assets (buildings and equipments)

Control the rationality and logical repartition of these assets amongst units, agencies or entities under supervision

Produce periodical reports based on results of audits that have been conducted

To make follow-up on the implementation of the Auditor General’s recommendations to the District and Province:

To analyse reports of the Auditor General of State Finances concerning the Institution

To ensure implementation of recommendations of the Auditor General of State Finances directed to the District & Province and provide advice thereupon

item.company: East African Science and Technology Commission (EASTECO)
item.description_html:
Background information about the job or company

This is a Level 3.II position with 1 post available. The role is under contract.

Responsibilities or duties

Provide legal opinions on dossiers and contracts engaging the Province:

  • Deal with legal issues, providing legal advice on contractual, staff, financial and institutional matters to ensure their compliance with applicable laws, instructions, regulations and procedures;
  • Prepare modal contracts and decisions to be adopted and used by the Province;
  • Propose necessary amendments to contracts and agreements to avoid possible misinterpretations in support of the best interests of the Province;
  • Prepare documents and conclusions concerning litigious issues involving the institution for the Attorney General;
  • Facilitate the interpretation of the applicable laws, instructions, regulations and procedures;
  • Monitor the implementation of the applicable laws, instructions, regulations and procedures;

  • Advise management on litigation risks and contribute to finding solutions to avoid litigations;
  • Advise management on the validity and conformity of procedures with the standing/ applicable laws and regulations and seek for legal texts related to these requests;
  • Analyze contentious files and / or requests emanating from users or agents of the Province;
  • Propose solutions with competent authorities;

Develop legal and regulatory provisions (by laws, instructions) of the Province:

  • Drafting legal texts regarding the Province and deliver legal opinions on the draft laws, instructions, regulations and procedures
  • Collect, safeguard decisions carrying jurisprudence on Province appeal, and establish the documentation to serve the institution in legal matters, and inform regularly the services concerned;

To analyze citizen complaints involving legal matters

item.title: E-Commerce Specialist job at Ministry Of Trade And Industry
item.description:
Background information about the job or company (e.g., role context, company overview)

This role supports the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MINICOM) IT department in its mission to digitalize trade and industry sectors. It involves developing and implementing actionable plans, supporting ICT strategies aligned with the Smart Rwanda Master Plan (SRMP), and reviewing current ICT services. The specialist will also identify areas for harmonization, collaborate on e-business strategies, and engage with stakeholders to understand and meet business requirements. Continuous auditing of e-commerce platforms for performance and data-driven decision-making are key aspects of this position. The role also involves drafting project proposals for e-commerce fund mobilization.

Responsibilities or duties

The E-Commerce Specialist will be responsible for:

Supporting MINICOM IT department in the digitalization of trade and industry sectors.

Developing actionable plans and coordination for their implementation.

Supporting MINICOM departments in implementing ICT strategies relevant to trade and industry sectors, with connections to the Smart Rwanda Master Plan (SRMP).

Reviewing current ICT services, applications, and infrastructures in the trade and industry sectors.

Proposing potential areas for harmonization of overlapping systems to improve efficiency.

Collaborating with internal departments to strategize on e-business department opportunities and enhancements.

Partnering with stakeholders and the business community to understand business requirements and develop strategies to meet them.

Continually auditing e-commerce platforms for performance and driving recommendations for improvements.

Engaging in data-driven decision-making for planning, execution, and optimization of e-commerce development in Rwanda.

Drafting project proposals for e-commerce for fund mobilization purposes.

Qualifications or requirements

The required work experience of 3 years or 1 year must be relevant to the fields of E-Commerce, Trade, Industry and Project Management.

Experience needed

3 years or 1 year of relevant experience in E-Commerce, Trade, Industry, and Project Management.

Any other provided details (e.g., benefits, work environment, team info, or additional notes)

N.B. The required work experience of 3 years or 1 year must be relevant to the fields of E-Commerce, Trade, Industry and Project Management.

The national council for science and technology (NCST) is seeking a Procurement Officer. This is a Level 5.II position with 1 post available under contract.

Responsibilities or duties

The Procurement Officer will be responsible for:

Collecting information on tenders to be issued in a given Financial year.

Participating in the planning and budgeting process of the Institution.

Preparing the procurement plan.

Submitting the procurement plan to management for approval.

Making a follow-up on the submission of the procurement plan to RPPA and its publication on the institution’s website.

Preparing tender documents.

Producing tender notices.

Distributing tender documents and receiving bids.

Organizing the opening and evaluation of bids.

Preparing notification letters for bidders and recommending contract awards.

Organizing and participating in contract negotiation.

Providing information/support documents for contract drafting to the Legal affairs.

Following up on contract execution and completion in collaboration with the user department.

Preparing certificates of completion for suppliers.

Serving as Secretary to the institution tender committee.

Producing and submitting timely monthly reports to RPPA on procurement plan progress.

Producing procurement reports as required by a funding institution or donor.

Facilitating Procurement Audit.

Ensuring a proper and safe filling system for procurement information.

Submitting periodical reports to the institution’s management.

Experience in procurement processes, tender management, and contract administration is expected.

item.title: Legal Advisor job at Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course
item.location: Kigali Golf Course, Kigali, Rwanda | Kigali
item.description:
Position Summary

The Legal Advisor is the organization's dedicated in-house legal, risk and compliance authority, providing proactive legal counsel while owning enterprise risk management and the compliance program. The role is prospective and advisory in nature, embedded within management, and is deliberately distinct from the Internal Audit function, which independently and retrospectively tests whether policies and controls are being followed. The Legal Advisor reports directly to the General Manager and works closely with the Board on material legal, risk, and compliance matters.

Key Responsibilities

Legal Advisory

Draft, review, and negotiate contracts, including supplier agreements, OTA (online booking platform) contracts, event and banquet contracts, leases, franchise or management agreements, Sponsorship and Membership.

Maintain a central contract register and monitor important contractual deadlines and renewals.

Manage disputes, claims, and litigation in coordination with external counsel, protecting the organization's legal and financial position.

Provide legal opinions to the General Manager and Board on business decisions, new initiatives, and licensing matters.

Monitor and interpret changes in relevant law and regulation, including labor, licensing, consumer protection, and data privacy, and translate these into practical guidance for the business.

Manage corporate governance documentation, including board resolutions, the contracts registry, and intellectual property/trademark records.

Act as company representative in legal and regulatory matters, liaising with external counsel and regulators as required.

Risk Management

Build and maintain the enterprise risk register, covering operational, financial, reputational, and strategic risk.

Design and maintain the organization's risk appetite and risk treatment frameworks.

Lead crisis and incident response planning, including guest safety incidents, data breaches, and reputational or PR crises.

Own business continuity planning and periodic insurance adequacy reviews.

Compliance

Policy Development: write, update, and implement company policies, standards, and internal control systems, and lead their rollout across departments.

Design and own the organization's overall compliance program, including codes of conduct and supporting frameworks.

Act as the primary point of contact for regulators and licensing authorities (e.g., liquor licensing, tourism/hospitality regulation, fire and safety codes).

Monitor ongoing compliance with anti-money laundering (AML), data protection, labor, and health and safety regulations.

Conduct proactive compliance risk assessments and gap analyses, distinct from Internal Audit's control testing.

Staff Training: educate employees and leadership on compliance standards, codes of conduct, and new or changing legal requirements, through periodic training sessions.

Compliance Reviews & Reporting: run periodic internal compliance reviews, document findings, and report compliance issues and recommendations to the General Manager and, where material, the Board — distinct from Internal Audit's independent assurance testing.

Investigations: look into suspected policy violations or legal/regulatory breaches referred to the role and manage intake of the whistleblowing/ethics hotline (case management; investigations requiring independent audit assurance remain with Internal Audit).

Governance and Coordination

Maintain a clear delineation of duties from Internal Audit to avoid duplication and preserve Internal Audit's independence: the Legal Advisor builds and owns policies and frameworks; Internal Audit independently tests whether they are being followed.

Convene a quarterly coordination meeting with Internal Audit to align risk registers and avoid duplicated fieldwork.

Escalate material legal, risk, and compliance matters to the General Manager and, where warranted, directly to the Board.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in law (LLB), business, or a related field or relevant master's degree is an added advantage.

Must be a member in good standing with the Rwanda Bar Association (RBA), or demonstrate eligibility for admission (e.g., completion of a Diploma in Legal Practice from a recognized institution).

A postgraduate qualification or certification in Risk Management and/or Compliance (e.g., ICA Diploma in Compliance, CAMS for AML) is a strong advantage.

Minimum 5–8 years of post-qualification legal experience, ideally combining law firm and in-house exposure.

Demonstrated experience in contract negotiation and commercial law.

Prior exposure to regulatory liaison with licensing bodies, Labor authorities, and tax/AML regulators.

Hospitality, tourism, retail, or service-industry legal experience strongly preferred.

Experience building or running a compliance program from the ground up is a plus.

Key Competencies

Legal drafting and negotiation: contracts, policies, and memoranda of understanding.

Regulatory intelligence: ability to track and translate legal and regulatory change into business action.

Risk analysis: sound quantitative and qualitative risk assessment methodology.

Stakeholder management: able to advise the General Manager and Board while working cross-functionally with Operations, HR, and Finance.

Crisis management: composure and sound decision-making under incident pressure.

Communication: able to translate complex legal and regulatory language into practical guidance for non-legal staff (Front Office, F&B, Housekeeping, and other operational teams).

Integrity and independence of judgment: willing to escalate uncomfortable findings to management.

Attention to detail: precision in policy drafting, contract review, and compliance documentation.

Commercial pragmatism: advice that is workable for a fast-paced, guest-facing business rather than purely academic.

Scope Boundary with Internal Audit

To preserve Internal Audit's independence and avoid duplication of duties, the following remain explicitly outside the scope of this role:

Independent testing of control effectiveness (remains with Internal Audit).

Retrospective audit reporting to the Audit Committee/Board.

Assurance opinions on financial or operational controls.

Leading or opining on investigations requiring independent audit assurance (the Legal Advisor may support with legal input only).

  • Lead crisis and incident response planning, including guest safety incidents, data breaches, and reputational or PR crises.
  • Own business continuity planning and periodic insurance adequacy reviews.

Compliance

  • Policy Development: write, update, and implement company policies, standards, and internal control systems, and lead their rollout across departments.
  • Design and own the organization's overall compliance program, including codes of conduct and supporting frameworks.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for regulators and licensing authorities (e.g., liquor licensing, tourism/hospitality regulation, fire and safety codes).
  • Monitor ongoing compliance with anti-money laundering (AML), data protection, labor, and health and safety regulations.
  • Conduct proactive compliance risk assessments and gap analyses, distinct from Internal Audit's control testing.
  • Staff Training: educate employees and leadership on compliance standards, codes of conduct, and new or changing legal requirements, through periodic training sessions.
  • Compliance Reviews & Reporting: run periodic internal compliance reviews, document findings, and report compliance issues and recommendations to the General Manager and, where material, the Board — distinct from Internal Audit's independent assurance testing.
  • Investigations: look into suspected policy violations or legal/regulatory breaches referred to the role and manage intake of the whistleblowing/ethics hotline (case management; investigations requiring independent audit assurance remain with Internal Audit).

Governance and Coordination

  • Maintain a clear delineation of duties from Internal Audit to avoid duplication and preserve Internal Audit's independence: the Legal Advisor builds and owns policies and frameworks; Internal Audit independently tests whether they are being followed.
  • Convene a quarterly coordination meeting with Internal Audit to align risk registers and avoid duplicated fieldwork.
  • Escalate material legal, risk, and compliance matters to the General Manager and, where warranted, directly to the Board.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in law (LLB), business, or a related field or relevant master's degree is an added advantage.
  • Must be a member in good standing with the Rwanda Bar Association (RBA), or demonstrate eligibility for admission (e.g., completion of a Diploma in Legal Practice from a recognized institution).
  • A postgraduate qualification or certification in Risk Management and/or Compliance (e.g., ICA Diploma in Compliance, CAMS for AML) is a strong advantage.
  • Minimum 5–8 years of post-qualification legal experience, ideally combining law firm and in-house exposure.
  • Demonstrated experience in contract negotiation and commercial law.
  • Prior exposure to regulatory liaison with licensing bodies, Labor authorities, and tax/AML regulators.
  • Hospitality, tourism, retail, or service-industry legal experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience building or running a compliance program from the ground up is a plus.

Key Competencies

  • Legal drafting and negotiation: contracts, policies, and memoranda of understanding.
  • Regulatory intelligence: ability to track and translate legal and regulatory change into business action.
  • Risk analysis: sound quantitative and qualitative risk assessment methodology.
  • Stakeholder management: able to advise the General Manager and Board while working cross-functionally with Operations, HR, and Finance.
  • Crisis management: composure and sound decision-making under incident pressure.
  • Communication: able to translate complex legal and regulatory language into practical guidance for non-legal staff (Front Office, F&B, Housekeeping, and other operational teams).
  • Integrity and independence of judgment: willing to escalate uncomfortable findings to management.
  • Attention to detail: precision in policy drafting, contract review, and compliance documentation.
  • Commercial pragmatism: advice that is workable for a fast-paced, guest-facing business rather than purely academic.

Scope Boundary with Internal Audit

To preserve Internal Audit's independence and avoid duplication of duties, the following remain explicitly outside the scope of this role:

  • Independent testing of control effectiveness (remains with Internal Audit).
  • Retrospective audit reporting to the Audit Committee/Board.
  • Assurance opinions on financial or operational controls.
  • Leading or opining on investigations requiring independent audit assurance (the Legal Advisor may support with legal input only).

item.title: Extension Knowledge & Content Developer job at Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture ( RICA )
item.company: Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture ( RICA )
item.description:
Background

The Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture (RICA) is an innovative English-language undergraduate institution that prepares future agricultural leaders in Rwanda and East Africa through practical, experiential learning. Its curriculum integrates Conservation Agriculture, One Health, innovation, entrepreneurship, communication, and leadership, supported by hands-on training across six agricultural enterprises.

The Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture (RICA) is implementing activities under the Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA) project on Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA), Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), and Livelihood Development. As implementation progresses, the project is generating valuable evidence, experiences, lessons, and results that need to be systematically captured, organized, analyzed, and shared.

Therefore, RICA intends to engage a Knowledge Content Creator to strengthen project knowledge management systems; document achievements, lessons learned, best practices, and impacts; and produce quality content for beneficiaries, partners, policymakers, donors, and the public.

ROLE PURPOSE:

The purpose of the assignment is to establish and maintain an effective knowledge-management and content-production function for the project. The staff will capture and organize project knowledge, convert technical evidence into accessible communication products, support internal learning and external visibility, and ensure that approved materials are easy to retrieve and reuse.

OBJECTIVES

Document project achievements, outcomes, innovations, lessons learned, and best practices.

Create compelling, audience-appropriate content, including human-interest stories that demonstrate changes experienced by project beneficiaries.

Translate technical information into clear, engaging, and accessible content for diverse audiences.

Strengthen extension learning by facilitating the flow of knowledge among project teams, partners, and stakeholders.

Ensure that all knowledge and communication products meet professional editorial, ethical, branding, and quality standards.

SCOPE OF WORK

Support extension teams to capture, validate, and share knowledge consistently and on time.

Research, write, and package feature articles, news stories, success stories, case studies, briefs, newsletters, blogs, and social-media content.

Prepare publication content for extension events, presentations, reports, and stakeholder engagement activities.

Visit extension project sites to collect firsthand information and document progress and results.

Conduct interviews with beneficiaries, local leaders, government officials, technical experts, and RICA partners.

Gather photographs, testimonies, quotations, data, and supporting records to enrich and substantiate extension materials.

Obtain and securely maintain informed-consent records for interviews, images, and personal stories, in accordance with applicable requirements.

Compile stories of change, lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and emerging recommendations.

Prepare concise reports and summaries of workshops, trainings, field visits, learning events, and other project activities.

DURATION

The assignment will be undertaken over a period of six (6) months renewable, commencing on the date of signing the contract.

DUTY STATION AND TRAVEL

The staff will be based at the RICA Campus in Bugesera District, with regular field travels as required. Travel arrangements and related costs will be handled in accordance with applicable RICA procedures.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in information management, marketing, mass communication, business studies, development studies, or another relevant field.

At least three (3) years of professional experience demonstrated in knowledge management, content development, marketing, journalism, development communication, or a closely related field.

Proven experience in designing or maintaining knowledge repositories, documentation systems, and websites.

Excellent English writing, editing, proofreading, interviewing, and storytelling skills.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

Ability to manage multiple assignments independently.

Excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

Ability and willingness to travel to field sites and work effectively in remote settings.

item.title: Assistant to the Director of Campus Operations and Events job at Ntare Louisenlund International School Rwanda
item.description:
Who We Are

Ntare Louisenlund International School Rwanda aspires to become a leading institution in Africa, dedicated to fostering excellence in education. Through the Rwanda plus-STEM program, the school attracts the finest talents in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences, and technology, serving as a catalyst for innovation, entrepreneurship, and future-shaping endeavors. Situated on a scenic 60-hectare campus in Rwanda’s Bugesera District, just a forty-five-minute drive from Kigali, the full boarding school currently accommodates 250 students from grades 7–8, and will welcome an additional 110 students into grade 9 in September 2026.

Ntare Louisenlund School is committed to delivering an exceptional international education, empowering students to secure scholarships at the world’s leading universities. The student body is uniquely diverse, consisting of a plus-STEM stream of talented students selected through a rigorous assessment process and funded by scholarships, alongside students from across Africa pursuing the IB Diploma whose families finance their education. As an IB World School, Ntare Louisenlund School currently offers the IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) from grades 7-9, with plans to introduce the Diploma Programme (DP) in the near future. The school is operated and managed by Ntare Louisenlund CBC in close collaboration with Stiftung Louisenlund, a renowned institution with over 75 years of experience running a premier secondary boarding school in Germany, ensuring a shared standard of excellence across both locations. Additionally, the school maintains a strategic partnership with the Rwandan government to support plus-STEM students receiving national scholarships.

Your Challenge & Responsibilities

The Assistant to the Director of Campus Operations and Events provides administrative, coordination and operational support to ensure the smooth running of campus operations and the effective planning and delivery of School events. The role serves as a central coordination point between the Director, internal departments, service providers and other stakeholders. The post holder is expected to be highly organized, service-oriented, discreet and able to manage multiple priorities in a busy international school environment.

Your main duties and responsibilities include:

Executive and Administrative Support

Manage the Director’s calendar, appointments, meetings, reminders and follow-up actions.

Prepare agendas, meeting packs, minutes, briefing notes, reports, presentations and routine correspondence.

Maintain accurate electronic and physical records for campus operations, events, suppliers, facilities and related activities.

Track decisions, assigned actions and deadlines, and provide timely reminders to responsible staff members.

Receive and appropriately direct enquiries, requests and concerns relating to campus operations and events.

Handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

Campus Operations Coordination

Support the Director in coordinating daily operational requirements across the School campus, including classrooms, offices, boarding facilities, common areas and event spaces.

Receive, log and follow up maintenance, facilities, transport, grounds, housekeeping, security and logistical requests with the relevant teams.

Assist in planning room allocations, venue readiness, furniture arrangements, signage and operational set-ups.

Conduct or support routine readiness checks and report defects, risks, delays or service gaps to the Director.

Maintain operational schedules, checklists, service records, asset-related information and departmental trackers.

Support coordination with contractors, vendors and service providers, including access arrangements, work schedules and completion follow-up.

Assist with stock monitoring and timely requests for operational and event-related supplies.

Events Planning and Delivery

Support the planning and delivery of School events, meetings, ceremonies, conferences, parent activities, student programs, official visits and community engagements.

Prepare event plans, timelines, checklists, duty rosters, venue layouts, guest lists and logistical requirements.

Coordinate event requirements such as venues, seating, audio-visual support, catering, décor, transport, accommodation, protocol, security, cleaning and signage.

Liaise with internal departments and external service providers to confirm responsibilities, timelines and standards.

Be present during event set-up, delivery and breakdown, including outside normal working hours when required.

Support guest reception, registration, ushering, protocol and the resolution of operational issues during events.

Assist with post-event reviews, documentation of lessons learned and follow-up on outstanding actions or supplier matters.

Procurement, Budget and Vendor Support

Prepare and track purchase requests, quotations, delivery notes, invoices and other supporting documentation in accordance with School procedures.

Assist the Director in monitoring departmental and event expenditure against approved budgets.

Maintain organized vendor and service-provider records, including contacts, quotations, agreements and performance notes.

Verify that requested goods and services have been delivered as agreed and promptly report any discrepancies.

Promote value for money, proper documentation and responsible use of School resources.

Communication and Stakeholder Coordination

Serve as a professional point of contact for staff, students, parents, visitors and suppliers on matters assigned by the Director.

Communicate operational and event arrangements clearly, accurately and in a timely manner.

Maintain positive working relationships across academic, boarding, administration, security, finance, procurement, transport, communications and other School functions.

Escalate urgent concerns, safety issues, service failures or reputational risks to the Director without delay.

Provide courteous and culturally sensitive service in line with the standards of an international school.

Safety, Safeguarding and Compliance

Comply with the School’s safeguarding, child-protection, health and safety, security, data-protection and confidentiality requirements.

Support the implementation of risk assessments, emergency arrangements, access controls and safety measures for events and campus activities.

Immediately report hazards, incidents, safeguarding concerns or breaches of procedure through the appropriate channels.

Ensure contractors, visitors and service providers follow School access, conduct and safety requirements.

Carry out duties in accordance with applicable Rwandan laws, School policies and approved procedures.

Your Profile

Bachelor’s degree or advanced diploma in Business Administration, Hospitality, Events Management, Facilities Management, Operations, Public Administration or a related field.

At least two years of relevant experience in administration, operations, facilities, hospitality, events or executive support; experience in a school, hotel, conference centre or similar service environment is an advantage.

Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple activities, stakeholders, schedules and deadlines.

Practical experience preparing reports, meeting minutes, trackers, purchase documentation and event plans.

Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office or Google Workspace, particularly Word/Docs, Excel/Sheets, PowerPoint/Slides, email and calendars.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Kinyarwanda is strongly preferred; knowledge of French or German is an added advantage.

A valid driving license is an advantage.

Experience within international schools, higher education, or nonprofit organizations.

Experience working in Africa and/or within multicultural environments.

Familiarity with donor-funded programs and grant compliance.

Required Competencies and Personal Attributes

Excellent organization, planning and time-management skills.

Strong attention to detail and a disciplined approach to documentation and follow-up.

Professional written and verbal communication skills.

Ability to anticipate needs, solve problems and remain calm under pressure.

High level of integrity, reliability, discretion and accountability.

Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.

Service mindset, flexibility and willingness to support activities beyond normal office hours when operationally necessary.

Ability to work independently while keeping the Director appropriately informed.

Commitment to safeguarding, student wellbeing and the values of Ntare Louisenlund School.

Key Performance Indicators

Administrative tasks, minutes, reports and follow-up actions are completed accurately and on time.

Operational requests are properly logged, assigned, monitored and closed within agreed timelines.

Events are delivered according to approved plans, budgets, safety requirements and service standards.

Venues, facilities and logistical arrangements are ready at the required time.

Vendor, procurement and expenditure documentation is complete, accurate and well organized.

Internal and external stakeholders receive timely, professional and helpful communication.

Risks, incidents, delays and service failures are promptly identified and escalated.

School policies, safeguarding standards and confidentiality requirements are consistently observed.

Benefits & Compensation

A fully equipped school campus with excellent facilities in a beautiful natural setting in Bugesera.

An exceptional in-house professional development program with travel opportunities for further IB professional development.

Small learning groups.

An extensive and diverse co-curricular program and the possibility of taking part in or offering co-curricular experiences for students.

Collaboration with an experienced, internationally recognized school in Germany.

Various partnerships with external educational partners.

A committed, dedicated, and team-oriented faculty.

A competitive compensation package (in Rwandan Francs), based on your level of experience
