item.description:
The University of Rwanda (UR), through the College of Medicine and Health Sciences (CMHS), School of Medicine and Pharmacy, is seeking a qualified and highly motivated Specialist Neurologist to strengthen specialist clinical care, medical education, research, and academic development within its affiliated teaching hospitals.

The Specialist Neurologist will provide high-quality, evidence-based neurological care to inpatients and outpatients while contributing actively to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, clinical supervision, research, mentorship, quality improvement, and professional service.

The successful candidate will work closely with clinical and academic teams to strengthen neurological services and contribute to the training of medical students, interns, residents, postgraduate trainees, and other healthcare professionals.

Responsibilities or duties

Provide specialist neurological assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up for patients with a wide range of neurological disorders.

Conduct specialist outpatient clinics and provide inpatient neurological consultations.

Participate in emergency neurological care, including the management of acute stroke, seizures, altered consciousness, and other neurological emergencies.

Request, interpret, and appropriately utilize laboratory, neuroimaging, electrophysiological, and other diagnostic investigations.

Develop and implement individualized treatment and follow-up plans and make appropriate referrals to multidisciplinary services.

Participate in ward rounds, multidisciplinary meetings, case conferences, clinical audits, morbidity and mortality meetings, and other clinical review activities.

Maintain accurate, confidential, and timely clinical records in accordance with professional standards and hospital policies.

Promote patient safety, ethical practice, evidence-based care, and compliance with applicable clinical guidelines and hospital procedures.

Teach medical students, interns, residents, postgraduate trainees, and other healthcare professionals through bedside teaching, lectures, seminars, case presentations, journal clubs, and other appropriate learning activities.

Supervise, assess, and mentor trainees in accordance with programme requirements and provide appropriate academic and career guidance.

Contribute to the development and review of curricula, clinical guidelines, teaching materials, examinations, and other academic resources.

Conduct and supervise clinical and academic research relevant to neurology and institutional health priorities.

Publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present research at professional and academic conferences.

Promote evidence-based practice and encourage research engagement among residents, medical students, and other healthcare professionals.

Participate in departmental and hospital committees, quality improvement initiatives, clinical audits, and on-call services.

Contribute to the development and review of departmental policies, protocols, standard operating procedures, and clinical guidelines.

Maintain active professional registration, medical licensure, continuing professional development, and other applicable professional requirements.

Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the Programme Director or Head of Department.

Qualifications or requirements

Recognized Medical Degree (MD, MBBS, MBChB) from an accredited institution.

Recognized postgraduate specialist qualification in Neurology, such as an MMed, Specialist Degree, or Fellowship in Neurology.

Valid registration and licence to practice medicine issued by the relevant professional regulatory authority.

Eligibility for appointment at Senior Lecturer level or above, in accordance with applicable University of Rwanda academic requirements.

For qualifications obtained outside Rwanda, the candidate must provide the required Equivalence Certificate from the Rwanda Higher Education Council (HEC) prior to final appointment.

Relevant clinical experience in neurology with demonstrated ability to independently manage neurological patients.

Demonstrated experience in teaching, clinical supervision, or mentorship of medical students, interns, residents, or other healthcare professionals.

Demonstrated experience in clinical, academic, or research activities relevant to neurology.

Strong clinical and diagnostic skills in the assessment and management of neurological conditions.

Excellent clinical decision-making and problem-solving abilities.

Strong commitment to evidence-based practice, patient safety, and quality clinical care.

Demonstrated ability to teach, supervise, mentor, and support the professional development of trainees.

Strong research, academic writing, and scientific communication skills.

Excellent interpersonal, communication, and teamwork skills.

Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary clinical and academic teams.

High standards of professional ethics, confidentiality, integrity, and accountability.

Commitment to continuous professional development and lifelong learning.

Ability to contribute effectively to clinical governance, quality improvement, and institutional development.

Why Join This Project?

Support the training and development of the next generation of medical doctors and specialist physicians.

Participate in clinical research and academic activities addressing national and regional health priorities.

Work within a multidisciplinary academic and clinical environment.

Contribute to evidence-based improvements in neurological care, medical education, and health service delivery.

item.title: Clinical Pathologist job at King Faisal Hospital Rwanda Foundation (KFHRF)
item.company: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda Foundation ( KFHRF )
item.description:
Background information about the job or company

The University of Rwanda (UR), through the College of Medicine and Health Sciences (CMHS), School of Medicine and Pharmacy, is seeking qualified and highly motivated Clinical Pathologists to strengthen specialist laboratory medicine services, postgraduate medical education, clinical research, laboratory quality management, and academic development within the University and its affiliated teaching hospitals.

The Clinical Pathologist will contribute to the delivery of high-quality specialist clinical pathology and laboratory medicine services while supporting undergraduate and postgraduate education, clinical supervision, research, laboratory quality assurance, mentorship, and academic programme development.

The successful candidates will work collaboratively with clinicians, laboratory professionals, academic staff, postgraduate trainees, and other healthcare professionals to strengthen diagnostic services and promote evidence-based clinical practice.

Responsibilities or duties

Provide specialist clinical pathology and laboratory medicine services across relevant areas, including clinical chemistry, haematology, microbiology, immunology, transfusion medicine, and related disciplines.

Interpret laboratory results and provide appropriate clinical consultation to healthcare professionals regarding diagnosis, patient management, and diagnostic utilization.

Promote appropriate and cost-effective utilization of laboratory investigations in support of quality patient care.

Lead or contribute to laboratory clinical governance, patient safety, quality assurance, quality control, and accreditation activities.

Support monitoring and implementation of applicable laboratory quality management systems and standards.

Develop, review, and implement laboratory standard operating procedures, clinical guidelines, policies, and quality improvement initiatives.

Participate in multidisciplinary clinical meetings, morbidity and mortality reviews, antimicrobial stewardship activities, and other relevant clinical forums.

Teach undergraduate medical students and postgraduate trainees through lectures, tutorials, seminars, laboratory sessions, case discussions, and other appropriate teaching methods.

Supervise postgraduate residents in clinical pathology and contribute to competency-based assessment, examinations, and trainee evaluations.

Contribute to curriculum development, review, and implementation for undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.

Utilize appropriate educational technologies, including digital learning and simulation-based approaches, to strengthen teaching and learning.

Mentor residents, early-career faculty, postgraduate students, and other healthcare professionals in clinical, academic, and research activities.

Support junior faculty in teaching, assessment, research, academic development, and career progression.

Develop, lead, and participate in clinically relevant research aligned with institutional, national, and regional health priorities.

Publish research findings in peer-reviewed scientific journals and present findings at relevant academic and professional conferences.

Supervise postgraduate dissertations and support postgraduate students in research design, data analysis, scientific writing, and publication.

Contribute to research grant proposals, resource mobilization, and academic collaborations.

Ensure that research activities comply with applicable ethical, regulatory, and professional requirements.

Participate in curriculum review, programme evaluation, accreditation activities, academic committees, and institutional quality improvement initiatives.

Support the development of institutional collaborations, subspecialty training opportunities, and research networks.

Maintain active professional registration, medical licensure, continuing professional development, and other applicable professional requirements.

Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the Programme Director or Head of Department.

Qualifications or requirements

Recognized Medical Degree (MD, MBBS, MBChB) from an accredited institution.

Recognized postgraduate degree in Clinical Pathology, such as an MMed, Specialist Degree, or Fellowship in Clinical Pathology.

Valid registration and licence to practice medicine issued by a recognized professional regulatory authority.

Eligibility for academic appointment at Lecturer level or above, in accordance with applicable University of Rwanda academic requirements.

Demonstrated experience in clinical laboratory practice, laboratory medicine, postgraduate teaching, clinical supervision, research, or laboratory quality management.

Demonstrated ability to teach, supervise, mentor, or assess medical students, residents, postgraduate trainees, or healthcare professionals.

For qualifications obtained outside Rwanda, the candidate must provide the required Equivalence Certificate from the Rwanda Higher Education Council (HEC) prior to final appointment.

Skills & Competencies

Strong technical and clinical knowledge in laboratory medicine and clinical pathology.

Excellent analytical, diagnostic, and clinical decision-making skills.

Strong understanding of laboratory quality assurance, quality control, patient safety, and clinical governance.

Demonstrated ability to teach, supervise, assess, and mentor postgraduate trainees and junior faculty.

Strong research, scientific writing, publication, and critical appraisal skills.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams.

Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities.

Commitment to evidence-based practice and continuous quality improvement.

High standards of professional ethics, integrity, confidentiality, and accountability.

Commitment to continuous professional development and lifelong learning.

Ability to contribute effectively to academic programme development, accreditation, and institutional improvement.

item.title: Regional Manager - Head of Subunit Financing & Recipients Relations job at GIZ Rwanda
item.description:
The position provides leadership to a team of specialists, collaborates with several units in, drives continuous process improvement, ensures high-quality service delivery to projects and partners, and safeguards GIZ's contractual and fiduciary interests throughout the lifecycle of financing arrangements.

B. Main Tasks and Responsibilities

Provide leadership to the staff assigned to you in accordance with the GIZ’s leadership principles, including addressing all staff-related issues in a professional and timely manner and taking decisions if and as needed

Lead, coordinate and manage the unit responsible for providing advice to projects on financing arrangements, including Local Contribution Contracts, Grant Agreements, Financing Agreements and other contractual instruments, as well as Integrated Development Partnerships with the Private Sector (iDPP) and construction contracts during the planning stage, in line with GIZ’s internal policies and procedures (P+R), applicable laws and compliance standards.

Guide and supervise the team in assuming process responsibility for the preparation and quality assurance of the Legal and Commercial Eligibility Check (KEP).

Coordinate and oversee the processing and validation of incoming requests for financing arrangements, ensuring that the team applies the required quality and compliance standards and observes applicable threshold limits before requests are submitted to the contract processing units.

Manage and coordinate the team’s activities related to contract amendments, extensions and closeout procedures, ensuring consistent application of relevant contractual and procedural requirements.

Provide strategic and professional guidance to the team in supporting recipients throughout contract implementation and in organizing appropriate capacity development measures.

Ensure that the team systematically monitors reporting deadlines, supports recipients during reporting phases, and conducts quality checks of documentation prior to submission to the responsible unit.

Oversee and coordinate the team’s activities to ensure that contractually required external audits are conducted and that audit contracts are prepared in a timely and compliant manner.

Guide and coordinate the team in safeguarding GIZ’s interests throughout the auditing process, including the coordination of auditors and recipients and participation in audit opening and closing meetings, as appropriate.

Ensure that the team follows up on audit findings, irregularities and instances of non-compliance and that appropriate corrective measures are initiated, monitored and documented.

Ensure that records management is properly organized and implemented within the group, including the systematic and compliant maintenance of relevant contractual, financial, audit and process documentation.

Strengthen cooperation structures with other units at headquarters and in the country office.

C. Required Qualifications, Competences and Experience

1. Qualifications and professional experience

A university degree in Business Administration, combined with experience in various commercial and technical roles in the field of development cooperation – preferably within GIZ. 

Several years’ experience in the line management of diverse teams in various cultural contexts, as well as experience in remote management

Several years’ experience in financial management, including (large-scale) EU co-financing, as well as experience in conducting internal audits

Customer focus and the ability to collaborate, combined with assertiveness, adaptability to a changing portfolio, commitment, reliability, diplomatic skills, gender competence and intercultural understanding of the region

In-depth familiarity with the new SAP software and confident use of MS software

Business fluency in German and English

2. Other knowledge and additional competences

The ability to provide direction and motivation in shaping the new landscape of roles and collaboration

Strong conceptual and analytical skills in designing efficient processes, whilst avoiding duplication and bottlenecks.

Several years’ experience in managing change processes.

A basic knowledge of French or Kinyarwanda is an asset.

item.title: Gender-Transformative & Social Inclusion Expert (GTSI) (H/F) job at Expertise France
item.description:
Expertise France is the French public agency for international technical cooperation. Present in over 100 countries, the agency engineers and implements capacity-building projects, mobilizes technical expertise, and acts as project coordinator across four priority areas: democratic, economic and financial governance; stability in crisis and post-crisis contexts; climate change and sustainable urban development; and strengthening health systems, social protection and employment. About TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” is on of Expertise France projects that is being implemented in Rwanda. The “TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” project aims to contribute to the National Strategy for Transformation and Vision 2050 established by the Government of Rwanda to guide the socio-economic development of the country towards a prosperous and high-income economy by 2050. Representing 25% of GDP and 70% of Rwanda's active population, agriculture is a key sector targeted in order to boost the country's economy and create jobs is one of the priorities for the sector's transformation, with the national objective of establishing TVET Centers of Excellence in Agriculture (CoE, also referred to as Centers of Vocational Excellence).

The “TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” project is implemented by Expertise France to support the national agency Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) in the establishment of TVET Centers of Excellence in Agriculture. In line with national priorities, the project aims to increase the sustainability, climate resilience and inclusion of agricultural practices by strengthening the skills of women and youth in Rwanda.

The project is structured around two specific objectives:

Improve access of women and youth to quality skills and formal certification in agricultural practices.

Improve the effectiveness of mechanisms for integrating women and young people into the agricultural labor market, with an emphasis on sustainable agriculture.

In Rwanda, 77% of farmers are women, mainly in subsistence agriculture, vulnerable to climate change. The project is classified under the OECD-DAC Gender Equality Policy Marker 2: gender equality is a principal objective of the intervention, and the project implements transformative and sustainable actions for women, young girls and their communities.

The project is implemented over a period of five years, with a budget of +16 million euros financed by the EU and the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. It includes technical assistance at the national level in support of RTB, and two Technical Secondary Schools — Kisaro TSS (Rulindo District) and AEF Nyagahanga (Gatsibo District) — are also supported with technical assistance, infrastructure rehabilitation and procurement of agricultural equipment as they transform into Agricultural TVET Centers of Excellence. The project is implemented in collaboration with the beneficiary partner RTB, as well as with donors and project partners, such as LuxDev.

The project is led by the Project Manager, with direct support from the Deputy Project Manager, and the team consists of 4 Technical Experts, a MEAL Officer, and 2 Project Advisors based in targeted TVET schools. The team is supported by Expertise France's Kigali-based Project Support Unit (PSU) for administration, finance, Human Resources and procurement, as well as Paris-based HQ.

The project has adopted and validated a Gender-Transformative and Socially Inclusive Framework Strategy (2024–2029) , with an accompanying Training Architecture and a detailed, DAC-aligned Action Plan. The project is now entering its transition phase — running for a minimum of three years — during which this strategy moves from formulation to full institutional implementation across both Centers of Excellence. This phase places substantially higher technical and delivery demands on the position than the project's start-up year.

Responsibilities or duties

1. To lead the implementation of the Gender-Transformative Framework Strategy

Operate the Theory of Change. Drive the five transformation pathways — inclusive governance; equitable and safe learning environments; gender-responsive work-based learning; safeguarding and GBV prevention; inclusive transition to employment and entrepreneurship — as a single integrated system, advancing them in parallel rather than as isolated activities.

Translate strategy into delivery. Convert the strategy’s Action Plan into detailed annual and quarterly operational programming: sequencing, responsibilities, milestones, budget lines and monitoring calendars, fully reflected in project workplans.

Secure OECD-DAC Marker 2 compliance. Lead the classification, indicator design (DAC 1 & 2 aligned, sex-, age- and disability-disaggregated), evidence base and EU reporting required to sustain the project’s Marker 2 status, in liaison with the MEAL Officer.

Provide technical direction across the team. Guide the other Technical Experts, Project Advisors and RTB counterparts so that gender-transformative and inclusion requirements are embedded in curricula, work-based learning, infrastructure design, procurement specifications and terms of reference across all workstreams — not carried by the GTSI workstream alone. Lead the GTSI Technical Working Group.

2. To design and deliver advanced capacity-building content

Author high-level training material. Personally design, write and quality-assure competency-based training content, facilitator guides, participant handbooks, audit tools and assessment instruments across all levels of the project’s Training Architecture. The authorship of this material is a core deliverable of the post.

Deliver and certify. Facilitate or co-facilitate training for school teachers and leadership, project and RTB staff, private-sector work-based learning host companies, and students; operate the associated certification and recognition framework with RTB.

Engage beyond the schools. Develop and implement the engagement approach for private-sector actors, cooperatives, farmers and adult learners, including Inclusion Compacts, employer awareness sessions and workplace inclusion standards.

Build sustainable learning systems. Establish and animate Communities of Practice so that gender and inclusion competency is sustained beyond direct project interventions.

3. To manage the GTSI activity package end to end

Programme and deliver. Own operational planning, sequencing and delivery of the full GTSI activity package to the standard set by the Action Plan.

Manage procurement and consultants. Prepare terms of reference, contribute to procurement in liaison with the PSU, and technically supervise national and international consultants mobilised on GTSI assignments, including quality control and technical validation of their deliverables.

Manage the budget. Plan, propose and track GTSI budget lines, including gender-responsive budgeting, ensuring sound execution and donor compliance.

Monitor, evaluate and report. Track progress against disaggregated indicators, capture lessons learned, operate the GTSI dashboard/MIS in liaison with the MEAL Officer, and report to project leadership, RTB and the donor.

4. To support the transition of the schools into TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture

Institutionalise the gender-transformative agenda. Support Kisaro TSS and AEF Nyagahanga to embed gender equality and social inclusion in governance, planning, budgeting, staff performance frameworks and accountability systems, including scorecards and community accountability forums.

Secure inclusive access to practice. Operationalise measures ensuring equitable access for female learners and learners with disabilities to practical training units, dual training and internships, including the control points needed to counter guidance bias and de facto exclusion.

Institutionalise safe learning environments. Support the establishment of GBV/SEAH reporting mechanisms, accessible grievance channels and safeguarding referral pathways aligned with PSEA standards.

Promote inclusive campuses. Provide technical inputs during design, construction and renovation so that facilities are accessible to women, persons with disabilities and other disadvantaged groups.

Qualifications or requirements

Master’s Degree in Gender and Development, Social Inclusion, Development Studies, Sociology or another relevant field.

Experience needed

At least 10 years of progressive professional experience in gender equality and social inclusion within development programmes.

Demonstrable experience of gender-transformative programming — that is, work explicitly aimed at changing institutional norms, structures and power relations — as distinct from gender mainstreaming, gender analysis, gender audits or awareness-raising.

Proven experience translating a gender-transformative strategy, theory of change or action plan into multi-year operational implementation down to activity level, within a single institutional system.

Demonstrated experience personally authoring and delivering advanced, competency-based training content for institutional audiences (teachers, management, technical staff) and private-sector actors.

Direct experience of OECD-DAC Gender Equality Policy Marker 2 and/or EU GAP III compliance, indicator design and donor reporting is strongly desirable.

Solid project-management experience embedded within an implementation team: operational planning, procurement, technical supervision of consultants, budget execution and monitoring of an activity package.

Experience providing technical direction to multidisciplinary teams of senior experts, and coordinating multi-stakeholder initiatives with government, private-sector, civil-society and academic partners.

Skills

Technical authorship. Ability to independently produce strategies, theories of change, action plans, guidance notes and training curricula of a standard suitable for donor and institutional validation.

Gender-transformative methodologies. Command of norm-change approaches, intersectionality, the Human Rights-Based Approach and Leave No One Behind, and their practical application to institutional transformation.

Understanding of TVET and agriculture sector challenges. Familiarity with labour market dynamics and skills development, especially for women and youth.

Disability inclusion, safeguarding and PSEA. GBV/SEAH mechanisms, Universal Design for Learning and accessibility standards.

Activity and budget management. Operational planning, procurement, consultant follow-up, gender-responsive budgeting and budget execution.

Communication, facilitation and advocacy. Ability to design and deliver technical presentations and facilitation before institutional partners, donors and private-sector audiences.

Initiative and autonomy. Capacity to identify needs, formulate approaches and produce deliverables without close supervision.

Digital literacy. Proficiency in standard office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Language proficiency. Excellent written and spoken command of English — the working language with the donor, RTB and partners — and of Kinyarwanda; French is an asset.

Any other provided details

Why Join Expertise France?

Contribute to a high-impact regional program shaping Africa's digital future.

Work alongside leading African and European institutions and experts.

Gain exposure to complex multi-country and multi-donor program management.

Develop your professional expertise within a recognized international organization.

Be part of a collaborative, multicultural, and inclusive working environment.

Purpose of the Position

The Communications Intern will support FAWE Rwanda’s communications activities aimed at enhancing organizational visibility, stakeholder engagement, and brand awareness. The intern will assist with content creation, digital communications, media engagement, event documentation, and advocacy initiatives while gaining practical experience in communication and development work.

Major Responsibilities

item.title: TVET Education Expert (H/F) job at Expertise France
item.description:
Expertise France is the French public agency for international technical cooperation. Present in over 100 countries, the agency engineers and implements capacity-building projects, mobilises technical expertise, and acts as project coordinator across four priority areas: democratic, economic and financial governance; stability in crisis and post-crisis contexts; climate change and sustainable urban development; and strengthening health systems, social protection and employment. About TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” is on of Expertise France projects that is being implemented in Rwanda. The “TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” project aims to contribute to the National Strategy for Transformation and Vision 2050 established by the Government of Rwanda to guide the socio-economic development of the country towards a prosperous and high-income economy by 2050. Representing 25% of GDP and 70% of Rwanda’s active population, agriculture is a key sector targeted in order to boost the country’s economy and create jobs. The development of agricultural skills is one of the priorities for the sector’s transformation, with the national objective of establishing TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture (CoE, also referred to as Centres of Vocational Excellence). These centres will help develop a new generation of qualified workforce, capable of stimulating sustainable agricultural development, contributing to food security, economic growth and improved livelihoods for rural communities in Rwanda.

The “TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” project is implemented by Expertise France to support the national agency Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) in the establishment of TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture. In line with national priorities, the project aims to increase the sustainability, climate resilience and inclusion of agricultural practices by strengthening the skills of women and youth in Rwanda.

The project is structured around two specific objectives:

Improve access of women and youth to quality skills and formal certification in agricultural practices.

Improve the effectiveness of mechanisms for integrating women and young people into the agricultural labour market, with an emphasis on sustainable agriculture.

In Rwanda, 77% of farmers are women, mainly in subsistence agriculture, vulnerable to climate change. The project is classified under the OECD-DAC Gender Equality Policy Marker 2: gender equality is a principal objective of the intervention, and the project implements transformative and sustainable actions for women, young girls and their communities.

The project is implemented over a period of five years, with a budget of +16 million euros financed by the EU and the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. It includes technical assistance at the national level in support of RTB, and two Technical Secondary Schools — Kisaro TSS (Rulindo District) and AEF Nyagahanga (Gatsibo District) — are also supported with technical assistance, infrastructure rehabilitation and procurement of agricultural equipment as they transform into Agricultural TVET Centres of Excellence. The project is implemented in collaboration with the beneficiary partner RTB, as well as with donors and project partners, such as LuxDev.

The project is led by the Project Manager, with direct support from the Deputy Project Manager, and the team consists of 4 Technical Experts, a MEAL Officer, and 2 Project Advisors based in targeted TVET schools. The team is supported by Expertise France’s Kigali-based Project Support Unit (PSU) for administration, finance, Human Resources and procurement, as well as Paris-based HQ.

The project has adopted and validated a Gender-Transformative and Socially Inclusive Framework Strategy (2024–2029), with an accompanying Training Architecture and a detailed, DAC-aligned Action Plan. The project is now entering its transition phase — running for a minimum of three years — during which this strategy moves from formulation to full institutional implementation across both Centres of Excellence. This phase places substantially higher technical and delivery demands on the position than the project’s start-up year.

Responsibilities or duties

1. To provide strategic and technical advice in TVET

Provide strategic and technical advice to the Project Manager and team on TVET programming.

Advise RTB and project partners on enhancing TVET curricula, pedagogy, and assessment methods to meet excellence standards in agriculture.

Assess the current state of agricultural TVET in Rwanda, identify gaps, and contribute to defining and implementing excellence standards.

Engage stakeholders in Rwanda’s TVET sector to ensure complementarity and synergies.

Support the development of employment and skills surveys, capturing evolving roles of women in agriculture and emphasising climate action strategies.

Lead the engagement with TVET institutions and facilitate linkages with agricultural market actors, in collaboration with the Agricultural Labour Market Expert.

Organise workshops and capacity-building sessions for partners and TVET trainers.

Contribute to defining the project’s digital and blended learning strategy for agricultural TVET, in support of trainers and adult learners.

2. To lead the project’s TVET activities

Support the Project Manager in the planning, budgeting, and alignment of TVET activities with project goals.

Coordinate the review and development of competency-based curricula and training materials for TVET in agriculture, animal health and food processing with the support of the project’s sector experts.

Coordinate curricula revisions with the project team to align with market needs and excellence standards, integrating climate-smart, gender-sensitive, and inclusive approaches.

Ensure that practice-based, hands-on learning is embedded throughout TVET delivery, including on-farm and workshop-based instruction, applied demonstrations and supervised field practice, so that trainees acquire employable agricultural competencies.

Lead the contracting and coordination of external experts, ensuring high-quality deliverables.

Contribute to procurement and administrative processes related to TVET activities (e.g., drafting terms of reference, evaluating technical proposals), in line with Expertise France’s internal procurement procedures and applicable donor rules.

Conduct training needs assessments for adult farmers and develop modular, mobile training programmes tailored to their constraints, especially for women.

Lead the digitalisation of training programmes and the deployment of digital and blended learning for students and adult learners (farmers and members of agricultural organisations), including the delivery of a trainer digital-skills gap assessment, a digital learning roadmap and a blended-learning scale-up plan.

Provide regular progress reports on TVET activities highlighting achievements, challenges, and recommendations.

Support the monitoring and evaluation efforts, to ensure the effectiveness of the project’s TVET activities.

3. To support targeted TVET schools’ transition to TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture

Assess and plan the technical, pedagogical, and infrastructure needs of the targeted TVET schools to achieve TVET Centre of Excellence in Agriculture status.

Support infrastructure feasibility assessments through TVET technical expertise.

Evaluate and address learning capacity gaps, including teacher training needs, learning materials, and training methods.

Offer capacity-building for management and pedagogical staff on new curricula, teaching methods (including digital for blended learning), and TVET CoE in Agriculture standards.

Develop governance models, accreditation frameworks, and assessment guidelines for TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture.

Support the schools in delivering revised curricula and teaching materials.

Contribute to developing trainers’ guides, Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) frameworks, and short courses for students and communities.

Facilitate learning exchanges among TVET schools.

Qualifications or requirements

Skills

Strong understanding of TVET systems, labor market dynamics, and skills development strategies, especially for women and youth.

Good understanding of the challenges in TVET and/or agriculture sectors, especially for women and youth.

Excellent communication and facilitation skills, with an excellent ability to translate technical concepts to a wide variety of audiences.

Strong interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.

Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.

Initiative-taking and sense of responsibility.

Proficiency in office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) and familiarity with digital learning platforms (LMS, e-learning tools).

Perfect command of English and Kinyarwanda; fluency in French is an asset.

Experience needed

A minimum of 10 years of professional experience in TVET systems and curricula development, particularly in agriculture, with a focus on competency-based education.

Solid project management experience, including planning, budgeting, monitoring, and evaluation of TVET or similar projects.

Experience in strategic advisory roles, providing technical support to stakeholders in TVET or related sectors.

Proven track record in capacity building and training delivery, including mentoring instructors and developing training materials.

Experience coordinating multi-stakeholder initiatives, including collaboration with government institutions, private sector actors, and academic institutions.

Knowledge of climate-smart and inclusive approaches in TVET programming, including gender-sensitive and digital transformation strategies.

Experience with digital and blended learning platforms and EdTech tools in TVET or education projects is an asset.

Any other provided details

The TVET Education Expert will be based within the project team in Kigali, under the direct supervision of the Project Manager. He/she will be responsible for the full implementation of a package of activities, and will provide TVET technical expertise to the project team, RTB and stakeholders, and contribute to the strategy, methodology and policy frameworks for TVET in agriculture, and any other pedagogical and technical processes that will enable the transition of TVET schools into TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture. The TVET Education Expert will work closely with the project team, partners and donors, for the successful implementation of the project.

item.title: Research Specialist job at Institute of Legal Practice and Development
item.company: Institute Of Legal Practice And Development
item.description:
Background information about the job or company (e.g., role context, company overview)

The Institute of Legal Practice and Development (ILPD) is seeking a Research Specialist to join their team. This role is crucial for supporting the Institute's research and consultancy assignments.

Responsibilities or duties

1. Design research methodologies and develop quantitative and qualitative data collection tools for research and consultancy assignments.

2. Coordinate the implementation of research projects, including planning, data collection, data management, quality assurance, and reporting.

3. Analyse qualitative and quantitative data using appropriate analytical techniques and software, and contribute to the interpretation of research findings.

4. Draft, review, and edit research reports, technical reports, policy briefs, and other research publications.

5. Participate in the preparation of research proposals, consultancy proposals, concept notes, and grant applications in response to identified opportunities.

6. Identify research and consultancy opportunities by monitoring public tenders, calls for proposals, and funding opportunities, and contribute to the preparation of competitive technical and financial proposals.

7. Organize and coordinate research activities, including stakeholder consultations, field missions, validation workshops, dissemination events, and other research-related engagements.

8. Maintain databases of research projects, consultancy assignments, research outputs, and institutional knowledge resources.

9. Support the monitoring, evaluation, and quality assurance of research and consultancy assignments to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and professional standards.

10. Assist in assessing institutional and stakeholder research needs and contribute to the development and periodic review of ILPD's research agenda.

11. Contribute to the dissemination and publication of research findings through reports, policy briefs, workshops, conferences, and other knowledge-sharing platforms.

12. Support the preparation of periodic reports on research and consultancy activities undertaken by the Directorate.

13. Coordinate the management of consultancy contracts between the Institute and its clients, ensuring compliance with contractual obligations and timely implementation of deliverables.

14. Perform any other research- and consultancy-related duties assigned by the supervisor or the Institute's Management.

Level: 3.II

Experience needed

Not specified.

Any other provided details (e.g., benefits, work environment, team info, or additional notes)

Exams to be conducted: Psychometric Test, Written, Oral.

item.description:
Background information about the job or company (e.g., role context, company overview)

This role is within the national public prosecution authority (NPPA) and focuses on providing assistance and protection to victims and witnesses.

Responsibilities or duties

The officer will be responsible for receiving and processing complaints from victims and witnesses, planning psychosocial support programs, assessing medical and psychological needs, assessing security risks, ensuring victims are not re-traumatized during testimony, providing material support to victims and witnesses, advocating for new legislation to improve witness protection, elaborating awareness strategies on witness rights, promoting the use of new information technologies for witness confidentiality, and performing any other assigned tasks.

Qualifications or requirements (e.g., education, skills)

Specific qualifications are not detailed in the provided text, but the role implies a need for strong interpersonal skills, empathy, and an understanding of legal and psychosocial support systems.

Experience needed

The position is under contract, Level 4.II, with one post available. Exams will include a Psychometric Test, Written exam, and Oral exam. The role reports to the Director of Victims & Witness Protection & Assistance.

item.title: Driver job at Rwanda Development Board
item.description:
Job responsibilities

Transport SPIU staff to destinations within Kigali and outside of Kigali as authorized.

Conduct daily inspections of assigned vehicles, maintain their cleanliness, and ensure that vehicles are in good and safe operating condition.

Promptly report any mechanical, technical, or physical damage to the immediate supervisor and facilitate appropriate action.

Report to duty on time and ensure compliance with all applicable road traffic laws and regulations.

Promote road safety and prevent road accidents by observing safe driving practices and promptly reporting any incidents or risks to the supervisor.

Required Education, Competencies & Skills

Have completed Secondary school (A2 Certificate)

Have a valid Driving license category B with at least 2 years of relevant experience working with Government Institutions or any recognized private or Charity organization accompanied by recommendations

Mechanical training Certificate is an added advantage

Some Computer Knowledge at least in Ms Word

Internal Auditor specialist will Administratively report to the SPIU Coordinator and technically to the Audit committee

He/she will be responsible:

  • He should identify the areas of the organization’s environment that pose the highest risk;
  • Any other assignment assigned by the management of SPIU.

  • Make sure of environmental management plans implementation for Project infrastructures;

item.title: Sector Strategic Planning Specialist job at Ministry of ICT and Innovation
item.description:
Background information about the job or company (e.g., role context, company overview)

The Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) is seeking a Sector Strategic Planning Specialist to contribute to the development and implementation of strategic plans within the sector. This role is crucial for ensuring effective planning, monitoring, and reporting of sector initiatives and budget execution.

Responsibilities or duties

The Sector Strategic Planning Specialist will be responsible for:

Participating in the preparation of various strategic plans of the sector.

Consolidating action plans from different units and institutions in the sector.

Supporting the implementation, monitoring, and update of sector strategic plans.

Preparing the sector strategic plan and budget in a timely manner and according to professional standards.

Developing tools for reporting and sharing them with different units and institutions in the sector.

Developing guidelines and procedures to report on the implementation and impact of budget execution and procurement plan in the sector.

Working with all Units, Programs, and institutions in the sector to ensure reporting deadlines prior to final submission are met and consolidating the sector’s quarterly and annually report.

Consolidating budget from different units and institutions in the sector and ensuring the linkage between the plans and the budgets.

Analyzing and consolidating the MTEFs from various units and institutions in the sector.

Liaising closely with the Finance Units of different institutions in the sector, for validation of financial reports.

Maintaining a list/database to track Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation and Reporting (PMER) capacities of all staff of different institutions in the sector.

Contributing to training on good PMER practices of all staff of different institutions in the sector.

Qualifications or requirements

Specific qualifications and experience are detailed in the full job posting.

Experience needed

Experience in strategic planning, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting is expected.

Any other provided details (e.g., benefits, work environment, team info, or additional notes)

This is a contract position. The role reports to the Future Planning Director General. Exams will be conducted, including a Psychometric Test, Written Test, and Oral Test.

item.title: Communications Officer at Rwanda Men's Resource Centre (RWAMREC)
item.description:
Rwanda Men’s Resource Centre (RWAMREC)

Legal status: Ministerial Order Nº 114/11 of 03/09/2008

P.O. Box 5768, Kigali, Rwanda

KG 11 Ave, YYUSSA PLAZA, Kimironko, 2nd Floor 

Tell-Cellular: +250788381183 | +250788315140

Email: [email protected]

Website: www.rwamrec.org

Terms of Reference: Communications Officer

22 June 2026

RWAMREC is Hiring a Communication Officer

ABOUT RWAMREC

The Rwanda Men’s Resource Centre (RWAMREC) is a non-governmental organization dedicated to transforming harmful masculinities and promoting gender equality in Rwanda and beyond. RWAMREC envisions a peaceful society where women and men share roles and responsibilities in raising families and governing society through equality, respect, and social justice.

RWAMREC’s mission is to promote gender equality by transforming masculinities and femininities through awareness creation, advocacy, capacity development, movement building, research, and service delivery. Through its programmes and partnerships, RWAMREC engages men and boys as allies for gender equality while supporting women’s rights, preventing gender-based violence, and promoting social justice.

POSITION OVERVIEW

RWAMREC seeks a dynamic, creative, and highly motivated Communication Officer to strengthen the organization’s visibility, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, knowledge management, and digital presence.

The Communication Officer will be responsible for developing and implementing communication strategies that effectively showcase RWAMREC’s programmes, campaigns, partnerships, research, advocacy initiatives, and organizational impact at national, regional, and international levels.

The incumbent will support the production of high-quality multimedia content, including written stories, photography, graphic design, videos, podcasts, social media content, reports, newsletters, and campaign materials. The Communication Officer will also contribute to knowledge management and organizational learning by ensuring that communication products, digital assets, and organizational information are properly documented, archived, analyzed, and disseminated.

The position requires a highly organized individual who is comfortable working with digital communication tools, social media management platforms, Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, analytics platforms, and knowledge management systems.

Expected start date: 1 August 2026.

REPORTING LINE

The Communication Officer will be a full-time staff member of RWAMREC and will report directly to the Communication Manager.

The incumbent will work closely with programme managers, project coordinators, monitoring and evaluation staff, administration and finance teams, consultants, partners, donors, media professionals, and other stakeholders to support the organization’s communication, visibility, advocacy, knowledge management, and digital engagement efforts.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Communication

Support the development and implementation of RWAMREC’s communication strategy and annual communication plans.

Ensure consistency of organizational branding, messaging, and visibility.

Support advocacy and campaign communication initiatives.

Contribute to stakeholder engagement and organizational positioning efforts.

Digital Communications and Social Media

Manage and regularly update RWAMREC’s social media platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X (Twitter), Threads, TikTok, YouTube, and emerging platforms.

Develop and implement content calendars.

Create, schedule, publish, and monitor engaging digital content.

Track social media performance and prepare periodic analytics reports.

Support audience engagement and community management across platforms.

Content Development

Produce and edit high-quality communication products, including:

Success stories, human-interest stories, blogs, press releases, news articles, newsletters, fact sheets, case studies, campaign materials, annual reports, and advocacy products.

Ensure all communication materials meet RWAMREC quality and branding standards.

Edit and proofread communication materials developed by programme teams.

Photography, Videography and Multimedia

Document programme activities through photography and videography.Produce and edit short videos, documentaries, interviews, reels, podcasts, and promotional content.

Develop multimedia products for digital campaigns and advocacy initiatives.

Maintain and organize RWAMREC’s multimedia archive.

Ensure informed consent is obtained, documented, and properly managed through standardized consent forms, and that all ethical communication standards are strictly respected when collecting stories, photos, and videos.

Media Relations and Visibility

Maintain relationships with journalists and media organizations.

Coordinate media coverage of organizational events and campaigns.

Draft press releases and media advisories.

Organize media engagements, interviews, and press conferences.

Monitor and document media coverage and visibility.

Website Management

Manage and regularly update the RWAMREC website.

Publish stories, blogs, news updates, reports, and communication products.

Monitor website performance and recommend improvements.

Support search engine optimization (SEO) and website visibility efforts.

Knowledge Management and Data Management

Support organizational knowledge management systems and processes.

Organize and maintain communication archives, media libraries, databases, and digital repositories.

Support documentation of lessons learned, best practices, and programme achievements.

Contribute to data organization, reporting, and dissemination of organizational knowledge products.

Event Communication and Campaigns

Support communication planning and visibility for events, conferences, trainings, webinars, and campaigns.

Coordinate event branding and promotional activities.

Develop event communication materials before, during, and after activities.

Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting

Track communication indicators and key performance metrics.

Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual communication reports.

Analyse social media, website, media coverage, and campaign performance data.

Provide recommendations to improve communication effectiveness.

Other Responsibilities

Support programme teams in meeting donor visibility requirements.

Represent RWAMREC in communication-related forums and networks when required.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

Qualification

A Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, or media studies.

A minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience in communications, journalism, digital storytelling, web design, or related fields.

Strong digital communication skills, with demonstrated experience in social media management, digital analytics, content development and creation, website management, and newsletter production.

Graphic design and multimedia skills, with proficiency in Canva or Adobe Creative Suite, are advantageous.

Fluency in Kinyarwanda and English is required; proficiency in French is an additional advantage.

Core Competencies

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Excellent interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills.

Strong organisational and project management abilities.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and work under tight deadlines.

High level of creativity, initiative, and attention to detail.

Commitment to gender equality, human rights, and social justice.

Respect for diversity, inclusion, and cultural sensitivity.

Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and collaborate with diverse teams and partners.

WHAT WE OFFER

RWAMREC is committed to providing a supportive, inclusive, and empowering work environment where staff can thrive both professionally and personally.

The successful candidate will benefit from:

A one-year renewable contract, subject to performance and funding availability, with a three (3) months probationary period.

Eighteen (18) days of annual leave per year, in addition to official public holidays.

A gender-transformative and values-driven work environment committed to gender equality, human rights, and social justice.

Opportunities for professional growth, mentorship, and continuous learning.

Exposure to national, regional, and international advocacy and development initiatives.

Opportunities to collaborate with leading organisations, networks, and practitioners working on engaging men and boys for gender equality, including actors within the MenEngage Alliance and other regional and global networks.

A dynamic, collaborative, and vibrant workplace that values innovation, creativity, teamwork, and diversity.

item.title: Oncology Research Manager at Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima (PIH)
item.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Job Title :
Oncology Research Manager
Department:
Oncology

Grade :
4B
Location:
Burera site

Reports to :
Director of Research and Training
Positions Reporting to:
Oncology coordinators, data collectors

1. Organizational Profile

Partners In Health (PIH) is a non-profit, global health organization that fights social injustice by bringing the benefits of modern medical science first and foremost to the most vulnerable communities around the world. PIH focuses on those who would not otherwise have access to quality health care. PIH partners with the world’s leading academic institutions to create rigorous evidence that shapes more sound and all-inclusive global health policies. PIH also supports local governments’ efforts to build capacity and strengthen national health systems. PIH runs programs in 11 countries (Haiti, Kazakhstan, Lesotho, Liberia, Malawi, Mexico, Navajo Nation, Peru, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and the United States of America), where it provides direct care to millions of patients, through public facilities and community engagement.

In Rwanda, PIH operates in three rural districts: Kayonza and Kirehe in the Eastern Province, and Burera in the Northern Province, where we support delivery of comprehensive integrated health care services which include cancer prevention, diagnosis and treatment.The Oncology Research Manager in this position will support all oncology research related projects that will be assigned to him/her.At PIH, we believe that who you are matters as much as what you know. As a humanitarian organization, we prioritize integrity, compassion, and a deep commitment to equity in healthcare. We are therefore looking for individuals who not only bring strong research expertise but also demonstrate outstanding character and alignment with our mission.

2

SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES:

Plan, coordinate and execute research projects within the oncology program.

Develop research protocols, study procedures and data collection tools together with the projects’ PIs and the PIH team.

Ensure that research milestones are attained as planned

Monitor and control expenses within allotted budget.

Ensure timely data collection and analysis

Supervise the oncology research coordinators and data collectors to ensure collection of high quality data

Collaborate with oncology clinicians and programmatic team to clarify unclear data

Respond to data quality control and data cleaning queries

Maintain data security per study protocols

Prepare and submit research progress or completion reports

Present findings to management and other dissemination platforms

Required Qualifications for the position

Advanced degree in Public health, nursing, medicine, global health statistics, or related field. PhD preferred

At least 5 years of full-time working experience in a related field, preferably with direct research involvement.

Proven skills in both quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, as well as mixed-methods studies.

Strong scientific writing and publication record. Applicants must submit a sample of scientific writing with their application, preferably a publication on which they were the first author.

Ability to lead a research project from conception to finish

Strong scientific writing and communication skills

Strong track record of team management.

Experience working with clinicians especially in cancer care and ability to learn basic information and terminology regarding cancer care

Strong organization, communication and writing skills

Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda

Skills in using data analysis software like STATA, MAXQDA or of any other qualitative and quantitative analysis software and using RedCap.

Experience in administering surveys and qualitative data collection methods

Experience collaborating in international organisations is a plus

Flexibility and willingness to travel to, live and work in rural areas.

Be a team player and have ability to work independently with a very minimal supervision.

Ability to live PIH/IMB values: Ubumuntu-Compassion, Ubupfura-Integrity, Ubwubahane-Mutual respect, Ubunyangamugayo-Honesty, Ubumwe-Togetherness, Agaciro- Dignity, Kugira ishyaka-Solidarity

Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Sexual Harassment:At Partners in Health, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work- including our patients, the families and community members – as well as our staff are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Partner in Health’s PSEAH policy. Partner in Health will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of this commitment, their readiness to follow it, and adhere to it.

How to apply:Please submit your CV, a letter of motivation (1 page maximum), and a work sample (e.g. a paper you were first author on, or a report you have written) that is pertinent to the topic.

item.title: Funding and Reporting Officer at Akagera Management Company
item.description:
Akagera Management Company 

P.O. Box 1448

Kigali

Rwanda

www.akagera.org 

AKAGERA NATIONAL PARK VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT 

Akagera Management Company Ltd was created through a partnership between African Parks and Rwanda Development Board (RDB) to manage Akagera National Park. We are seeking a dynamic and experienced candidate to fill the position of a Funding and Reporting Officer in Akagera National Park.

JOB TITTLE: FUNDING AND REPORTING OFFICER 

REPORTING TO: FUNDING AND REPORTING MANAGER 

SCOPE OF THE JOB:

The Funding and Reporting Officer supports the effective management of the Park’s grant portfolio by ensuring compliance with donor requirements and contributing to high-quality internal and external reporting. The role assists in identifying funding needs, coordinating grant-related activities, monitoring project progress, and documenting the Park’s ecological, social, and economic impact.

Serving as a key link between the park and the African Parks Network (APN) Headquarters teams including Fundraising, and the business intelligence unit the officer supports data collection, report writing, proposal development, budgeting, and monitoring and evaluation activities.

Working closely with the Funding and Reporting Manager, Park Manager, Finance Manager, and Heads of Department, the Officer helps ensure that project achievements, funding priorities, and conservation impacts are effectively communicated to donors, partners, and other stakeholders.

Duties and Key responsibilities

Support the effective and compliant implementation of the Park’s grant portfolio by monitoring project activities and donor requirements.

Assist in identifying, tracking, and documenting the Park’s funding needs and priorities.

Support the development, collection, and tracking of monitoring and evaluation data and performance indicators.

Coordinate the collection, compilation, and submission of internal and external reports in collaboration with relevant departments.

Contribute to the preparation and review of the Park’s 5-Year Business Plan and annual budgets.

Support in preparing daily, weekly, and monthly operational reports.

Coordinate and support donor and partner visits, including logistics, briefing materials, and follow-up actions.

Liaise with African Parks Network (APN) Headquarters teams to facilitate timely reporting, information sharing, and grant compliance.

Maintain accurate grant records, project documentation, and reporting databases.

Contribute to the development of funding proposals, donor updates, and impact stories that showcase the Park’s conservation and community achievements.

Additional Expectations: 

Ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.

Proactive and solution-oriented approach to challenges.

Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

Adaptable and flexible in responding to changing priorities and operational needs.

Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Willingness to travel within the park and attend meetings, workshops, and donor engagements as required.

Interest in conservation, biodiversity protection, and sustainable community development.

Commitment to the values and mission of African Parks Network.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Minimum Education and Qualification Required 

Minimum 3 years’ experience working in the region in donor relations, tourism or conservation at a high level.

Demonstrable experience handling data and storytelling.

Experience with donor grant management, proposals and reporting.

Excellent organizational, analytical, oral and written communications skills in English.

Ability to work in remote/isolated area.

Experience in donor relations.

Good computing skills, particularly Word, Excel, Power Point & Outlook.

Strong project management and evidence of working collaboratively with teams.

Strong leadership skills, with demonstrable ability to keep teams organized and focused on the key priorities within a multitude of projects with deadlines, taking strong ownership of safeguarding and improving quality standards.

Strong understanding of finance and accounting principles, including budgeting, financial reporting, expenditure tracking, and basic financial analysis.

Ability to work closely with finance teams to support grant budgeting, budget variance monitoring, financial documentation, and donor financial reporting.

Note

Applications that are not meeting the above criteria will not be considered.

AKAGERA NATIONAL PARK VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT 

Akagera Management Company Ltd was created through a partnership between African Parks and Rwanda Development Board (RDB) to manage Akagera National Park. We are seeking a dynamic and experienced candidate to fill the position of a Funding and Reporting Officer in Akagera National Park.

JOB TITTLE: FUNDING AND REPORTING OFFICER 

REPORTING TO: FUNDING AND REPORTING MANAGER 

SCOPE OF THE JOB:

The Funding and Reporting Officer supports the effective management of the Park’s grant portfolio by ensuring compliance with donor requirements and contributing to high-quality internal and external reporting. The role assists in identifying funding needs, coordinating grant-related activities, monitoring project progress, and documenting the Park’s ecological, social, and economic impact.

Serving as a key link between the park and the African Parks Network (APN) Headquarters teams including Fundraising, and the business intelligence unit the officer supports data collection, report writing, proposal development, budgeting, and monitoring and evaluation activities.

Working closely with the Funding and Reporting Manager, Park Manager, Finance Manager, and Heads of Department, the Officer helps ensure that project achievements, funding priorities, and conservation impacts are effectively communicated to donors, partners, and other stakeholders.

Duties and Key responsibilities

  • Support the effective and compliant implementation of the Park’s grant portfolio by monitoring project activities and donor requirements.
  • Assist in identifying, tracking, and documenting the Park’s funding needs and priorities.
  • Support the development, collection, and tracking of monitoring and evaluation data and performance indicators.
  • Coordinate the collection, compilation, and submission of internal and external reports in collaboration with relevant departments.
  • Contribute to the preparation and review of the Park’s 5-Year Business Plan and annual budgets.
  • Support in preparing daily, weekly, and monthly operational reports.
  • Coordinate and support donor and partner visits, including logistics, briefing materials, and follow-up actions.
  • Liaise with African Parks Network (APN) Headquarters teams to facilitate timely reporting, information sharing, and grant compliance.
  • Maintain accurate grant records, project documentation, and reporting databases.
  • Contribute to the development of funding proposals, donor updates, and impact stories that showcase the Park’s conservation and community achievements.

Additional Expectations: 

  • Ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Proactive and solution-oriented approach to challenges.

item.description:
JOB OPPORTUNITY

WASH ENGINEER- SHORT-TERM CONTRACT

World Vision is a child-focused Christian humanitarian organization implementing development programmes in 30 Districts of Rwanda. Our interventions in the strategic period of 2026-2030 seek to reach 2.5 million of the most vulnerable children. This is done through programming in Child Protection, and Education, Nutrition and WASH, and Poverty Alleviation (Resilience and Livelihoods).

World Vision Rwanda seeks to hire a highly qualified, dedicated and experienced Rwandan national for the role of WASH Engineer, joining an established and experienced team. This position incorporates a range of skills and development in multiple areas, allowing for an exciting opportunity for career growth in a dynamic, global organization. It will be based in Kigali, Rwanda and reports to the WASH Technical Design Manager.

Purpose of the position:

The WASH Engineer will be responsible for the day-to-day supervision, quality assurance, and progress tracking of construction activities undertaken by contracted firms at 18 selected HCFs and 7 School located in three districts namely Rutsiro, Rusizi and Nyamasheke. The role ensures that the contractors deliver high-quality WASH infrastructure in full compliance with approved technical designs, BOQs, national standards, World Vision Infrastructure Quality Assurance and Quality Control Plan and donor requirements. The position holder will be stationed in Nyungwe cluster’s office, Nyamasheke district and will frequently be traveling to the above-mentioned districts

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITES

% of time

Activity

End Results

40

Perform water resources development studies and conduct design review as required;

Review and conduct detail investigation on water resource development project sites

Ensure continuous services of the WASH & Health infrastructures and services

Prepare/Review technical terms of reference (TOR), Technical drawings, Designs of water and civil infrastructure facilities, through different stages like Feasibility, preliminary/semi detailed and detailed engineering designs, bill of quantities (BoQs)/ cost estimate, technical specifications and tender documents for water supply systems, sanitation and hygiene facilities.

Filing all documents related to WASH infrastructures

Supervise contractors during the construction and installation of WASH facilities (e.g., water supply systems, sanitation blocks, waste management systems, incinerators, handwashing stations, etc.).

Verify adherence to technical drawings, BOQs, national building codes, MoH WASH in HCF standards, and WVR quality benchmarks.

Conduct regular site inspections and produce technical site visit reports. Flag and document any design deviations or contractor noncompliance.

Develop and maintain a site supervision schedule for the ongoing constructions projects.

Track construction progress against the implementation plan and submit weekly and monthly progress reports to WVR.

Recommend corrective actions where construction timelines or quality standards are at risk.

Facilitate and document site meetings and joint inspections with district officials, health facility management, and partners.

Timely map completed WASH infrastructures in mWater

Water resources development studies and designs meet the required standards.

Water resource investigation reports are well prepared and of high quality.

WASH and health infrastructure services are properly maintained.

Bills of Quantities (BoQs), cost estimates, technical specifications, tender documents, and Terms of Reference (ToR) are prepared in a timely manner and to a high standard.

Proper documentation of WASH infrastructure project implementation is ensured.

Projects are completed on time, and infrastructure quality is maintained.

Completed WASH infrastructures are mapped and reported in the mWater Output Monitoring Survey (OMS).

40

Keep abreast of WASH sector developments in Rwanda, especially those that may affect on-going program activities

Ensure that construction projects are meeting their administrative, quality, programmatic goals, outcomes, and outputs on time and on budget, towards the realization of WVR projects and universal coverage goals; Sustainable development goals; and Rwanda’s Government commitment to achieve universal access to basic water and sanitation coverage

Advise on the development and maintenance of the water, sanitation and hygiene infrastructures;

Prepare weekly, monthly, quarterly, biannual and annual progress reports of WASH status in the Project and in accordance with donor and WV Rwanda requirements.

Supervise contractors/suppliers during implementation to ensure quality workmanship, safety and value for money is achieved within scheduled times.

Take lead in dispossessing, handing over and commissioning of WASH projects.

Serve as a field liaison between WVR, district engineers, and health care facility and Schools staff on all technical matters.

Support the organization of technical acceptance processes and final handovers.

Assist in preparing site completion certificates and compiling as-built documentation.

Provide updates regarding WASH and Health infrastructures that may affect program activities is continuously provided.

Timely monitoring of WASH, health and development projects to ensure they meet intended goals and strict adherence to the Rwanda government regulations WHO and the SPHERE standards.

Clear plan for the development and maintenance of WASH infrastructures within the project is available and regularly updated.

High quality and timely report is produced.

Report on the progress of the project on regular basis as required by the reporting schedule i.e. weekly, monthly, semi-annually and donor reports.

All completed WASH and health infrastructures are timely branded and handed over to the district or institutions for post management,

20

Review tender documents both for design and construction of water resource projects; ensure that all PRs related to WASH infrastructures are raised and resources assigned to them are well utilized.

Review and verify construction estimations and actual costs for WASH projects in the program.

Ensure that resources assigned are properly and efficiently utilized.

Provide support to SC/HO in BoQs and tender document preparation.

Ensure that all WASH infrastructures hard and soft copy related documents are well kept

Ensure that contractors observe safety and environmental protection protocols throughout the construction phase.

Monitor inclusion of gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive features in WASH infrastructure (e.g., hygiene-friendly toilets).

Support the final commissioning, testing, and handing over of the completed infrastructures.

Verify the accuracy and completeness of as-built drawings and maintenance manuals.

Contribute to lessons learned and project closure reports.

All tender documents meet the desired technical and financial specifications.

Construction costs are verified to make sure that they are realistic.

Maintain WASH resources efficiency within the project budget.

Bid evaluation are timely done as per SC requirements

All WASH infrastructures documents are filled in a proper manner.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

Experience in reviewing and conducting detailed investigations on water resource development projects in the area.

Prepare bill of quantities, specification and cost estimate for water resources, sanitation and hygiene facilities and perform site meetings and elaboration of construction site visit reports

Prepare hydraulic calculations and technical designs.

Data collection and its analysis and technical study preparation and report presentation

Coordinate site yard works

Verification of attachments and invoices submitted by the contractors/suppliers.

Monitor, supervise and evaluate project progress on a monthly basis.

Approve the executed works according to the drawings and standards

Required Education, training, license,

registration, and

certification

Bachelor of Science in civil engineering, Water engineering, sanitary engineering or related fields

At least 5 years’ experience in the design and construction of WASH infrastructure projects. Please highlight the projects you have worked on in your CV.

Experience in using MS Officer, Excel, PPT, and other computer skills

Experience in using engineering software’s: AUTOCAD civil 3D, ARCHICAD, ArcGIS (Arc view, Arc map), and EPANET etc…

Experience in project design, proposal writing, needs assessments, surveys, and information management.

Knowledge of national WASH in HCFs standards s and construction contract management.

Strong experience in supervising contractors, preparing technical reports, and ensuring compliance with specifications.

Must be a committed Christian, able to stand above denominational diversities.

Preferred Knowledge

and Qualifications

Water resources/ hydraulic engineering technical training

Having experience in working with NGO or other institutions recognized for WASH expertise is an added advantage.

A team player, capable of building staff and community capacity in Water, Sanitation and hygiene projects through training.

Ability to take initiative, a team leader able to work with minimum supervision

Travel and/or

Work Environment

Requirement

The position requires the ability and willingness to travel domestically up to 70% of the time.

Physical

Requirements

The ability to work and respond to any given task.

Language

Requirements

Effective in written and verbal communication in English and Kinyarwanda

KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

Contact (within WV or outside WV)

Reason for contact

Frequency of contact

WASH Technical Design Manager

Reporting and supervision

Daily

Health and Hygiene Coordinators

Supervisory and Functional support

Daily

Program Managers at the cluster level

Reporting and supervisor Functional

Daily

Nutrition & WASH Programme Development and Quality Manager

Involved in the performance contracts and appraisal

Monthly

Cluster WASH Engineers

Collaboration and functional support

Need basis
